category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary drug used in the long-term treatment of leprosy that acts by inhibiting folate synthesis as a structural analog of PABA is [___].
back:
• Dapsone (diaminodiphenylsulfone)
• Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Key component of all leprosy regimens

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 28-year-old male with leprosy develops sudden onset fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine after starting Dapsone. Laboratory tests reveal Heinz bodies. What is the underlying cause?
back:
• Drug-induced oxidative stress/hemolysis
• Occurs in patients with G6PD deficiency
• Dapsone is a known oxidative trigger

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: How does the pharmacological storage of Clofazimine contribute to its long half-life and specific side effects?
back:
• Stored widely in skin and reticuloendothelial tissues
• Forms visible crystals inside phagocytic cells
• Half-life is approximately 2 months

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended drug regimens for Paucibacillary versus Multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin
• Multibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin + Clofazimine
• Triple therapy prevents emergence of resistance

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the drug used specifically to suppress Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) reactions occurring during leprosy therapy.
back:
• Thalidomide
• Used when reactions to dying bacilli occur
• Counteracts Dapsone-related ENL symptoms

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The phenazine dye used in multibacillary leprosy that causes a characteristic reddish-brown discoloration of the skin is [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• Also discolors conjunctivae
• Used specifically in multibacillary cases

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient on leprosy treatment presents with cyanosis and symptoms of hypoxia, but his PaO2 is normal. Lab findings confirm methemoglobinemia. Which drug is responsible?
back:
• Dapsone
• Common but usually not clinically significant
• Results from drug-induced oxidation of hemoglobin

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the mechanism of Rifampin in the context of leprosy treatment.
back:
• Binds to the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Inhibits bacterial RNA synthesis
• Highly effective bactericidal agent

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the use of Clarithromycin versus standard therapy in leprosy management.
back:
• Clarithromycin: Semisynthetic macrolide with M. leprae activity
• Standard: Tri-drug regimen (Dapsone, Rifampin, Clofazimine)
• Clarithromycin is an alternative, not first-line

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: What is the standard adult daily dosage of Rifampin used in the treatment of leprosy?
back:
• 600 mg daily
• Must be given with at least one other drug
• Prevents emergence of drug resistance

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: For the treatment of paucibacillary leprosy, the World Health Organization recommends a two-drug regimen consisting of Dapsone and [___].
back:
• Rifampicin (Rifampin)
• This combination is used to prevent the emergence of drug resistance
• Treatment duration is typically 6 months

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient undergoing treatment for lepromatous leprosy presents with painful erythematous skin nodules and fever. This type 2 reaction, known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum, is typically managed by adding [___].
back:
• Thalidomide
• Alternatively, corticosteroids are used
• It occurs due to the deposition of immune complexes during therapy

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the primary mechanism of action by which Dapsone exerts its anti-leprotic effects.
back:
• Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Competitively antagonizes p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Blocks the synthesis of folic acid essential for bacterial growth

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient with more than five skin lesions and a positive smear for acid-fast bacilli requires a triple-drug regimen. Contrast this Multibacillary (MB) regimen with the Paucibacillary (PB) protocol regarding drug composition.
back:
• MB Regimen: Rifampicin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine
• PB Regimen: Rifampicin and Dapsone only
• MB treatment duration is usually 12 months compared to 6 months for PB

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Enumerate the three primary drugs used in the standard multidrug therapy (MDT) for leprosy.
back:
• Rifampicin
• Dapsone
• Clofazimine
• These drugs are used in combination to prevent Mycobacterium leprae resistance

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A common side effect of [___] therapy in leprosy patients is a harmless orange-red discoloration of urine, sweat, and tears.
back:
• Rifampicin (Rifampin)
• Occurs due to the drug's inherent pigment
• Patients must be counseled to avoid unnecessary alarm

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 30-year-old leprosy patient develops dark urine and pallor after starting Dapsone. Which underlying enzyme deficiency should be suspected as the cause of this hemolysis?
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
• Dapsone causes oxidative stress leading to RBC destruction
• Methemoglobinemia is another common hematologic complication

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe the unique pharmacokinetic profile of Clofazimine that results in its characteristic skin discoloration.
back:
• Highly lipophilic phenazine dye
• Stored in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin
• Very long half-life (approx. 2 months), leading to brownish-black skin pigmentation

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the bactericidal activity and cellular targets of Rifampicin versus Dapsone in Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Rifampicin: Bactericidal; inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Dapsone: Bacteriostatic; inhibits dihydropteroate synthase (folate pathway)
• Rifampicin is the most potent component of MDT

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: To which specific chemical class of drugs does Dapsone belong?
back:
• Sulfones
• It is structurally related to sulfonamides
• Retained in skin, muscle, liver, and kidneys

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary mechanism of action for the sulfone drug dapsone involves the competitive inhibition of [___] synthesis in Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Folate synthesis
• Structurally acts as a PABA analog
• Inhibits the enzyme dihydropteroate synthase

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 30-year-old male with lepromatous leprosy starts MDT and develops sudden pallor, jaundice, and dark urine. Labs show bite cells and Heinz bodies. What is the most likely cause?
back:
• Dapsone-induced hemolytic anemia
• Underlying G6PD deficiency
• Oxidative stress leads to RBC destruction

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the specific role of Rifampin within the multidrug therapy (MDT) for leprosy.
back:
• Highly bactericidal against M. leprae
• Blocks viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Prevents selection of dapsone-resistant mutants

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-standard drug regimens for Multibacillary versus Paucibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone
• Treatment duration is significantly longer for multibacillary disease

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe the unique tissue distribution and characteristic dermatological side effect of Clofazimine.
back:
• Phenazine dye stored in reticuloendothelial tissues
• Half-life of approximately 2 months
• Causes pink to brownish-black skin/conjunctiva discoloration

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) is a common reaction during dapsone therapy that is typically managed using the drug [___].
back:
• Thalidomide
• Acts by suppressing the immune/inflammatory reaction
• Often used when corticosteroids are insufficient

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient on leprosy treatment presents with a cyanotic appearance but normal oxygen tension on blood gas. This functional anemia is caused by [___].
back:
• Methemoglobinemia
• Side effect of Dapsone therapy
• Involves oxidation of hemoglobin iron to ferric state

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: How does Clofazimine contribute to the management of lepromatous leprosy beyond its bactericidal effects?
back:
• Possesses intrinsic anti-inflammatory properties
• Helps prevent or suppress Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)
• Reduces the need for systemic steroids

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the handling of Rifampin versus Dapsone regarding the risk of resistance.
back:
• Rifampin: Rapid resistance if used as monotherapy
• Dapsone: Slow resistance development
• Both must be used in combination to ensure efficacy

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Enumerate the three primary drugs that constitute the first-line multidrug therapy for Leprosy.
back:
• Dapsone (a sulfone)
• Rifampin (a rifamycin)
• Clofazimine (a phenazine dye)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: In the treatment of multibacillary leprosy, the three-drug combination recommended by the WHO includes dapsone, rifampin, and [___].
back:
• Clofazimine.
• Used specifically for multibacillary cases (positive smears).
• Added to the regimen to prevent the development of drug resistance.
• Typically administered for a duration of 12 months.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient undergoing therapy for leprosy presents with reddish-brown skin pigmentation and darkening of the conjunctivae. This side effect is most likely caused by [___].
back:
• Clofazimine.
• A phenazine dye that accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues.
• Causes dose-related skin and conjunctival discoloration.
• Pigmentation usually resolves slowly after drug discontinuation.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role of Dapsone in inhibiting the growth of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Blocks the synthesis of folate, which is essential for bacterial nucleic acids.
• Mechanism is structurally and functionally similar to sulfonamides.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO recommended treatment durations and drug requirements for Paucibacillary versus Multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin and Dapsone for 6 months.
• Multibacillary: Rifampin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine for 12 months.
• Classification is based on the organism burden in skin smears.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the mandatory screening test required before initiating Dapsone to prevent drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) assay.
• Dapsone causes oxidative stress in erythrocytes.
• Deficiency leads to acute hemolysis and potentially severe methemoglobinemia.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The painful inflammatory condition involving skin nodules that occurs during dapsone treatment of lepromatous leprosy is called [___].
back:
• Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL).
• A Type II lepra reaction caused by immune complex deposition.
• Often managed with corticosteroids or thalidomide.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient develops cyanosis and 'chocolate-colored' blood while on triple-drug therapy. Name the causative drug and the underlying biochemical abnormality.
back:
• Drug: Dapsone.
• Abnormality: Methemoglobinemia.
• Occurs due to oxidation of hemoglobin iron to the ferric state.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe how Rifampin functions as the most potent component of leprosy multi-drug therapy (MDT).
back:
• Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase in the bacillus.
• Exerts highly effective bactericidal action against M. leprae.
• Rapidly reduces the bacterial load to prevent transmission and resistance.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the clinical indications for using Minocycline or Clarithromycin in leprosy management.
back:
• Used as second-line alternative agents.
• Indicated when primary drugs like rifampin or dapsone are not tolerated.
• Often used in salvage therapy for resistant strains.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Name the primary drug used to suppress the Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) reaction during leprosy treatment.
back:
• Thalidomide.
• Provides symptomatic relief from inflammatory skin lesions.
• Used with strict contraceptive precautions due to teratogenicity.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The standard WHO triple-drug regimen recommended for the treatment of multibacillary leprosy consists of Rifampin, Dapsone, and [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• It is a phenazine dye
• Used to prevent resistance development

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 40-year-old patient being treated for lepromatous leprosy presents with a new brownish-black discoloration of the skin and conjunctivae. This is a characteristic side effect of [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• Slowly released from reticuloendothelial deposits
• Half-life can be up to 2 months

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Dapsone inhibits the growth of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Inhibits folate synthesis
• Competitive antagonist of p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Targets the enzyme dihydropteroate synthase

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO treatment regimens for paucibacillary leprosy versus multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin
• Multibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin + Clofazimine
• Multibacillary involves higher bacterial loads (positive smears)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: List the major hematologic adverse effects associated with Dapsone therapy.
back:
• Hemolysis (especially in G6PD deficiency)
• Methemoglobinemia
• Agranulocytosis (rare)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: During the treatment of lepromatous leprosy, the reaction known as [___] often develops and may be suppressed by thalidomide.
back:
• Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)
• Characterized by painful skin nodules
• Occurs as a reaction to dapsone therapy

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient with leprosy presents with sudden onset fever and painful subcutaneous nodules. Which immunomodulatory drug is indicated specifically for this complication?
back:
• Thalidomide
• Used to treat Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)
• Dapsone may be continued alongside it

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: How does Rifampin exert its bactericidal effect against leprosy bacilli?
back:
• Binds to the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Inhibits bacterial RNA synthesis
• Highly effective; even monthly doses are beneficial

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the tissue storage properties of Clofazimine and Rifampin.
back:
• Clofazimine: Stored widely in reticuloendothelial tissues; extremely long half-life (2 months)
• Rifampin: Excreted through liver/bile; undergoes enterohepatic recirculation; shorter half-life

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the primary therapeutic role of Iodoquinol and Paromomycin in the context of leprosy.
back:
• No role in leprosy
• These are luminal amebicides used for Entamoeba histolytica
• Leprosy requires Dapsone/Rifampin/Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary sulfone drug utilized in leprosy treatment that acts by inhibiting folate synthesis is [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• Competitive inhibitor of dihydropteroate synthase
• Structurally related to sulfonamides
• Bacteriostatic against M. leprae

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient develops a reddish-brown skin discoloration and conjunctival pigmentation while on multidrug therapy. Identify the causative agent.
back:
• Clofazimine
• A phenazine dye
• Accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues
• May take months to resolve after discontinuation

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Rifampin exerts its bactericidal effect on Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Binds to the β subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Blocks RNA synthesis
• Highly effective as a single monthly dose in some regimens

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended drug regimens for paucibacillary leprosy versus multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin and Dapsone
• Multibacillary: Rifampin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine
• Multibacillary requires triple therapy due to higher organism burden

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Enumerate the metabolic pathway inhibited by Dapsone in the treatment of leprosy.
back:
• Folate synthesis pathway
• Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Prevents synthesis of dihydrofolic acid from PABA

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL), an inflammatory complication of lepromatous leprosy treatment, is specifically suppressed by [___].
back:
• Thalidomide
• Acts as an immunomodulator
• Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenicity

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 30-year-old male with leprosy and G6PD deficiency develops dark urine and sudden pallor after starting therapy. Which drug is the likely trigger?
back:
• Dapsone
• Causes oxidative stress leading to hemolysis
• Methemoglobinemia is a common but often asymptomatic side effect

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe the unique tissue distribution and storage characteristics of Clofazimine.
back:
• High lipophilicity results in wide storage in RE tissues
• Crystals can be seen within phagocytic cells
• Extremely long half-life (~2 months)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Distinguish the clinical use of Minocycline or Clarithromycin in the context of leprosy management.
back:
• Used as second-line or alternative agents
• Effective against M. leprae in patients resistant to first-line MDT
• Often used in specialized research or salvage protocols

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the primary reason why multiple drugs are administered simultaneously for the treatment of leprosy.
back:
• Prevents emergence of drug-resistant strains
• Dapsone resistance is common if used as monotherapy
• Ensures eradication of both intracellular and extracellular bacilli

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary oral antihelminthic drug used in the treatment of leprosy that acts by inhibiting folate synthesis is [___].
back:
• Dapsone (diaminodiphenylsulfone)
• Mechanism: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Structurally related to sulfonamides

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient being treated for multibacillary leprosy presents with a reddish-brown pigmentation of the skin and conjunctivae. Identify the drug responsible for this side effect.
back:
• Clofazimine
• A phenazine dye
• Accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role of Rifampin in the treatment of leprosy according to its biological function.
back:
• Potent bactericidal agent
• Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Prevents emergence of dapsone resistance when used in combination

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended multidrug therapy (MDT) regimens for paucibacillary versus multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine
• Multibacillary definition: Positive smear from any site

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Name the immunomodulatory agent used specifically to suppress Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) reactions during leprosy treatment.
back:
• Thalidomide
• Used when ENL is not distinguished from dapsone reactions
• Contraindicated in pregnancy

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Before prescribing dapsone for leprosy, patients must be screened for [___] deficiency to avoid drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
• Dapsone is a potent oxidizing agent
• Hemolysis is the most common dapsone side effect

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient on triple therapy develops tender skin nodules, fever, and joint pain shortly after starting treatment. Identify the clinical reaction and the likely trigger.
back:
• Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)
• Triggered by antigens released from dying M. leprae bacilli
• Common in lepromatous leprosy

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe how the pharmacokinetic properties of Dapsone contribute to its efficacy in treating skin-involved leprosy.
back:
• Highly lipophilic
• Concentrates and is retained in the skin, muscle, liver, and kidneys
• Long half-life (1–2 days) allows for daily dosing

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the bactericidal versus bacteriostatic roles of the three main drugs used in multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Rifampin: Highly bactericidal
• Dapsone: Primarily bacteriostatic
• Clofazimine: Slowly bactericidal/bacteriostatic

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: List the three drugs that constitute the standard WHO triple therapy for multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Rifampin
• Dapsone
• Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary oral anti-folate drug that serves as the backbone of leprosy treatment by inhibiting dihydropteroate synthase is [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• Acts by inhibiting folate synthesis (PABA antagonist)
• Used in both paucibacillary and multibacillary regimens

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient with leprosy begins multidrug therapy and shortly after develops dark urine, jaundice, and a significant drop in hemoglobin. This drug-induced hemolysis most likely implicates [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• Occurs predominantly in patients with G6PD deficiency
• Requires screening for the enzyme defect before initiation

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role of Rifampin within a multidrug therapy (MDT) regimen for leprosy.
back:
• Highly bactericidal against Mycobacterium leprae
• Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Rapidly renders the patient non-infectious

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended drug components for the treatment of paucibacillary leprosy versus multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine
• Addition of Clofazimine provides extra anti-inflammatory and bactericidal activity

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the phenazine dye used in leprosy that frequently results in pink to brownish-black skin discoloration.
back:
• Clofazimine
• Stored widely in reticuloendothelial tissues
• May also cause gastrointestinal distress and conjunctival staining

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The reaction known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) occurring during the treatment of lepromatous leprosy is often managed with the adjunctive agent [___].
back:
• Thalidomide
• Alternative: Corticosteroids
• Used to suppress the inflammatory response to dying bacilli

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient on triple-drug therapy presents with intense pruritus and skin pigmentation changes. Biopsy reveals drug crystals inside phagocytic reticuloendothelial cells. The responsible drug is [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• Crystals accumulate in the skin and gut
• Very long half-life (approx. 2 months)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: How does Dapsone therapy potentially trigger the development of Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)?
back:
• Rapid killing of large numbers of bacilli
• Release of mycobacterial antigens
• Formation of immune complexes (Type III hypersensitivity)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Distinguish between the primary toxicities of Dapsone and Clofazimine.
back:
• Dapsone: Hemolysis (G6PD), methemoglobinemia, and peripheral neuropathy
• Clofazimine: Skin discoloration (ichthyosis) and gastrointestinal intolerance

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Name the three standard drugs included in the WHO 'Blister Pack' for the treatment of multibacillary leprosy.
back:
1. Rifampin
2. Dapsone
3. Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary drug used in the long-term treatment of leprosy that acts as a structural analog of p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) is [___].
back: * Dapsone

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 30-year-old male on multidrug therapy for multibacillary leprosy presents with brownish-black skin discoloration and conjunctival pigmentation. Identify the most likely drug responsible.
back:
* Clofazimine
* Phenazine dye causing accumulation in reticuloendothelial tissues.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the mechanism by which Dapsone inhibits the replication of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
* Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
* Blocks the synthesis of folate from PABA.
* Bacteriostatic action against leprosy bacilli.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the World Health Organization (WHO) drug regimens used to treat paucibacillary versus multibacillary leprosy.
back:
* Paucibacillary: Dapsone and Rifampin.
* Multibacillary: Dapsone, Rifampin, and Clofazimine.
* Multibacillary therapy typically lasts 12 months.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Name the bactericidal rifamycin derivative that must always be given in combination with other drugs to prevent the selection of resistant Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
* Rifampin
* Potent inducer of cytochrome P450 enzymes.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: For patients requiring the standard WHO combination for paucibacillary leprosy, the two essential components are dapsone and [___].
back: * Rifampin

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient with known glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency is prescribed dapsone. Specify the hematologic complication for which this patient is at maximum risk.
back:
* Hemolytic anemia (hemolysis)
* Methemoglobinemia is also common but usually less severe.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe how the phenazine dye Clofazimine acts against mycobacteria and its significant pharmacokinetic storage property.
back:
* Binds to mycobacterial DNA to inhibit template function.
* Stored widely in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin.
* Extremely long half-life (approximately 2 months).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the clinical roles of Thalidomide and Clofazimine in managing leprosy-associated reactions.
back:
* Thalidomide: Used to suppress Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL).
* Clofazimine: Standard drug in MDT that also aids in suppressing ENL.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Enumerate the three core drugs included in the standard WHO Multidrug Therapy (MDT) for lepromatous (multibacillary) leprosy.
back:
* Dapsone
* Rifampin
* Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: In the long-term treatment of leprosy, the drug [___] is the most widely used sulfone and acts as a folate synthesis antagonist.
back:
* Dapsone (diaminodiphenylsulfone)
* Bacteriostatic against M. leprae
* Competitive inhibitor of dihydropteroate synthase

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient from an endemic region presents with symmetric anesthetic skin lesions and positive acid-fast bacilli on skin smears. Identify the standard WHO-recommended triple-drug regimen.
back:
* Rifampin (600 mg monthly)
* Dapsone (100 mg daily)
* Clofazimine (50 mg daily + 300 mg monthly)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role and mechanism of Clofazimine in the treatment of leprosy.
back:
* Phenazine dye with bactericidal activity against M. leprae
* Mechanism: Binds to DNA or disrupts membrane function
* Exerts anti-inflammatory effects to suppress Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended multidrug therapy (MDT) for Paucibacillary leprosy versus Multibacillary leprosy.
back:
* Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone (6 months)
* Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine (12 months)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the primary mechanism by which Rifampin exerts its bactericidal effect on Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
* Inhibition of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
* Binds to the beta subunit to block RNA synthesis
* Highly effective against M. leprae

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A major adverse effect of the leprosy drug [___] is the development of dose-related hemolysis, particularly in patients with G6PD deficiency.
back:
* Dapsone
* Also causes methemoglobinemia
* May provoke Erythema Nodosum Leprosum

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient with lepromatous leprosy develops painful skin nodules, fever, and lymphadenopathy during treatment. Name this reaction and the drug used to specifically suppress it.
back:
* Reaction: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (Type 2 Lepra Reaction)
* Treatment: Thalidomide (Clofazimine is an alternative)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: How does the pharmacokinetic profile of Clofazimine affect its dosing and storage in the body?
back:
* Highly lipophilic; stored in reticuloendothelial tissues
* Very long half-life (approx. 2 months)
* Excreted primarily in feces

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the clinical presentation and management of the two primary types of lepra reactions.
back:
* Type 1 (Reversal): Delayed hypersensitivity; treated with Corticosteroids
* Type 2 (ENL): Immune complex deposition; treated with Thalidomide or Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: What is the most characteristic cosmetic side effect of Clofazimine that patients must be counseled about?
back:
* Reddish-brown to black discoloration of the skin
* Discoloration of conjunctivae and body fluids

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: In the treatment of leprosy, the drug dapsone acts as a structural analog of PABA to competitively inhibit the enzyme [___].
back:
• Dihydropteroate synthase
• Blocks the synthesis of folic acid
• Bacteriostatic against Mycobacterium leprae

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient being treated for lepromatous leprosy develops sudden fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine. Labs show Heinz bodies and methemoglobinemia. Identify the most likely causative drug.
back:
• Dapsone
• Triggers oxidative stress
• Causes hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role of Rifampin in the World Health Organization (WHO) recommended multidrug therapy for leprosy.
back:
• Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Highly bactericidal against M. leprae
• Prevents emergence of dapsone-resistant mutants

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the drug regimens recommended for paucibacillary leprosy versus multibacillary leprosy according to WHO guidelines.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone (6 months)
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine (12 months)
• Clofazimine added for high bacterial loads

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the primary immunomodulatory drug used to suppress Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) reactions triggered during dapsone therapy.
back:
• Thalidomide
• Reduces inflammatory response in lepromatous leprosy
• Used for reactional states, not primary infection

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A characteristic adverse effect of the drug [___] is the red-to-brownish black discoloration of the skin and conjunctivae.
back:
• Clofazimine
• Phenazine dye
• Accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient notices their urine and sweat have turned orange-red shortly after starting treatment. This finding is most likely associated with which drug?
back:
• Rifampin
• Benign physical property of the drug
• Not indicative of liver toxicity or bleeding

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the mechanism by which resistance to Dapsone typically emerges in Mycobacterium leprae populations.
back:
• Selection of resistant mutants during monotherapy
• Mutations in genes encoding dihydropteroate synthase
• Occurs more frequently in high-burden lepromatous cases

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the tissue storage and elimination half-lives of Dapsone and Clofazimine.
back:
• Dapsone: Half-life 1–2 days; excreted in urine
• Clofazimine: Half-life ~2 months; stored in RE tissues
• Clofazimine persists longer due to tissue crystals

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Name the three components of the standard triple-drug regimen used to treat multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Rifampin
• Dapsone
• Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary drug of choice for the treatment of leprosy, which acts by competitively inhibiting dihydropteroate synthase, is [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• A sulfone derivative
• Inhibits folate synthesis
• Bacteriostatic against M. leprae

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient treated for multibacillary leprosy develops pink-to-brownish skin discoloration and gastrointestinal intolerance. Identify the causative agent.
back:
• Clofazimine
• A phenazine dye
• Accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues
• Half-life is approximately 2 months

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the mechanism by which Rifampin exerts its bactericidal effect on *Mycobacterium leprae*.
back:
• Binds to the β subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Inhibits bacterial RNA synthesis
• Prevents gene transcription

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended drug regimens for paucibacillary versus multibacillary leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone (6 months)
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine (12 months)
• Triple therapy prevents resistance in high-burden cases

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the drug used in leprosy that is also commonly used to treat or prevent Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia.
back:
• Dapsone
• Alternative for patients intolerant to TMP-SMZ
• Requires G6PD screening

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: During dapsone therapy for lepromatous leprosy, the occurrence of painful erythematous skin nodules and systemic symptoms is known as [___].
back:
• Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL)
• A Type 2 lepra reaction
• Results from antigen release from dying bacilli

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient on dapsone therapy presents with jaundice, fatigue, and Heinz bodies on peripheral smear. What is the likely underlying condition?
back:
• G6PD deficiency
• Dapsone causes oxidative stress
• Leads to acute hemolytic anemia

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the therapeutic role of thalidomide in a patient being treated for lepromatous leprosy.
back:
• Suppresses Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL)
• Immunomodulatory action
• Reserved for severe Type 2 reactions

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Distinguish between the bactericidal and bacteriostatic components of the standard triple-drug regimen for leprosy.
back:
• Rifampin: Rapidly bactericidal
• Dapsone: Primarily bacteriostatic
• Clofazimine: Primarily bacteriostatic

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the macrolide antibiotic that has demonstrated clinical activity against *Mycobacterium leprae*.
back:
• Clarithromycin
• Inhibits 50S ribosomal subunit
• Used in alternative regimens for NTM and leprosy

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Dapsone acts as a primary anti-leprosy agent by competitively inhibiting the synthesis of [___].
back:
• Folate.
• It inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Mechanism is structurally and functionally analogous to sulfonamides.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient presents with skin lesions showing a low organism burden (paucibacillary leprosy). The recommended WHO multidrug therapy (MDT) for this patient consists of [___] and [___].
back:
• Dapsone.
• Rifampin.
• This two-drug regimen prevents the emergence of dapsone-resistant strains.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Discuss the pharmacokinetic distribution and primary clinical side effect of Clofazimine.
back:
• Distribution: Stored widely in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin.
• Half-life: Extremely long (approx. 2 months).
• Side Effect: Red-brown to black discoloration of skin and conjunctivae.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the drug combinations required for Paucibacillary versus Multibacillary leprosy as per WHO guidelines.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin.
• Multibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin + Clofazimine.
• MDT is mandatory for both to prevent resistance.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Enumerate the three specific drugs used in the standard MDT for lepromatous (multibacillary) leprosy.
back:
• Dapsone (Sulfone).
• Rifampin (Rifamycin).
• Clofazimine (Phenazine dye).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The painful inflammatory condition known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL), which may occur during dapsone therapy, is specifically suppressed by [___].
back:
• Thalidomide.
• Used to manage the immune-mediated Type 2 reaction.
• Corticosteroids may also be indicated in severe cases.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient on leprosy treatment presents with cyanosis and headache; lab tests confirm methemoglobinemia. Which component of the MDT is the most likely cause?
back:
• Dapsone.
• Methemoglobinemia is a common, dose-related toxic effect of sulfones.
• Methemoglobin levels are usually not clinically significant at standard doses.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the biochemical risk of administering Dapsone to a patient with G6PD deficiency.
back:
• Dapsone is an oxidant drug.
• It induces hemolytic anemia in G6PD-deficient individuals.
• Patients should be screened for the deficiency before starting therapy.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the bactericidal efficacy of Rifampin versus Dapsone in the treatment of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Rifampin: Highly bactericidal; kills 99.9% of bacilli rapidly.
• Dapsone: Primarily bacteriostatic; inhibits folate synthesis.
• MDT utilizes both to achieve radical cure.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: State the adult daily dosage and route for Dapsone in the standard treatment of leprosy.
back:
• Dosage: 100 mg.
• Route: Oral.
• It is well absorbed and widely distributed to tissues.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The standard WHO triple-drug regimen for the treatment of multibacillary leprosy consists of Dapsone, Rifampin, and [___].
back: • Clofazimine

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient currently on multi-drug therapy (MDT) presents with a pink-to-brownish skin discoloration and darkening of the conjunctivae. Which drug is the likely cause?
back:
• Clofazimine
• It is a phenazine dye that accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Dapsone exerts its bacteriostatic effect on Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Competitive inhibition of dihydropteroate synthase
• Antagonizes p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Prevents the synthesis of folic acid

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A clinician is assigning treatment for two patients: one with smear-negative paucibacillary leprosy and one with smear-positive multibacillary leprosy. Contrast the drug components and typical duration required for these cases.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone (6 months)
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine (12 months)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Prior to starting Dapsone for leprosy, why is it critical to screen the patient for G6PD deficiency?
back:
• Dapsone causes oxidative stress
• Can trigger severe hemolytic anemia
• Methemoglobinemia is also a risk

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: During the treatment of lepromatous leprosy, the severe inflammatory condition known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) is specifically suppressed using [___].
back:
• Thalidomide
• Corticosteroids are an alternative

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient undergoing treatment for leprosy notices that their urine and sweat have turned a harmless orange-red color. Which component of their MDT regimen is responsible?
back:
• Rifampin
• This is a benign side effect due to the drug's color and excretion.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the unique pharmacokinetic properties of Clofazimine that result in its exceptionally long terminal half-life of roughly 2 months.
back:
• Highly lipophilic dye
• Sequestered as crystals in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin
• Slow release from tissue deposits

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast the molecular targets of Rifampin and Dapsone in the management of leprosy.
back:
• Rifampin: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (inhibits RNA synthesis)
• Dapsone: Dihydropteroate synthase (inhibits folate synthesis)

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: To which chemical class of antibiotics does Clofazimine belong?
back: • Phenazine dye

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: According to the WHO protocol for leprosy management, the standard 6-month treatment regimen for paucibacillary (PB) cases includes Dapsone and [___].
back:
• Rifampin
• Dapsone (daily dose)
• Rifampin (once-monthly supervised dose)
• Duration is strictly 6 months

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A 30-year-old patient with over 5 skin lesions and a positive skin smear is diagnosed with multibacillary leprosy. Identify the WHO-recommended triple therapy drugs for this condition.
back:
• Rifampin
• Dapsone
• Clofazimine
• This combination is administered for a total of 12 months.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the biological pathway targeted by Dapsone to inhibit the growth of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Acts as a structural analog of PABA
• Prevents synthesis of dihydrofolic acid
• Similar mechanism to sulfonamides

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended treatment duration and drug count for Paucibacillary (PB) versus Multibacillary (MB) leprosy.
back:
• PB: 2 drugs (Rifampin, Dapsone) for 6 months
• MB: 3 drugs (Rifampin, Dapsone, Clofazimine) for 12 months
• PB is for low bacterial load; MB is for high burden

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Name the specific immunological reaction often occurring during lepromatous leprosy treatment and its first-line suppressive agent.
back:
• Reaction: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)
• Treatment: Thalidomide
• Characterized by painful skin nodules and systemic symptoms

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: In the WHO multibacillary MDT, the specific drug responsible for causing reversible reddish-brown skin and conjunctival discoloration is [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• It is a phenazine dye
• Slowly released from reticuloendothelial stores
• Side effect is cosmetic but can be distressing

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A patient undergoing leprosy treatment presents with sudden jaundice and dark urine. Laboratory results confirm hemolytic anemia. This clinical finding is most likely a side effect of [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• Risk is significantly increased in G6PD-deficient patients
• Can also cause methemoglobinemia (cyanosis)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Detail the role of Rifampin in the Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) for leprosy including its molecular target.
back:
• Role: Highly bactericidal against M. leprae
• Target: Binds to the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Inhibits bacterial RNA synthesis

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Distinguish between the bacterial burden criteria used to categorize leprosy as Paucibacillary versus Multibacillary for treatment selection.
back:
• Paucibacillary: 1-5 skin lesions; smear-negative at all sites
• Multibacillary: >5 skin lesions; or smear-positive at any site

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Identify the macrolide antibiotic mentioned as an active agent against Mycobacterium leprae that can be used if standard drugs are unavailable.
back:
• Clarithromycin
• Derived from Erythromycin
• Inhibits protein synthesis via 50S ribosomal subunit
• Also active against MAC and M. kansasii

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: In the standard treatment of leprosy, the bacteriostatic drug [___] acts by competitively inhibiting dihydropteroate synthase and is notorious for causing hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients.
back:
* Dapsone (Sulfone)
* Inhibits folate synthesis from PABA
* Bacteriostatic against M. leprae
* Can cause methemoglobinemia and Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient presents with tender, erythematous skin nodules and fever shortly after starting Multi-Drug Therapy. This inflammatory condition, termed Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL), is primarily triggered by the drug [___].
back:
* Dapsone
* Represents a Type 2 Lepra reaction
* Occurs due to release of bacterial antigens
* Managed with thalidomide or corticosteroids.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role of Clofazimine in the management of leprosy, specifically its effect on intracellular bacterial processes.
back:
* Phenazine dye
* Binds to DNA, inhibiting template function
* Generates cytotoxic oxygen radicals
* Provides anti-inflammatory action helpful in managing lepra reactions.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A 28-year-old male with multiple anesthetic skin patches and positive slit-skin smears is diagnosed with Multibacillary leprosy. Contrast his treatment regimen with that of a Paucibacillary patient.
back:
* Multibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin + Clofazimine for 12 months.
* Paucibacillary: Dapsone + Rifampin for 6 months.
* Difference: Clofazimine is added for high bacterial loads.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Which bactericidal drug in the leprosy MDT regimen targets DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and can lead to orange discoloration of body fluids?
back:
* Rifampin
* Inhibits RNA synthesis (transcription)
* Highly bactericidal for M. leprae
* Potent inducer of hepatic CYP450 enzymes.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A reversible but prominent side effect of therapy for Multibacillary leprosy is [___] discoloration of the skin and conjunctiva.
back:
* Reddish-brown to black pigmentation
* Caused by Clofazimine accumulation
* Crystals seen in reticuloendothelial cells
* May take months to clear post-treatment.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient with leprosy being treated with MDT complains of palpitations. An ECG shows QT interval prolongation. Which agent in the combination therapy is most likely responsible?
back:
* Clofazimine
* Known to cause cardiac conduction abnormalities
* Requires careful monitoring if co-administered with other QT-prolonging drugs.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Describe the metabolic blockade created by Dapsone that results in its bacteriostatic effect on Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
* Competitive antagonism of Para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
* Inhibits the enzyme dihydropteroate synthase
* Prevents synthesis of dihydrofolic acid
* Ultimately halts purine and DNA production.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Distinguish between the bactericidal and bacteriostatic components of the standard World Health Organization leprosy treatment.
back:
* Rifampin: Potently bactericidal; inhibits RNA polymerase.
* Dapsone: Bacteriostatic; folate antagonist.
* Clofazimine: Weakly bactericidal; DNA-binding agent.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: List the three drugs that constitute the first-line Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) for leprosy recommended by the WHO.
back:
* Dapsone (Sulfone derivative)
* Rifampin (Rifamycin antibiotic)
* Clofazimine (Phenazine dye)
* Used in combination to prevent drug resistance.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: In the treatment of leprosy, the most widely used sulfone that functions as a structural analog of PABA to inhibit folate synthesis is [___].
back: * Dapsone (diaminodiphenylsulfone). * Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase. * Primarily bacteriostatic against Mycobacterium leprae.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A leprosy patient develops painful, erythematous skin nodules and fever during therapy. This condition, Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL), is frequently triggered by antigens from dying bacilli during treatment with which sulfone?
back: * Dapsone. * ENL is a type II hypersensitivity reaction to bacillary antigens. * Occurs most commonly in lepromatous (multibacillary) leprosy.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the role of Clofazimine in leprosy management and contrast its clinical usage with the paucibacillary regimen.
back: * Role: Added to MDT to prevent dapsone resistance. * Usage: Reserved for multibacillary (lepromatous) leprosy. * Contrast: Paucibacillary regimens typically omit Clofazimine, using only Rifampin and Dapsone.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient presents with multiple skin lesions and high bacillary counts. Contrast the WHO-recommended multidrug therapy (MDT) for this multibacillary case versus a paucibacillary case.
back: * Multibacillary: Triple therapy with Rifampin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine. * Paucibacillary: Dual therapy with Rifampin and Dapsone only. * Both utilize Rifampin as the primary bactericidal agent.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Enumerate the three primary pharmacological agents used in the World Health Organization (WHO) multidrug therapy for leprosy.
back: * Dapsone (Folate synthesis inhibitor). * Rifampin (RNA polymerase inhibitor). * Clofazimine (Phenazine dye).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The anti-leprosy agent [___] is characterized by high tissue storage and a long half-life of two months, often causing a brownish-black discoloration of the skin and conjunctivae.
back: * Clofazimine. * Discoloration is due to storage in reticuloendothelial tissues. * Also used for its anti-inflammatory effects in ENL.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient on multidrug therapy for leprosy develops jaundice and dark urine. Evaluation reveals acute hemolysis. Which specific drug was likely responsible in the setting of a possible G6PD deficiency?
back: * Dapsone. * Causes oxidative stress in erythrocytes. * Patients should be screened for G6PD deficiency before initiation.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of Dapsone and how its effect on Mycobacterium leprae differs from that of Rifampin.
back: * Dapsone: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase (bacteriostatic). * Rifampin: Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (bactericidal). * MDT combines them to maximize efficacy and prevent resistance.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Contrast Dapsone and Clofazimine regarding their half-lives and the significance of their metabolic clearance.
back: * Dapsone: T1/2 of 1-2 days; primarily acetylated in the liver. * Clofazimine: T1/2 of ~2 months; slowly released from tissue deposits. * Clofazimine persists in the body long after treatment stops.

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the drug used to suppress severe Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) and its major contraindication.
back: * Drug: Thalidomide. * Use: Suppresses inflammatory nodules in leprosy. * Contraindication: Pregnancy (highly teratogenic).

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: The primary drug for leprosy that functions by inhibiting the bacterial enzyme dihydropteroate synthase to block folate synthesis is [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• Competitively antagonizes p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Primarily bacteriostatic against Mycobacterium leprae
• Also used for Pneumocystis jiroveci prophylaxis

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient presents with symmetric skin nodules and a high bacterial load on skin smear. The recommended WHO triple-drug regimen for this multibacillary condition consists of [___].
back:
• Dapsone
• Rifampin
• Clofazimine
• Standard duration is 12 months for multibacillary disease

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Explain the mechanism of action of Rifampin in the management of Mycobacterium leprae infections.
back:
• Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Blocks bacterial RNA synthesis
• Highly bactericidal against M. leprae
• Prevents emergence of dapsone resistance

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: A patient with few anesthetic patches and negative smears (paucibacillary) is compared to one with symmetric skin thickening and numerous bacilli (multibacillary). Contrast the standard WHO drug combinations for these two categories.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Dual therapy with Rifampin and Dapsone
• Multibacillary: Triple therapy with Rifampin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine
• Prevents resistance in high-burden cases

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: Identify the characteristic dermatological and ocular side effects associated with long-term Clofazimine therapy.
back:
• Reddish-brown skin discoloration
• Pigmentation of conjunctivae
• Ichthyosis (skin dryness)
• Reversible upon discontinuation but slow to resolve

category: Enumerate the drugs for leprosy
front: In clinical classification for treatment, the presence of more than five skin lesions or a positive skin smear categorizes leprosy as multibacillary, requiring the specific addition of [___] to the dual regimen.
back:
• Clofazimine
• Phenazine dye
• Essential for preventing resistance in multibacillary leprosy
• possesses anti-inflammatory properties helpful in erythema nodosum leprosum

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Dapsone, a cornerstone of leprosy Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT), acts by competitively inhibiting the enzyme [___] in the folate synthesis pathway of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
* Dihydropteroate synthase
* Prevents synthesis of dihydrofolic acid
* Mechanism is structurally similar to sulfonamides

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A patient presents with seven hypopigmented, anaesthetic skin patches and a positive skin smear for acid-fast bacilli. Identify the WHO classification and the required treatment duration.
back:
* Multibacillary (MB) Leprosy
* Treatment duration: 12 months
* Regimen: Rifampicin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the role of Rifampicin in the Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) for leprosy regarding its cellular target and bactericidal activity.
back:
* Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
* Blocks bacterial transcription and RNA synthesis
* Most potent bactericidal agent against M. leprae in the MDT regimen

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the drug components and recommended treatment durations for WHO-defined Paucibacillary (PB) versus Multibacillary (MB) leprosy.
back:
* PB: Rifampicin + Dapsone for 6 months
* MB: Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine for 12 months
* PB is for 1-5 lesions; MB is for >5 lesions or smear positivity

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: In the WHO supervised monthly dose for Multibacillary leprosy, which two specific drugs must be administered directly by a health worker to ensure compliance?
back:
* Rifampicin (600 mg)
* Clofazimine (300 mg)
* Remaining Dapsone and Clofazimine are self-administered daily

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: According to WHO criteria, leprosy patients with [___] or fewer skin lesions and a negative skin smear are treated under the Paucibacillary (PB) protocol.
back:
* Five (5)
* PB requires only 2 drugs (Rifampicin and Dapsone)
* Treatment duration is shortened to 6 months

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A leprosy patient on MDT develops painful subcutaneous nodules, fever, and neuritis. Identify this reaction and the specific drug used to suppress it according to the text.
back:
* Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL / Type 2 Reaction)
* Suppressed by Thalidomide
* Caused by immune complex deposition (Type III hypersensitivity)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the immunological difference between a Type 1 (Reversal) reaction and a Type 2 (ENL) reaction occurring during leprosy management.
back:
* Type 1: Delayed-type hypersensitivity (Type IV); involves nerve swelling
* Type 2: Humoral immune response (Type III); involves systemic symptoms and vasculitis
* Both require immediate anti-inflammatory treatment to prevent permanent nerve damage

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the primary adverse effects of Dapsone and Clofazimine that are critical for patient counseling during leprosy treatment.
back:
* Dapsone: Dose-related hemolysis (risk in G6PD deficiency) and methemoglobinemia
* Clofazimine: Reddish-black skin/conjunctival discoloration and GI distress
* Clofazimine skin changes take months to reverse after cessation

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Identify the phenazine dye in the MDT regimen that is stored in the reticuloendothelial system and possesses a half-life of roughly 2 months.
back:
* Clofazimine
* Visible as crystals inside phagocytic cells
* Slowly released from tissue stores, resulting in prolonged effect

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: The WHO-recommended Multidrug Therapy (MDT) duration for a patient classified as Paucibacillary (PB) leprosy is exactly [___] months.
back:
• 6 months
• Completed within a maximum of 9 months
• Consists of monthly Rifampicin and daily Dapsone

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A 35-year-old male presents with eight anesthetic skin patches and multiple thickened nerves. According to WHO criteria, the classification and required therapy duration are [___].
back:
• Classification: Multibacillary (MB) leprosy
• Duration: 12 months
• Criteria: >5 lesions or more than one nerve involved

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the biological mechanism of Rifampicin when used as the monthly supervised component of leprosy MDT.
back:
• Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Blocks viral/bacterial mRNA synthesis
• Highly bactericidal against Mycobacterium leprae

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the drug components of the WHO Paucibacillary (PB) versus Multibacillary (MB) adult treatment packs.
back:
• PB Pack: Rifampicin (600mg monthly) and Dapsone (100mg daily)
• MB Pack: Rifampicin (600mg monthly), Dapsone (100mg daily), and Clofazimine (300mg monthly/50mg daily)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Specify the standard drug used for the acute management of a Type 1 (Reversal) Lepra reaction with nerve involvement.
back:
• Prednisolone (Corticosteroids)
• Controls delayed hypersensitivity (Type IV)
• Prevents permanent nerve damage and disability

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: In the standard WHO Multibacillary (MB) regimen, the two drugs administered under direct supervision once every 28 days are [___] and [___].
back:
• Rifampicin (600 mg)
• Clofazimine (300 mg)
• Ensures compliance for the most potent bactericidal components

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A leprosy patient on MDT develops new, painful, erythematous nodules and high fever. Identify the reaction type and the indicated drug for severe cases unresponsive to steroids.
back:
• Reaction: Type 2 (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum)
• Treatment: Thalidomide (specific for ENL)
• Caused by immune complex deposition (Type III hypersensitivity)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Describe the specific inhibitory action of Dapsone within the folate synthesis pathway of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Competitive inhibitor of dihydropteroate synthase
• Structural analog of p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Bacteriostatic action by preventing folic acid production

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Distinguish between the Paucibacillary (PB) and Multibacillary (MB) classification based solely on the bacterial index (BI) from a slit-skin smear.
back:
• PB: Skin smears are negative for Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) at all sites
• MB: Skin smear is positive at any site (even if lesion count is low)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Identify the unique dermatological side effect associated with the daily component of the Multibacillary (MB) MDT regimen.
back:
• Clofazimine-induced skin discoloration
• Manifests as brownish-black pigmentation
• Slowly reversible upon discontinuation of the drug

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: According to the WHO, standard Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) for leprosy includes Rifampicin, Dapsone, and [___] for the treatment of multibacillary cases.
back:
• Clofazimine
• Included in Multibacillary (MB) regimens only
• Acts as a phenazine dye with anti-inflammatory properties

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A 30-year-old male presents with four hypopigmented, anaesthetic skin lesions and negative slit-skin smears. What is the WHO-recommended duration for his antibiotic regimen?
back:
• 6 months
• Patient is classified as Paucibacillary (PB) leprosy (1–5 lesions)
• Regimen: Rifampicin (monthly) and Dapsone (daily)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the biological mechanism of Dapsone's anti-myobacterial activity in the treatment of leprosy.
back:
• Competitive inhibition of dihydropteroate synthase
• Structural analog of p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Blocks folate synthesis required for nucleic acid production

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO classification criteria for Paucibacillary (PB) and Multibacillary (MB) leprosy based on skin lesions and smears.
back:
• PB: 1–5 skin lesions; negative smears at all sites
• MB: >5 skin lesions; or any positive slit-skin smear regardless of lesion count

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: What is the standard WHO-recommended treatment duration for a patient diagnosed with multibacillary (MB) leprosy?
back:
• 12 months
• Consists of Rifampicin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine
• Designed to prevent relapse and drug resistance

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: The development of reddish-black skin discoloration and dark conjunctivae in a leprosy patient is a characteristic side effect of [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• Due to drug accumulation in reticuloendothelial tissues and skin
• Reversible upon discontinuation, though slow to resolve

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A leprosy patient on MDT develops painful subcutaneous nodules, fever, and neuritis. What is the underlying immunologic diagnosis?
back:
• Type 2 Lepra Reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum)
• Occurs primarily in multibacillary patients
• Caused by an Arthus-type immune complex deposition (Type III hypersensitivity)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the role of Rifampicin within the WHO Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) pulse dosing protocol.
back:
• Administered as a 600 mg monthly supervised dose
• Highly bactericidal against Mycobacterium leprae
• Must always be used in combination to prevent rapid selection of resistant mutants

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the management of a Type 1 lepra reaction with a severe Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL).
back:
• Type 1: High-dose corticosteroids to prevent nerve damage
• Type 2: Thalidomide is the treatment of choice (standard alternative is corticosteroids)

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Prior to initiating Dapsone, which genetic deficiency should ideally be screened to prevent acute hemolytic anemia?
back:
• Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
• Dapsone causes oxidative stress in erythrocytes
• Leads to methemoglobinemia and hemolysis in deficient individuals

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: For the management of multibacillary leprosy, the WHO-recommended triple-drug regimen includes Dapsone, Rifampin, and [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• Used to prevent dapsone resistance and treat inflammatory reactions
• Administered for a standard duration of 12 months.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A 40-year-old patient being treated for leprosy presents with reddish-brown skin discoloration and darkened conjunctivae. Identify the drug responsible and its unique pharmacokinetic property.
back:
• Clofazimine
• Highly lipophilic phenazine dye
• Accumulates in reticuloendothelial tissues with a half-life of roughly 2 months.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the mechanism of action of Dapsone in the treatment of Mycobacterium leprae.
back:
• Structural analog of p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
• Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Blocks the synthesis of folate, halting nucleic acid production.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended drug regimens for Paucibacillary (PB) versus Multibacillary (MB) leprosy.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone for 6 months
• Multibacillary: Rifampin + Dapsone + Clofazimine for 12 months
• MB requires Clofazimine to target higher bacterial loads.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Which medication is specifically used to suppress the severe systemic inflammatory reaction known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)?
back:
• Thalidomide
• Effectively manages ENL symptoms but is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to severe teratogenicity.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: In the WHO leprosy protocol, Rifampin is administered as a supervised monthly dose of [___] mg.
back:
• 600 mg
• Potent bactericidal agent inhibiting DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Essential component in both PB and MB regimens.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
coreConcept: Dapsone Side Effects in G6PD Deficiency
front: A leprosy patient with a known history of G6PD deficiency is started on the standard WHO regimen. He soon develops pallor and dark urine. Identify the likely drug and complication.
back:
• Dapsone
• Causes oxidative stress in erythrocytes
• Results in dose-related Hemolysis or Hemolytic Anemia.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
coreConcept: Bactericidal vs Bacteriostatic Roles in MDT
front: How does the role of Rifampin differ from Dapsone in the clinical clearance of leprosy parasites?
back:
• Rifampin: Highly bactericidal; rapidly reduces bacterial viability within days
• Dapsone: Primarily bacteriostatic; requires prolonged administration to inhibit folate metabolism.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the diagnostic criteria for initiating Paucibacillary (PB) therapy versus Multibacillary (MB) therapy based on skin smears.
back:
• Paucibacillary: Smear-negative at all sites
• Multibacillary: Smear-positive at any site
• MB requires more intensive therapy due to higher infectivity.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Name the two secondary drugs commonly substituted for leprosy patients who cannot tolerate or fail standard Rifampin/Dapsone therapy.
back:
• Minocycline
• Ofloxacin
• Both provide alternative bactericidal activity against M. leprae.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: WHO classifies leprosy for multidrug therapy purposes into two categories based on the number of lesions: [___] (1-5 lesions) and [___] (>5 lesions).
back: • Paucibacillary (PB) refers to 1-5 lesions with negative smears. • Multibacillary (MB) refers to >5 lesions or positive smears. • WHO MDT classification determines the specific drug combination and duration.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A patient presents with symmetric skin nodules and a positive skin smear for acid-fast bacilli (Multibacillary leprosy). The WHO recommended 12-month triple therapy regimen includes [___].
back: • Rifampin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine. • Standard duration is 12 months. • Triple therapy is essential for high bacterial loads to ensure total eradication and prevent the selection of resistant mutants.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the bactericidal role of Rifampin in the WHO standard leprosy protocol.
back: • Targets bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase to inhibit transcription. • Acts as a potent bactericidal agent against M. leprae. • Administered as a once-monthly supervised dose in the WHO MDT protocol.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the primary adverse effects of Dapsone and Clofazimine in leprosy treatment.
back: • Dapsone: Frequently causes dose-related hemolysis, particularly in G6PD-deficient patients, and methemoglobinemia. • Clofazimine: Known for causing distinctive brownish-black skin discoloration and potentially serious gastrointestinal side effects during prolonged use.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Identify the standard duration of WHO multidrug therapy (MDT) for Paucibacillary leprosy.
back: • Total duration of 6 months. • Utilizes a two-drug regimen (Rifampin and Dapsone). • Designed for patients with limited bacterial burden and 1-5 skin lesions to achieve radical cure.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: During dapsone therapy for lepromatous leprosy, a systemic inflammatory reaction called [___] may occur, which is managed with thalidomide.
back: • Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL). • Represents a Type 2 hypersensitivity reaction to dying bacilli. • Characterized by fever and painful skin nodules, often requiring thalidomide or corticosteroids for management.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A 25-year-old with three hypo-pigmented, anesthetic skin lesions is diagnosed with Paucibacillary leprosy. The required WHO treatment protocol is [___].
back: • Combination of Rifampin and Dapsone. • 6-month treatment course is standard. • Rifampin is given at 600mg monthly (supervised) and Dapsone at 100mg daily (unsupervised) for paucibacillary disease.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: How does Clofazimine carry out its secondary biological function in the management of leprosy?
back: • Acts as a phenazine dye with significant anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. • Binds to fungal DNA but also stabilizes lysosomal membranes in host cells. • Useful for suppressing the inflammatory Erythema Nodosum Leprosum reaction.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the mechanisms of Dapsone and Rifampin in targeting Mycobacterium leprae.
back: • Dapsone: Sulfone that competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase, blocking folate synthesis. • Rifampin: Rifamycin that binds to the beta-subunit of RNA polymerase, halting transcription. • This combination prevents resistant strains from emerging.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Name the three drugs required in the WHO standard Multidrug Therapy (MDT) for multibacillary leprosy.
back: • Rifampin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine. • Used for 12 months to treat smear-positive or highly infectious cases. • This multidrug approach is the global standard for curing leprosy and ending disease transmission.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: According to WHO classification, patients presenting with 1 to 5 anaesthetic skin lesions and a negative slit skin smear are categorized as [___].
back:
• Paucibacillary (PB) leprosy.
• Requires 6 months of multidrug therapy (MDT).
• Standard regimen excludes daily Clofazimine.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A patient presents with 7 symmetrical skin patches and multiple thickened nerves. Slit skin smear confirms acid-fast bacilli. State the WHO category and total treatment duration.
back:
• Category: Multibacillary (MB) leprosy.
• Treatment Duration: 12 months of standard MDT.
• Criteria: >5 lesions or any positive skin smear.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Explain the role and supervised administration frequency of Rifampicin in the standard WHO adult Multibacillary (MB) regimen.
back:
• Role: Potent bactericidal agent inhibiting bacterial RNA polymerase.
• Frequency: 600 mg administered once monthly under direct supervision.
• Significance: Most critical component for killing M. leprae.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the drug components of the WHO Multidrug Therapy (MDT) for adult Paucibacillary (PB) versus Multibacillary (MB) leprosy.
back:
• PB Regimen: Rifampicin (monthly) + Dapsone (daily).
• MB Regimen: Rifampicin (monthly) + Dapsone (daily) + Clofazimine (monthly and daily).
• Key difference: Clofazimine is added for MB cases.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Specify the self-administered components and dosages for an adult on the standard WHO Multibacillary (MB) regimen.
back:
• Dapsone: 100 mg daily.
• Clofazimine: 50 mg daily.
• Duration: Both taken daily for the full 12-month course.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: In the management of Type 1 (Reversal) reactions, the primary drug utilized to prevent irreversible nerve damage is [___].
back:
• Prednisolone (Corticosteroids).
• Regimen: Usually started at 40-60 mg daily and tapered over several months.
• Goal: Suppression of delayed-type hypersensitivity.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A patient on MDT develops painful erythematous nodules, high fever, and orchitis. Identify the complication and the drug specifically indicated for severe cases.
back:
• Complication: Type 2 Reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum).
• Specific Drug: Thalidomide.
• Alternative: High-dose Prednisolone or Clofazimine if Thalidomide is unavailable.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: How does Dapsone exert its therapeutic effect against Mycobacterium leprae within the MDT protocol?
back:
• Mechanism: Folate synthesis antagonist.
• Target: Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Property: Bacteriostatic against M. leprae; helps prevent emergence of Rifampicin resistance.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: Contrast the WHO-recommended child doses (ages 10-14) versus adult doses for the monthly supervised component of MB therapy.
back:
• Rifampicin: 450 mg (Child) vs 600 mg (Adult).
• Clofazimine: 150 mg (Child) vs 300 mg (Adult).
• Dapsone: 50 mg (Child) vs 100 mg (Adult) supervised.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: What is the recommended protocol if a patient fails to complete the 12-month MB course within the maximum allowed timeframe?
back:
• WHO Rule: 12 months of treatment must be completed within 18 months.
• Failure: If timeframe is exceeded, the patient is considered a defaulter.
• Action: Restart the full course of MDT.

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: The WHO multidrug therapy (MDT) for multibacillary (MB) leprosy includes a 12-month regimen of Rifampicin, Dapsone, and [___].
back:
• Clofazimine
• Included in the standard MB blister pack
• Acts as both an anti-inflammatory and bactericidal agent

category: Explain standard protocols (WHO recommendation) for management of leprosy
front: A patient presents with four distinct anesthetic skin lesions and a negative slit-skin smear. State the WHO treatment classification.
back:
• Paucibacillary (PB) leprosy
• Classification covers patients with 1 to 5 skin lesions
