• Diethylcarbamazine (DEC)
• A synthetic piperazine derivative
• Increases susceptibility of microfilariae to destruction by host defense mechanisms
• Major adverse effects result from release of proteins from dying worms

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 40-year-old patient with strongyloidiasis is prescribed an antihelminthic that subsequently causes dizziness, severe nausea, and a rare but fatal progression to Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Identify the likely medication.
back:
• Thiabendazole
• A benzimidazole compound with higher toxicity than newer analogs
• Common effects: Anorexia, nausea, and vomiting
• Serious risks: Irreversible liver failure and fatal skin reactions

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of ivermectin-induced paralysis in nematodes and arthropods.
back:
• Potentiates glutamate-gated and GABA-gated chloride channels
• Increases membrane conductance to chloride ions
• Leads to hyperpolarization of neuromuscular membranes
• Results in flaccid paralysis and eventual death of the nematode

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Distinguish between diethylcarbamazine and ivermectin regarding their current use in treating onchocerciasis.
back:
• Ivermectin: Current drug of choice; selectively microfilaricidal; effectively blocks microfilarial release
• Diethylcarbamazine: No longer standard for this indication
• DEC induces more severe systemic reactions and carries significant risk of irreversible ocular damage

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Name the primary indication and biochemical target of metrifonate.
back:
• Indication: Treatment of Schistosoma haematobium infections
• Target: Organophosphate cholinesterase inhibition
• Temporarily paralyzes adult worms, causing transit to the lungs for destruction
• Not active against Schistosoma mansoni or japonicum

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The primary mechanism of [___] involves binding to the d-Ala-d-Ala terminus of nascent peptidoglycan pentapeptides, thereby inhibiting transglycosylase and cell wall cross-linking.
back:
• Vancomycin
• Inhibits cell wall synthesis
• Results in weakened peptidoglycan and cell lysis

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 4-day-old neonate presents with vomiting, flaccidity, and an ashen-gray skin color after receiving an antibiotic for a suspected infection. This condition results from the inhibition of [___] in the absence of adequate glucuronic acid conjugation.
back:
• 50S ribosomal subunit (peptidyl transferase)
• Diagnosis: Gray Baby Syndrome
• Causative agent: Chloramphenicol

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the role of the 30S ribosomal subunit in the bactericidal activity of Aminoglycosides.
back:
• Irreversibly binds 30S subunit
• Interferes with initiation complex formation
• Induces mRNA misreading (incorporation of incorrect amino acids)
• Breaks up polysomes into nonfunctional monosomes

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast the mechanism of resistance to Vancomycin in Enterococci with the mechanism of resistance to Methicillin in Staphylococci.
back:
• Vancomycin resistance: Modification of d-Ala-d-Ala target site to d-Ala-d-lactate
• Methicillin resistance: Production of altered PBPs (PBP2a) with low antibiotic affinity

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Identify the metabolic step in the folate pathway specifically inhibited by Sulfonamides.
back:
• Competitive inhibition of dihydropteroate synthase
• Prevents condensation of PABA and pteridine
• Blocks synthesis of dihydrofolic acid

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The drug-induced peripheral neuropathy associated with Isoniazid (INH) therapy is caused by a relative deficiency of [___].
back:
• Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)
• INH promotes excretion of pyridoxine
• Managed by daily B6 supplementation (25-50 mg)

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 30-year-old athlete experiences acute Achilles tendon pain after starting a course of Ciprofloxacin. This drug class exerts its effect by targeting [___].
back:
• DNA Gyrase (Topoisomerase II) and Topoisomerase IV
• Prevents DNA relaxation and daughter strand separation
• Adverse Effect: Tendonitis/Tendon Rupture

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Describe the physiological process leading to 'Red Man Syndrome' during the administration of Vancomycin.
back:
• Non-immunologic, rate-dependent release of histamine
• Occurs during rapid IV infusion
• Manifests as flushing, pruritus, and erythematous rash (face and upper torso)

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the ribosomal targets of Macrolides and Tetracyclines.
back:
• Macrolides: Bind 50S subunit; block peptide exit tunnel (inhibit translocation)
• Tetracyclines: Bind 30S subunit; block aminoacyl-tRNA binding to the acceptor (A) site

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Define the primary mechanism by which Amphotericin B induces fungal cell death.
back:
• Binds ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane
• Forms transmembrane pores
• Causes leakage of intracellular ions (K+) and macromolecules

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Benzimidazole derivatives such as albendazole and mebendazole exert their antihelminthic effect primarily by inhibiting the synthesis of [___].
back:
• Microtubules
• They bind to β-tubulin, preventing polymerization
• This disrupts glucose uptake and leads to parasite death.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A patient being treated for Onchocerca volvulus with ivermectin develops high fever, hypotension, and bronchospasm within 24 hours. Identify the pathophysiology behind this reaction.
back:
• Mazzotti reaction
• Caused by the host immune response to antigens released from dying microfilariae
• Managed with corticosteroids and antihistamines.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the cellular mechanism by which Praziquantel induces paralysis and dislodgement of schistosomes and cestodes.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium
• Causes strong muscular contraction followed by paralysis
• Leads to vacuolization and disintegration of the parasite tegument.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetic interaction of corticosteroids (e.g., dexamethasone) when co-administered with Albendazole versus Praziquantel for neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Albendazole: Dexamethasone increases its active sulfoxide metabolite levels
• Praziquantel: Dexamethasone significantly decreases its bioavailability (by up to 50%)
• This makes albendazole preferred in inflammatory CNS cases.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Describe the neuromuscular step targeted by Pyrantel Pamoate to achieve parasite expulsion.
back:
• Acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent
• Stimulates release of acetylcholine and inhibits cholinesterase
• Results in depolarizing paralysis, allowing worms to be expelled by peristalsis.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The antihelminthic agent [___] acts by intensifying GABA-mediated neurotransmission, resulting in the paralysis of nematodes and arthropods.
back:
• Ivermectin
• Only targets peripheral nerves in invertebrates (GABA-gated chloride channels)
• Does not cross the blood-brain barrier in humans at standard doses.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 30-year-old with a high Loa loa microfilarial burden (>2500/mL) receives Diethylcarbamazine. He develops retinal hemorrhages and encephalopathy. What is the clinical application of this finding?
back:
• High-burden loiasis carries a risk of severe toxicity with Diethylcarbamazine
• Toxicity is due to rapid microfilarial destruction
• Albendazole or apheresis is preferred for initial reduction of load.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: How does Doxycycline act as a macrofilaricidal agent against Wuchereria bancrofti despite being an antibiotic?
back:
• Targets Wolbachia, an essential intracellular bacterial symbiont of the worm
• Elimination of Wolbachia leads to sterility and eventual death of adult filarial worms
• Superior to traditional drugs for killing adult stages.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast the metabolic inhibitory effects of Niclosamide with the cholinergic effects of Metrifonate.
back:
• Niclosamide: Inhibits oxidative phosphorylation or stimulates ATPase in cestodes
• Metrifonate: Organophosphate that inhibits cholinesterase, paralyzing S. haematobium
• Niclosamide is for tapeworms; Metrifonate is for flukes.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Name the two most severe, potentially fatal adverse reactions associated with systemic Thiabendazole use that have led to its replacement by safer agents.
back:
• Irreversible liver failure
• Stevens-Johnson syndrome
• (Also high incidence of neuropsychiatric symptoms and GI distress).

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The primary antihelminthic mechanism of albendazole in treating intestinal nematodes involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis.
back:
* Inhibits microtubule synthesis by binding to beta-tubulin.
* Leads to impaired parasite glucose uptake.
* Results in cellular structure disruption and parasite death.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 30-year-old male with Onchocerciasis develops intense pruritus, fever, and lymphadenitis within 24 hours of receiving ivermectin. This clinical reaction is primarily caused by [___].
back:
* Release of proteins from dying microfilariae.
* Known as a Mazotti-like reaction.
* Managed with corticosteroids if severe.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the cellular mechanism by which Praziquantel causes the detachment and death of adult schistosomes.
back:
* Increases cell membrane permeability to Calcium ions.
* Massive Calcium influx causes parasite muscle contraction and paralysis.
* Leads to vacuolization and disintegration of the parasite tegument.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: In a patient with refractory Strongyloidiasis, treatment is changed from Albendazole to Ivermectin. Contrast the mechanism of action of Ivermectin with that of the benzimidazoles.
back:
* Ivermectin: Intensifies GABA-mediated transmission, paralyzing the nematode.
* Benzimidazoles: Inhibit microtubule synthesis by binding beta-tubulin, disrupting cellular structure.
* Ivermectin is the drug of choice for Strongyloides.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Identify the primary risk of using Diethylcarbamazine in patients with very high Loa loa microfilarial loads.
back:
* Encephalopathy and retinal hemorrhages.
* Caused by severe host inflammatory response to dying microfilariae.
* Requires pretreatment screening of microfilarial density.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Severe, irreversible [___] failure and fatal Stevens-Johnson syndrome are rare but life-threatening adverse effects associated with Thiabendazole use.
back:
* Liver failure.
* Thiabendazole is significantly more toxic than other benzimidazoles.
* Often replaced by ivermectin or albendazole for better tolerability.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 40-year-old patient on a 6-month course for hydatid disease develops significant alopecia and pancytopenia. Identify the causative drug and the necessary monitoring.
back:
* Drug: Albendazole.
* Monitoring: Periodic blood counts and liver function tests.
* These are cumulative toxicities of long-term benzimidazole therapy.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the specific mechanism of action of Metrifonate and why it results in the death of Schistosoma haematobium adults in the lungs.
back:
* Organophosphate that inhibits cholinesterase, paralyzing adult worms.
* Paralyzed worms detach and are carried to small lung arterioles.
* Host defenses then destroy the immobilized parasites.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast the adverse effect profile of weekly Chloroquine for malaria prophylaxis with the cumulative toxicities of long-term high-dose therapy.
back:
* Weekly prophylaxis: Generally mild GI upset or pruritus.
* Long-term high-dose: Irreversible retinopathy, ototoxicity, myopathy, and peripheral neuropathy.
* Both risk hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: State the therapeutic reason why Praziquantel is strictly contraindicated in the treatment of ocular cysticercosis.
back:
* Parasite destruction within the eye induces a severe inflammatory response.
* Results in irreversible and permanent tissue damage to the eye.
* Surgical management is preferred for ocular cysts.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The specific 8-aminoquinoline agent used for the radical cure of Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale by targeting dormant liver hypnozoites is [___].
back:
• Primaquine
• Targets exoerythrocytic stages
• Prevents clinical relapses
• Requires G6PD screening before use

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with severe P. falciparum malaria requires urgent parenteral therapy in a US hospital. Identify the dextrorotatory stereoisomer of quinine typically utilized in this setting.
back:
• Quinidine gluconate
• Effective blood schizonticide
• Requires continuous cardiac monitoring (QT prolongation)
• Transition to oral therapy once stable

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role and mechanism of action of the endoperoxide bridge in artemisinin derivatives.
back:
• Acts via production of free radicals
• Triggered by iron-catalyzed cleavage of the bridge
• Leads to rapid parasite death
• Highly effective against asexual erythrocytic stages

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the specific parasite stages targeted by Chloroquine versus Primaquine.
back:
• Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide (erythrocytic stage only)
• Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide (hepatic hypnozoites) and gametocide
• Chloroquine treats symptoms; Primaquine prevents relapses

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary molecular mechanism of resistance utilized by Plasmodium falciparum against Chloroquine.
back:
• Mutations in the PfCRT gene
• Encodes a putative transporter in the food vacuole
• Results in decreased drug accumulation at target site

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The fixed-dose combination commonly used for prophylaxis in multidrug-resistant areas that pairs a hydroxynaphthoquinone with a folate antagonist is [___].
back:
• Malarone (Atovaquone + Proguanil)
• Inhibits mitochondrial electron transport and dihydrofolate reductase
• Taken daily; short post-exposure duration

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from a region with multidrug-resistant P. falciparum presents with fever. Which oral artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) is the preferred standard of care in the USA?
back:
• Coartem (Artemether + Lumefantrine)
• Rapidly kills parasites (artemether) while lumefantrine prevents recrudescence
• Administered with fatty food to improve absorption

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: How does the Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine combination achieve synergistic antimalarial activity?
back:
• Sequential blockade of folate synthesis
• Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
• Prevents purine and DNA synthesis

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the cardiac safety profiles of the phenanthrene methanol Halofantrine with the aryl alcohol Lumefantrine.
back:
• Halofantrine: Severe QT/PR prolongation; risk of fatal arrhythmias
• Lumefantrine: Minor, clinically insignificant QT effects; safe for combination use
• Halofantrine is contraindicated with prior mefloquine use

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Name the prokaryote-like organelle within Plasmodium that is targeted by antibiotics like Doxycycline to inhibit protein synthesis.
back:
• Apicoplast
• Doxycycline acts as a slow-acting blood schizonticide
• Always used in combination for treatment (e.g., with Quinine)

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The only available antimalarial agent active against the dormant hypnozoite stages of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale is [___].
back:
• Primaquine.
• Acts as a tissue schizonticide.
• Essential for achieving a "radical cure" to prevent relapses.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from Sub-Saharan Africa presents with fever and lethargy. Blood smear shows P. falciparum rings. If chloroquine resistance is suspected, name the first-line oral combination therapy approved in the USA.
back:
• Artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem).
• An Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT).
• Highly effective against multi-drug resistant P. falciparum.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of action by which Artemisinin and its analogs carry out their parasiticidal function.
back:
• Production of free radicals.
• Triggered by iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge within the parasite.
• Rapidly acting blood schizonticides.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical usage and administration of Quinine and Quinidine in the management of severe falciparum malaria.
back:
• Quinine: Standard parenteral therapy (IV/IM) outside the USA.
• Quinidine: Dextrorotatory isomer of quinine; used IV in the USA.
• Toxicity: Quinidine is more cardiotoxic (requires ECG monitoring).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two specific enzymes in the folate synthesis pathway targeted by the synergistic combination of Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine.
back:
• Dihydropteroate synthase (inhibited by Sulfadoxine).
• Dihydrofolate reductase (inhibited by Pyrimethamine).
• Blocks sequential steps in purine synthesis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Weekly chemoprophylaxis with the drug [___] is contraindicated in patients with a history of epilepsy or psychiatric disorders.
back:
• Mefloquine.
• Known for severe neuropsychiatric toxicities (seizures, psychosis).
• FDA carries a black box warning for these effects.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient undergoing radical cure for P. vivax develops sudden hemolytic anemia and jaundice. This reaction is caused by Primaquine therapy in the presence of [___].
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
• Standard screening is mandatory before starting therapy.
• Primaquine is contraindicated in pregnancy due to fetal G6PD risk.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the mechanism of action of Chloroquine within the malaria parasite's food vacuole.
back:
• Prevents biocrystallization of heme (hemoglobin breakdown product) into non-toxic hemozoin.
• Build-up of free heme is toxic to the parasite.
• Resistance is mediated by the PfCRT transporter mutation.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the cardiac safety profiles of the phenanthrene-methanols Halofantrine and Lumefantrine.
back:
• Halofantrine: Significant QT/PR prolongation; high risk of fatal arrhythmias.
• Lumefantrine: Minor QT prolongation; clinically insignificant and safe.
• Lumefantrine is only used in combination with Artemether (Coartem).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Define the therapeutic goal of "Blood Schizonticides" and name two representative drugs.
back:
• Goal: Eradicate asexual erythrocytic stages responsible for clinical illness.
• Drugs: Chloroquine, Quinine, Mefloquine, or Artemisinins.
• Do not eliminate dormant liver stages.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
coreConcept: Primaquine clinical utility and hypnozoite eradication
front: In the treatment of dormant hepatic stages (hypnozoites) of *P. vivax* and *P. ovale*, the 8-aminoquinoline of choice is [___].
back:
Primaquine

* Only drug effective against hypnozoite stages.
* Provides a radical cure to prevent relapse.
* Requires G6PD screening prior to administration to avoid hemolysis.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A 30-year-old traveler returning from Nigeria presents with lethargy, high fever, and 1.5% *P. falciparum* parasitemia. Specify the preferred intravenous agent to rapidly reduce the fungal burden and improve survival.
back:
Intravenous Artesunate

* First-line for severe/complicated falciparum malaria.
* Superior survival outcomes compared to quinine/quinidine.
* Very rapidly acting blood schizonticide.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the synergistic mechanism of the combination drug Malarone used in malaria prophylaxis.
back:
Atovaquone + Proguanil

* Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
* Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
* Effective against both tissue and erythrocytic schizonts.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the clinical usage and target site of Metronidazole versus Paromomycin in the management of an amebic liver abscess.
back:
Tissue vs Luminal action

* Metronidazole: Tissue amebicide; kills trophozoites in the liver/wall.
* Paromomycin: Luminal amebicide; eradicates cysts in the bowel.
* Both are needed to ensure complete cure.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the drug class and primary indication for Miltefosine in modern antiprotozoal therapy.
back:
Alkylphosphocholine analog

* First effective oral drug for Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar).
* Also used in New World cutaneous leishmaniasis.
* Teratogenic; contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: The first-line drug for treating advanced African Trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) with central nervous system involvement caused by *T. brucei gambiense* is [___].
back:
Eflornithine

* Ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor.
* Preferred over the more toxic melarsoprol.
* Effective only for West African sleeping sickness.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A patient with AIDS presents with a non-productive cough, fever, and hypoxia. A diagnosis of *Pneumocystis jiroveci* is made. Specify the first-line antiprotozoal regimen and its primary biochemical target.
back:
Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ)

* Targets folate synthesis pathway.
* Sequential inhibition of dihydropteroate synthase and dihydrofolate reductase.
* Pentamidine is reserved for intolerant patients.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Describe how Chloroquine exerts its selective toxicity against susceptible erythrocytic *Plasmodium* parasites.
back:
Prevents biocrystallization of heme

* Heme (toxic) is normally converted to hemozoin (non-toxic).
* Chloroquine blocks this process in parasite food vacuoles.
* Toxic heme buildup leads to parasite death.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Distinguish between the primary drugs used for the early hemolymphatic stage vs. the late CNS stage of East African Sleeping Sickness.
back:
Stage-dependent therapy

* Early stage (*T. brucei rhodesiense*): Suramin.
* Late stage (CNS involvement): Melarsoprol.
* Suramin cannot cross the blood-brain barrier.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the specific antiprotozoal agent used to treat primary toxoplasmosis acquired during pregnancy to reduce congenital transmission risk.
back:
Spiramycin

* A macrolide antibiotic.
* Lowers the risk of vertical transmission to the fetus.
* Does not treat existing fetal infection.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: The drug of choice for treating all clinical forms of extraintestinal amebiasis, including amebic liver abscess, is [___].
back:
• Metronidazole
• Used with a luminal amebicide to ensure total eradication of the infection.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A 5-year-old child presents with lethargy and a 1.5% Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia after returning from Nigeria. According to the WHO, the superior intravenous agent for reducing mortality in this severe case is [___].
back:
• Intravenous Artesunate
• Preferred over quinine/quinidine due to faster parasite clearance and lower toxicity.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism of action of Artemisinin derivatives against malaria parasites.
back:
• Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge
• Production of toxic free radicals
• Damage to parasite proteins and mitochondrial membranes.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the clinical indications for Luminal amebicides versus Tissue amebicides.
back:
• Luminal (e.g., Paromomycin, Iodoquinol): Eradicate cysts in the bowel; treats asymptomatic carriers.
• Tissue (e.g., Metronidazole): Kill trophozoites in bowel wall or liver; treats colitis and abscesses.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: State the primary reason Primaquine is essential for the radical cure of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale.
back:
• Only available drug active against dormant hepatic hypnozoites
• Prevents future clinical relapses from the liver reservoir.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: The first effective oral agent for the treatment of visceral leishmaniasis, particularly in regions with antimonial resistance like India, is [___].
back:
• Miltefosine
• Alkylphosphocholine analog; avoids the need for parenteral administration.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A patient from rural South America presents with acute fever and Romaña sign. If Chagas disease is confirmed, identify the standard nitroimidazole drug used for treatment.
back:
• Benznidazole
• Alternative: Nifurtimox
• Both are effective for acute infection but limited in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: How do folate synthesis inhibitors like Pyrimethamine and Proguanil selectively inhibit plasmodial growth?
back:
• Inhibit plasmodial dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)
• Block conversion of dihydrofolic acid to tetrahydrofolic acid
• Prevents purine and DNA synthesis.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacological properties of Suramin with Melarsoprol in African Trypanosomiasis.
back:
• Suramin: Used for early hemolymphatic stage (East African); does not cross the BBB.
• Melarsoprol: Trivalent arsenical for late CNS stage; highly toxic (risk of reactive encephalopathy).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the non-absorbable aminoglycoside antibiotic used as a first-line luminal amebicide in the USA.
back:
• Paromomycin sulfate
• Minimally absorbed from the gut
• Active against intestinal protozoa like E. histolytica and Giardia.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: In the classification of tissue schizonticides, the drug that targets the primary liver stage of all human malaria species but is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency is [___].
back:
• Primaquine
• Class: 8-Aminoquinoline
• Action: Eradicates hepatic hypnozoites (radical cure for *P. vivax* and *P. ovale*).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A 28-year-old female presents with foul-smelling vaginal discharge and is treated with a single 2g dose of a nitroimidazole. Name the drug and its primary toxicity if taken with alcohol.
back:
• Tinidazole (or Metronidazole)
• Mechanism: Reduction by ferredoxin to toxic metabolites
• Toxicity: Disulfiram-like reaction (nausea/vomiting).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the mechanism of action of Pyrimethamine-Sulfadoxine (Fansidar) and why it is less effective for P. falciparum in many areas today.
back:
• Mechanism: Inhibits sequential steps in plasmodial folate synthesis
• Resistance: Point mutations in dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A patient with kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is choosing between Sodium Stibogluconate and Miltefosine. Contrast these two based on their classification and route of administration.
back:
• Sodium Stibogluconate: Pentavalent antimonial; administered parenterally (IV/IM)
• Miltefosine: Alkylphosphocholine; administered orally; potential teratogen.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: List the essential pharmacological steps for the activation of Proguanil in the prevention of malaria.
back:
• Activation: Prodrug converted to active metabolite cycloguanil
• Enzyme: Host CYP450 enzymes
• Target: Inhibits plasmodial dihydrofolate reductase.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: In the treatment of asymptomatic intestinal amebiasis, the aminoglycoside antibiotic that is preferred because it acts directly as a luminal amebicide without significant systemic absorption is [___].
back:
• Paromomycin
• Action: Eradicates *E. histolytica* cysts in the gut lumen
• Benefit: Negligible systemic toxicity.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: An AIDS patient with a CD4 count of 40 receives monthly inhaled Pentamidine. Explain the clinical application of this specific route and dose.
back:
• Indication: Prophylaxis for *Pneumocystis jiroveci* pneumonia
• Benefit: Localizes drug to lungs, reducing systemic toxicities like hypoglycemia and nephrotoxicity.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Two patients are being treated for severe malaria. One receives intravenous Quinidine and the other intravenous Artesunate. Explain the molecular mechanism of the latter and why it is now preferred.
back:
• Mechanism: Cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge by iron produces parasite-killing free radicals
• Preference: Faster clearance and lower toxicity than Quinidine/Quinine.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the roles of Metronidazole and Diloxanide Furoate in the treatment loop of amebiasis.
back:
• Metronidazole: Systemic amebicide; kills trophozoites in tissues (colitis, abscess)
• Diloxanide: Luminal amebicide; kills cysts in bowel lumen to prevent carriage.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the specific intracellular biochemical target for antimalarial antibiotics such as Doxycycline and Clindamycin.
back:
• Apicoplast
• Mechanism: Inhibits protein synthesis in this prokaryote-like organelle
• Note: Used only in combination due to slow action.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Drugs that target and eliminate the dormant hepatic stages (hypnozoites) of *Plasmodium vivax* and *P. ovale* to prevent disease relapse are classified as [___].
back: Tissue schizonticides (e.g., Primaquine).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from a region in Southeast Asia with documented multidrug-resistant *P. falciparum* presents with fever and chills. Identify the standard oral classification of therapy now recommended in the USA for uncomplicated cases.
back: Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT), specifically Artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism of action used by the artemisinin class (e.g., Artesunate) to kill erythrocytic parasites.
back:
• Production of toxic free radicals.
• Triggered by iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge.
• Potent, rapid-acting blood schizonticidal activity.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical utility and administration of Quinine with its stereoisomer Quinidine in the management of falciparum malaria.
back:
• Quinine: Primarily oral use for uncomplicated resistant cases.
• Quinidine: Intravenous use for severe/complicated malaria.
• Toxicity: Both cause cinchonism and QTc prolongation; Quinidine is more cardiotoxic.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Categorize the components of Fansidar and explain the synergistic biochemical blockade provided by this combination.
back:
• Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Synergy: Blocks two sequential steps in the plasmodial folic acid synthesis pathway.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The pharmacological goal of achieving a 'radical cure' in *P. vivax* malaria requires the use of [___] to target hypnozoites in addition to standard blood schizonticides.
back: Primaquine (an 8-aminoquinoline).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient requiring terminal prophylaxis for *P. vivax* must undergo genetic screening for which enzymatic deficiency prior to receiving 8-aminoquinolines?
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
• Screening prevents acute drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
• Crucial because Primaquine is a potent oxidant.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain how the two components of Malarone (Atovaquone and Proguanil) carry out their biological function during chemoprophylaxis.
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
• Proguanil: Enhances atovaquone's effect and inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Unique benefit: Active against both tissue and erythrocytic schizonts.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast blood schizonticides with gametocides regarding their role in managing an individual patient versus controlling a population epidemic.
back:
• Blood Schizonticides: Terminate clinical illness (individual cure).
• Gametocides: Destroy sexual stages (e.g., Primaquine for *P. falciparum*).
• Public Health: Gametocides prevent mosquito infection, reducing population transmission.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Classify Chloroquine and specify the molecular target it inhibits within the malaria parasite.
back:
• Class: 4-aminoquinoline.
• Target: Parasite food vacuole.
• Mechanism: Prevents biocrystallization of heme into non-toxic hemozoin, causing heme-mediated toxicity.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: The 8-aminoquinoline [___] is the primary drug used for the radical cure of *Plasmodium vivax* and *ovale* because it is the only agent that reliably eradicates dormant liver hypnozoites.
back:
*   Primaquine
*   Acts as a tissue schizonticide
*   Crucial for preventing malaria relapses
*   Requires screening for G6PD deficiency to prevent severe hemolytic anemia

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A patient with amebic dysentery is treated with Metronidazole. To prevent recurrence, a luminal amebicide like [___] must be added to the regimen.
back:
*   Paromomycin (or Iodoquinol/Diloxanide furoate)
*   Nitroimidazoles do not reliably kill luminal cysts
*   Luminal agents target asymptomatic intestinal carriage
*   Essential for complete eradication of *Entamoeba histolytica*

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the mechanism of action between Artemisinins (e.g., Artesunate) and 4-Aminoquinolines (e.g., Chloroquine).
back:
*   Artemisinins: Iron-catalyzed cleavage produces toxic free radicals that damage parasite proteins/membranes
*   Chloroquine: Inhibits heme polymerase, causing toxic free heme accumulation in food vacuoles
*   Both are potent blood schizonticides

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic roles of Melarsoprol and Suramin in managing African Trypanosomiasis.
back:
*   Suramin: First-line for early hemolymphatic *T. brucei rhodesiense*; cannot cross blood-brain barrier
*   Melarsoprol: Trivalent arsenical for advanced CNS disease (crosses BBB)
*   Toxicity: Melarsoprol causes fatal reactive encephalopathy in 5-10% of patients

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the two drug components of the Malarone combination and its specific advantage regarding treatment duration.
back:
*   Components: Atovaquone and Proguanil
*   Synergy: Blocks mitochondrial electron transport and dihydrofolate reductase
*   Advantage: Targets liver and blood stages; prophylaxis only required for 1 week post-exposure

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: [___] is a nitrothiazolyl-salicylamide used to treat metronidazole-resistant *Giardia lamblia* and *Cryptosporidium parvum* by inhibiting the PFOR pathway.
back:
*   Nitazoxanide
*   Active metabolite: Tizoxanide
*   Targets pyruvate-ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR)
*   Lacks the mutagenic effects typically seen with Metronidazole

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: An HIV-positive patient with a CD4 count of 80/μL requires primary prophylaxis against both *Pneumocystis jiroveci* and *Toxoplasma gondii*. The drug of choice is [___].
back:
*   Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ)
*   Dosed as one double-strength tablet daily
*   Antifolate mechanism: Synergistic blockade of PABA conversion and dihydrofolate reductase
*   Reduces morbidity from multiple opportunistic infections

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism of eflornithine in treating West African sleeping sickness and why it is ineffective against the East African species.
back:
*   Mechanism: Irreversible suicide inhibition of ornithine decarboxylase
*   Effect: Depletes polyamines (putrescine/spermidine) needed for cytostasis
*   Differential: Ineffective against *T. b. rhodesiense* due to rapid enzyme turnover and low drug affinity

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Distinguish between the clinical adverse effects of Quinine and Mefloquine.
back:
*   Quinine: Cinchonism (tinnitus, headache), hypoglycemia (via insulin stimulation), and QT prolongation
*   Mefloquine: Serious neuropsychiatric effects (psychosis, seizures, vivid dreams)
*   Mefloquine has an FDA black box warning for CNS toxicity

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Name the aminoglycoside antibiotic used parenterally for visceral leishmaniasis that also serves as a first-line luminal amebicide.
back:
*   Paromomycin
*   Oral use: Eradicates intestinal *E. histolytica* cysts (poorly absorbed)
*   Parenteral use: Alternative for visceral leishmaniasis in cases of drug resistance (e.g., to stibogluconate)

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The drug class specifically targeting dormant liver hypnozoites for the radical cure of Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale is the [___].
back:
• 8-Aminoquinolines.
• Primary example: Primaquine.
• Acts as a tissue schizonticide to prevent relapses.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
coreConcept: First-line Treatment of Resistant Falciparum Malaria
front: A traveler returning from Nigeria presents with lethargy and 1.5% P. falciparum parasitemia. Considering the risk of chloroquine resistance, specify the first-line oral combination therapy available in the USA.
back:
• Artemether-Lumefantrine (Coartem).
• Alternately: Atovaquone-Proguanil (Malarone).
• Use: Uncomplicated falciparum malaria.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism of 4-aminoquinolines (e.g., Chloroquine) within the parasite food vacuole.
back:
• Prevents heme biocrystallization into non-toxic hemozoin.
• Causes buildup of toxic free heme.
• Results in parasite membrane damage and death.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical roles and administration routes of Quinine and Quinidine in the management of severe P. falciparum malaria.
back:
• Quinine: Standard parenteral therapy globally; oral sulfate for uncomplicated cases.
• Quinidine: Dextrorotatory isomer; used intravenously in the USA under cardiac monitoring due to cardiotoxicity (QT prolongation).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: List the two components of the fixed-dose combination drug "Malarone" and identify their respective drug classes.
back:
• Atovaquone: Hydroxynaphthoquinone (inhibits mitochondrial electron transport).
• Proguanil: Biguanide/antifolate (inhibits dihydrofolate reductase).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: According to WHO guidelines, the therapeutic strategy combining a fast-acting endoperoxide with a long-acting partner drug is known as [___].
back:
• Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT).
• Prevents recrudescence and slows resistance development.
• Examples: Artemether-Lumefantrine, Artesunate-Amodiaquine.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. vivax is prescribed Primaquine for terminal prophylaxis. Identify the essential enzyme screening required before initiation to prevent drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD).
• Deficiency causes oxidative stress leading to hemolysis.
• Avoid in G6PD-deficient patients and pregnancy.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role of the endoperoxide bridge in the antimalarial mechanism of Artemisinin derivatives.
back:
• Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge occurs in the parasite.
• Generates toxic free radicals.
• Rapidly kills asexual blood stages (blood schizonticide).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between Tissue Schizonticides and Blood Schizonticides based on their life cycle targets.
back:
• Tissue Schizonticides: Target liver stages (exoerythrocytic); prevent infection/relapse (e.g., Primaquine).
• Blood Schizonticides: Target erythrocytic stages; clinical cure of symptomatic illness (e.g., Chloroquine, Artemisinins).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the drug class and primary clinical utility of Mefloquine.
back:
• Class: Quinoline methanol.
• Use: Chemoprophylaxis in chloroquine-resistant areas and treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
• Black box warning: Potential neuropsychiatric toxicities.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
coreConcept: Classification of Antimalarial Drugs by Life Cycle Stage
front: Drugs that eliminate dormant liver forms (hypnozoites) of *P. vivax* and *P. ovale* are classified as [___] schizonticides.
back:
• Tissue
• Kills dormant hepatic stages to prevent relapses.
• Primary example: Primaquine.
• Essential for radical cure of vivax and ovale malaria.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
coreConcept: Clinical Classification of Amebicides (Tissue vs Luminal)
front: A 30-year-old traveler with amebic liver abscess is treated with metronidazole. To prevent relapse from intestinal carriage, the clinician must add a [___] amebicide such as paromomycin.
back:
• Luminal
• Eradicates *E. histolytica* cysts in the bowel lumen.
• Necessary because tissue amebicides (metronidazole) do not reliably clear luminal parasites.
• Examples: Paromomycin, Iodoquinol, Diloxanide furoate.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Chloroquine exerts its blood schizonticidal effect on susceptible Plasmodia.
back:
• Concentrates in parasite food vacuoles.
• Inhibits biocrystallization of hemoglobin breakdown products (heme) into hemozoin.
• Causes toxic buildup of free heme, leading to parasite cell death.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
coreConcept: Classification of Drugs for African Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the first-line agents used for the early hemolymphatic stage of West African versus East African sleeping sickness.
back:
• West African (*T.b. gambiense*): Pentamidine is the drug of choice.
• East African (*T.b. rhodesiense*): Suramin is the drug of choice.
• Neither drug is effective for advanced CNS disease.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the 8-aminoquinoline drug that acts as a gametocide for all human malaria species and is essential for 'radical cure.'
back:
• Primaquine.
• Gametocidal action: Renders *P. falciparum* gametocytes noninfectious to mosquitoes.
• Radical cure: Eliminates liver hypnozoites of *P. vivax* and *P. ovale*.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: The oral combination drug containing a quinone and a folate antagonist used for both treatment and prophylaxis of resistant *P. falciparum* is [___].
back:
• Malarone (Atovaquone-Proguanil).
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
• Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Discontinued only 1 week after travel due to activity against tissue stages.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A lethargic patient presents with a high *P. falciparum* parasite burden and renal failure. Identify the preferred drug of choice for this severe clinical presentation over traditional quinolines.
back:
• Intravenous Artesunate.
• Rapid-acting blood schizonticide derived from artemisinin.
• Superior to IV quinine/quinidine in mortality reduction.
• Standard of care for severe or complicated malaria.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the synergistic mechanism of action of the combination drug Fansidar (Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine).
back:
• Blocks sequential steps in folate synthesis.
• Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase (PABA analog).
• Pyrimethamine: Inhibits plasmodial dihydrofolate reductase.
• Synergistically inhibits DNA synthesis in blood-stage parasites.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacological class and safety profiles of the luminal amebicides Iodoquinol and Paromomycin.
back:
• Iodoquinol: Halogenated hydroxyquinoline; associated with risk of dose-related neurotoxicity.
• Paromomycin: Aminoglycoside; not absorbed from the gut.
• Paromomycin is generally preferred in the USA due to superior safety/availability.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the first effective oral drug registered for the treatment of visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar).
back:
• Miltefosine.
• Alkylphosphocholine analog.
• Replaces parenteral antimonials or amphotericin B.
• Highly effective in India; contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenicity.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: In the management of malaria, Chloroquine acts by binding to and preventing the biocrystallization of [___] into non-toxic hemozoin within the parasite food vacuole.
back:
• Heme (ferriprotoporphyrin IX)
• Resulting accumulation of free heme is toxic to the Plasmodia.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
coreConcept: P. vivax Life Cycle and Radical Cure
front: A traveler returning from Papua New Guinea presents with fever. Blood smear confirms Plasmodium vivax. Despite initial clinical response to blood schizonticides, the patient relapses months later. This relapse is due to [___].
back:
• Hypnozoites (dormant liver stage)
• Requires radical cure with Primaquine to prevent late reactivation.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the biochemical activation required for Metronidazole to exert its effect against anaerobic protozoa like Entamoeba histolytica.
back:
• Non-enzymatic reduction by reacting with reduced ferredoxin.
• Occurs only in anaerobic cells.
• Produces reactive intermediates that damage DNA.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the treatment approach for a patient with early-stage (hemolymphatic) West African trypanosomiasis versus late-stage disease with CNS involvement.
back:
• Early-stage: Pentamidine (drug of choice).
• Late-stage: Eflornithine (first-line) or Melarsoprol (highly toxic arsenical).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the three chemical classes of drugs used specifically as luminal amebicides to eradicate E. histolytica carriage.
back:
• Dichloroacetamides (Diloxanide furoate)
• Halogenated hydroxyquinolines (Iodoquinol)
• Aminoglycosides (Paromomycin)

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: To prevent drug-induced oxidative hemolysis, patients must be screened for [___] before initiating therapy with Primaquine.
back: • Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: An HIV-positive patient presents with ring-enhancing brain lesions and is diagnosed with Toxoplasmosis. The synergistic first-line treatment regimen consists of [___].
back:
• Pyrimethamine plus Sulfadiazine
• Combined with Folinic acid to limit myelosuppression.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Describe the unique chemical mechanism by which Artemisinins (e.g., Artesunate) kill malaria parasites.
back:
• Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge.
• Production of lethal free radicals that damage parasite proteins.

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the distinct antimalarial mechanisms of the two components found in the fixed-combination drug Malarone.
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
• Proguanil: Inhibits parasite dihydrofolate reductase (via its metabolite cycloguanil).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the first effective oral drug developed for the treatment of Visceral Leishmaniasis.
back: • Miltefosine (an alkylphosphocholine analog).

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: In the radical cure of *Plasmodium vivax* and *Plasmodium ovale* malaria, the drug [___] must be administered to eradicate dormant hypnozoites.
back:
• Primaquine
• Eradicates hepatic stages to prevent relapse
• Requires G6PD testing before administration to avoid hemolysis

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A patient presents with acute American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease). The primary nitroimidazole agent used to eliminate parasites and prevent disease progression is [___].
back:
• Benznidazole
• Alternative: Nifurtimox
• Most effective in acute phase; limited efficacy in chronic disease

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Explain the pharmacodynamic rationale for utilizing Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT) over artemisinin monotherapy for *P. falciparum*.
back:
• Artemisinins have short half-lives (30–60 mins)
• Partner drugs with longer half-lives ensure clearance of residual parasites
• Prevents selection of artemisinin-resistant strains

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A clinician is choosing therapy for early-stage African Trypanosomiasis. Contrast the drug of choice for the West African form (*T.b. gambiense*) versus the East African form (*T.b. rhodesiense*).
back:
• West African (Gambiense): Pentamidine
• East African (Rhodesiense): Suramin
• Neither drug is effective for late-stage disease (CNS involvement)

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the first effective oral medication for visceral leishmaniasis and its primary maternal contraindication.
back:
• Miltefosine
• Contraindication: Pregnancy (teratogenicity)
• Used as an alternative to parenteral sodium stibogluconate or amphotericin B

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: The drug [___] is the first-line antifolate used in combination with sulfadiazine to treat toxoplasmosis.
back:
• Pyrimethamine
• Inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase
• Co-administered with folinic acid (leucovorin) to limit myelosuppression

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: A patient is diagnosed with amebic colitis. Identify the two categories of amebicides required for cure and the primary drug representing each class.
back:
• Tissue amebicide: Metronidazole (kills trophozoites in bowel wall/liver)
• Luminal amebicide: Paromomycin or Iodoquinol (kills organisms in lumen)

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the biochemical mechanisms by which Quinolines (e.g., Chloroquine) and Artemisinins exert their bactericidal effects on plasmodia.
back:
• Quinolines: Prevent biocrystallization of heme into hemozoin, causing toxic heme buildup
• Artemisinins: Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge releases toxic free radicals

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic target of Chloroquine versus Primaquine in the management of *Plasmodium vivax*.
back:
• Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide (targets erythrocytic parasites to stop clinical illness)
• Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide/hypnozoitocide (targets liver stages to prevent relapse)

category: Classify antiprotozoal drugs
front: Identify the primary antiprotozoal drug used to treat both Giardiasis and Trichomoniasis, and its most important behavioral precaution.
back:
• Metronidazole (or Tinidazole)
• Precaution: Avoid alcohol intake (disulfiram-like reaction)
• Mechanism: Reduced intracellularly to toxic intermediates that damage DNA

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Antimalarial drugs that act specifically on the asexual erythrocytic stages to terminate clinical illness are classified as [___].
back:
- Blood schizonticides.
- These kill the stage responsible for clinical symptoms.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient returning from a malaria-endemic region is diagnosed with P. vivax. To prevent a relapse, the clinician must prescribe [___] to target the hypnozoite stage.
back:
- Primaquine.
- It is the only available agent active against dormant hepatic stages.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical interaction between Atovaquone and the plasmodial parasite during treatment.
back:
- Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
- It is effective against both tissue and erythrocytic schizonts.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the molecular targets of the quinoline methanol drugs (Quinine/Mefloquine) with the artemisinin derivatives.
back:
- Quinoline methanols: Suspected interference with heme processing in the food vacuole.
- Artemisinins: Produce toxic free radicals following iron-catalyzed cleavage of an endoperoxide bridge.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Classify the components of the oral antimalarial Malarone and specify its primary clinical utility.
back:
- Components: Atovaquone (quinone) and Proguanil (folate antagonist).
- Utility: Effective for both treatment and daily chemoprophylaxis of resistant P. falciparum.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The antimalarial drug [___] is classified as an 8-aminoquinoline and is uniquely effective against dormant liver stages.
back:
- Primaquine.
- It also has gametocidal activity against all human malaria species.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with a history of epilepsy requires malaria prophylaxis. Which commonly used antimalarial must be avoided due to its potential for neurologic and psychiatric toxicities?
back:
- Mefloquine.
- It is contraindicated in patients with seizures, psychiatric disorders, or cardiac conduction defects.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the synergistic mechanism achieved by combining Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine in the drug Fansidar.
back:
- Blocks sequential steps in the folate pathway.
- Sulfadoxine inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
- Pyrimethamine inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the primary clinical use of intravenous artesunate versus intravenous quinidine in modern severe malaria management.
back:
- Artesunate: First-line standard of care; superior survival and lower toxicity.
- Quinidine: Alternative in the USA when artesunate is unavailable; requires continuous cardiac monitoring.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Classify the antimalarial drugs Lumefantrine and Halofantrine according to their shared chemical subgroup.
back:
- Phenanthrene methanols.
- Note: Halofantrine use is limited by serious cardiac toxicity (QT prolongation).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The only available antimalarial agent that is active against the dormant hypnozoite stages of Plasmodium vivax and P ovale is [___].
back:
Primaquine
- Class: 8-aminoquinoline
- Primary Use: Radical cure of P vivax and P ovale
- High-Yield: Prevents relapses by targeting dormant liver forms

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from a region with known chloroquine-resistant P falciparum develops high-grade fever. Identify the preferred oral combination therapy in the USA for this uncomplicated infection.
back:
Malarone (Atovaquone-Proguanil)
- Alternative: Coartem (Artemether-Lumefantrine)
- Activity: Potent blood schizonticide
- High-Yield: Effective against multidrug-resistant strains

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which artemisinin and its analogs (e.g., artesunate) exert their rapidly acting blood schizonticidal effect.
back:
Free radical production
- Mechanism: Heme-mediated cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge
- Result: Reactive radicals damage parasite proteins and lipids
- Clinical: Fastest parasite clearance time among all antimalarials

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the gametocidal spectrum of Quinine with that of Primaquine.
back:
Gametocidal Activity
- Quinine: Active against P vivax and P ovale only
- Primaquine: Active against all species, including P falciparum
- Clinical Impact: Primaquine reduces the transmission reservoir to mosquitoes

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two specific enzymes inhibited by the synergistic combination of Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine (Fansidar).
back:
Folate Pathway Inhibition
- Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
- Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
- Mechanism: Sequential blockade of parasite folic acid synthesis

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: In the USA, the standard intravenous treatment for severe or complicated P falciparum infection when artesunate is unavailable is [___].
back:
Quinidine gluconate
- Requirement: Continuous ECG monitoring for QT prolongation
- Toxicity: Cinchonism and hypoglycemia
- Transition: Switch to oral agents once patient can swallow

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A 25-year-old male with P vivax malaria requires radical cure therapy. Which inherited genetic condition must be screened for before administering Primaquine to prevent severe hemolysis?
back:
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
- Pathophysiology: Primaquine causes oxidative stress to erythrocytes
- Consequence: Acute intravascular hemolysis
- Alternative: Chloroquine weekly for suppression if G6PD-deficient

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Detail how mutations in the PfCRT protein lead to high-level Chloroquine resistance in Plasmodium falciparum.
back:
Transporter-mediated efflux
- Mechanism: Mutant PfCRT transporter in the food vacuole membrane
- Action: Increases drug efflux from the vacuole
- Result: Prevents inhibition of heme biocrystallization into hemozoin

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the post-exposure prophylaxis duration required for Malarone versus Mefloquine after leaving an endemic area.
back:
Chemoprophylaxis Timing
- Malarone: 1 week (active against tissue stages)
- Mefloquine: 4 weeks (blood schizonticide only)
- High-Yield: Malarone allows shorter post-travel coverage

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the critical dietary instruction provided to patients taking the artemether-lumefantrine combination (Coartem).
back:
Administer with a fatty meal
- Rationale: Lumefantrine absorption is highly fat-dependent
- Impact: Significantly increases bioavailability and efficacy
- Contrast: Halofantrine should be taken without food to avoid toxicity

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Classify [___] as the only available antimalarial agent effectively active against the dormant hypnozoite stages of Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale.
back:
• Primaquine (8-aminoquinoline)
• It provides radical cure for relapsing malarias
• Also acts as a gametocide against all four human malaria species

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from the border areas of Thailand presents with fever. Given the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum in this region, which antibiotic is the preferred chemoprophylactic agent?
back:
• Doxycycline
• Inhibits protein synthesis in the plasmodial apicoplast
• Used as an alternative to mefloquine in high-resistance regions

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role of the iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge in the pharmacodynamics of Artemisinin derivatives.
back:
• Leading to the production of lethal free radicals
• Results in rapid blood schizonticidal activity
• Standard for treating both complicated and uncomplicated falciparum malaria

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic targets of Chloroquine with those of Primaquine regarding the Plasmodium life cycle.
back:
• Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide (kills erythrocytic stages); no effect on latent liver stages
• Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide (kills hepatic stages/hypnozoites); also gametocidal

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the chemical class of Mefloquine and its primary limitation in clinical use.
back:
• Class: Quinoline methanol
• Limitation: Serious neuropsychiatric toxicities (seizures, psychosis)
• Carries a black box warning for neurologic and psychiatric side effects

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The fixed-dose combination of [___] and Proguanil acts synergistically to disrupt mitochondrial electron transport and folate synthesis.
back:
• Atovaquone
• Commercially known as Malarone
• Used for both treatment and chemoprophylaxis of resistant P. falciparum

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient presents with severe P. falciparum malaria, manifested by lethargy and renal impairment. According to current WHO standards, what is the preferred parenteral treatment?
back:
• Intravenous Artesunate
• Superior to quinine in reducing mortality
• Followed by a full oral course of ACT (Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy)

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain how the combination of Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine achieves its antimalarial effect.
back:
• Blockade of sequential steps in the folate synthesis pathway
• Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
• Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the use of Lumefantrine with that of Quinidine in the management of falciparum malaria.
back:
• Lumefantrine: Oral use only; fixed combination with artemether (Coartem) for uncomplicated cases
• Quinidine: Intravenous use; reserved for severe cases under cardiac monitoring

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Name the primary 4-aminoquinoline drug used for prophylaxis in areas without resistant P. falciparum and its specific mechanism in the parasite vacuole.
back:
• Chloroquine
• Prevents biocrystallization of heme into non-toxic hemozoin
• Leads to accumulation of toxic free heme, killing the parasite

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The only antimalarial drug class that is reliably effective against the dormant hypnozoite stages of P. vivax and P. ovale is the [___].
back:
● 8-aminoquinolines (specifically Primaquine).
● Necessary for radical cure to prevent clinical relapses.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from a region with multidrug-resistant P. falciparum develops fever. If the physician prescribes a drug known to cause cinchonism (tinnitus and flushing), the likely agent is [___].
back:
● Quinine or Quinidine.
● Often used in combination with Doxycycline or Clindamycin for resistant strains.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the mechanism of action by which 4-aminoquinolines like chloroquine exert toxicity against malaria parasites within erythrocytes.
back:
● Concentrates in parasite food vacuoles.
● Prevents heme biocrystallization into non-toxic hemozoin.
● Results in buildup of toxic free heme, killing the parasite.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical application of Primaquine as a tissue schizonticide versus its role as a gametocide in P. falciparum control.
back:
● Tissue schizonticide: Eradicates dormant hepatic hypnozoites in P. vivax/ovale.
● Gametocide: Renders P. falciparum gametocytes noninfective to mosquitoes, decreasing community transmission.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two components of the standard first-line fixed-dose combination therapy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria currently approved in the USA.
back:
● Artemether and Lumefantrine (Coartem).
● Artemether is a rapid-acting artemisinin; Lumefantrine is a longer-acting aryl alcohol.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Artemisinins act as very rapidly acting [___] schizonticides, but have no effect on the hepatic stages of the parasite.
back:
● Blood.
● Includes artesunate, artemether, and dihydroartemisinin.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A 25-year-old male requires treatment for P. vivax. Before initiating the 8-aminoquinoline drug required for radical cure, which laboratory screening is mandatory to prevent drug-induced anemia?
back:
● G6PD (Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) level.
● Deficiency leads to severe hemolysis or methemoglobinemia with Primaquine use.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the chemical activation and subsequent effect of artemisinin derivatives like artesunate on plasmodia.
back:
● Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge within the parasite.
● Production of free radicals that damage parasite organelles and proteins.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the preferred agent for chloroquine-sensitive malaria with the standard of care for severe/complicated falciparum malaria.
back:
● Sensitive malaria: Chloroquine (oral).
● Severe malaria: Intravenous Artesunate (preferred over IV Quinidine/Quinine due to lower toxicity).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Which antimalarial drug, used for both weekly prophylaxis and treatment, carries an FDA black box warning regarding neurologic and psychiatric toxicities?
back:
● Mefloquine.
● Can cause seizures, confusion, or acute psychosis; avoided in patients with psychiatric history.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The primary antimalarial drug used to eradicate the dormant hepatic hypnozoite stages of *Plasmodium vivax* and *P. ovale* is [___].
back:
• Primaquine
• Classified as an 8-aminoquinoline tissue schizonticide.
• Essential for radical cure to prevent clinical relapse.
• Screening for G6PD deficiency is mandatory prior to initiation.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A 5-year-old returns from Nigeria with lethargy, high parasitemia, and renal impairment. Considering the diagnosis of severe *P. falciparum* malaria, the preferred intravenous treatment is [___].
back:
• Intravenous Artesunate
• An artemisinin derivative that is superior to quinine for survival.
• Rapidly kills all asexual erythrocytic stages.
• Must be followed by a full oral course of combination therapy.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Artemisinin-class drugs (e.g., artesunate) exert their rapid blood schizonticidal effect.
back:
• Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the drug's endoperoxide bridge occurs in the parasite.
• This reaction generates toxic free radicals.
• These radicals damage parasite membranes and proteins, causing rapid cell death.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical utility of Chloroquine with Quinine in the context of current *P. falciparum* drug resistance patterns.
back:
• Chloroquine: Use is severely limited by widespread PfCRT transporter mutations; used only in specific sensitive regions.
• Quinine: Remains effective against most chloroquine-resistant strains; used primarily for severe disease or in combination regimens.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Name the two components of the first-line artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) currently approved for use in the USA.
back:
• Artemether and Lumefantrine (Coartem)
• Artemether provides rapid initial parasite reduction.
• Lumefantrine is a long-acting blood schizonticide preventing recrudescence.
• Administer with fatty food to ensure adequate absorption.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Antimalarial agents that act by inhibiting the plasmodial enzyme dihydrofolate reductase include Pyrimethamine and [___].
back:
• Proguanil
• Often co-formulated with Atovaquone (as Malarone).
• Synergistically blocks sequential steps in the parasite folate synthesis pathway.
• Also possesses activity against some hepatic stages.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with severe malaria is treated with intravenous Quinidine gluconate. Which physiological parameter must be continuously monitored during infusion, and why?
back:
• Cardiac Rhythm (EKG) and Blood Pressure.
• Quinidine causes dose-related QT interval prolongation.
• High risk of dangerous arrhythmias and severe drug-induced hypotension.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the specific intracellular inhibitory mechanism of Chloroquine within the erythrocytic stage parasite.
back:
• Accumulates in the acidic parasite food vacuole.
• Prevents the conversion of toxic free heme into non-toxic hemozoin.
• Build-up of free heme causes oxidative damage and parasite lysis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between Tissue Schizonticides and Blood Schizonticides based on their target within the Plasmodium life cycle.
back:
• Tissue Schizonticides: Target developing or dormant liver forms (hypnozoites); prevent initial infection or relapse.
• Blood Schizonticides: Target asexual erythrocytic parasites; terminate clinical symptoms and clear parasitemia.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Classify Mefloquine into its chemical group and identify its primary high-yield clinical application for travelers.
back:
• Quinoline Methanol.
• Primary Use: Weekly chemoprophylaxis for travelers to chloroquine-resistant regions.
• Cation: Contraindicated in patients with a history of seizures or psychiatric disorders.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The class of antimalarials that includes Chloroquine and Amodiaquine, which primarily target asexual erythrocytic stages, is the [___].
back:
* Class: 4-Aminoquinolines
* Use: Functions as rapidly acting blood schizonticides
* Mechanism: Interferes with the biocrystallization of toxic heme into non-toxic hemozoin within parasite food vacuoles
* Spectrum: Primary treatment for sensitive P. falciparum and P. vivax

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from a region endemic for P. vivax is treated for the acute attack but requires therapy to prevent future relapses. The drug class indicated for this radical cure is the [___].
back:
* Class: 8-Aminoquinolines (e.g., Primaquine)
* Target: Specifically eliminates dormant hepatic hypnozoites of P. vivax and P. ovale
* Importance: Essential for radical cure to prevent late-onset relapses
* Contraindication: G6PD deficiency must be screened for to avoid severe hemolysis

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role of Blood Schizonticides like Chloroquine and Quinine upon intracellular parasite replication during a symptomatic malarial attack.
back:
* Physiological Impact: These agents target asexual erythrocytic stages to eliminate clinical symptoms like paroxysmal fever
* Therapeutic Goal: They prevent further host red blood cell destruction and resulting anemia
* Examples: Includes chloroquine, quinine, and rapidly acting artemisinin-based derivatives

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
coreConcept: Differential targets of Tissue vs Blood Schizonticides
front: Contrast Tissue Schizonticides and Blood Schizonticides regarding their specific roles in the management of symptomatic and latent malaria.
back:
* Tissue Schizonticides: Target pre-erythrocytic liver stages; provide causal prophylaxis or eradicate dormant hypnozoites (e.g., Primaquine)
* Blood Schizonticides: Target asexual erythrocytic parasites; resolve clinical illness and prevent morbidity (e.g., Chloroquine, Quinine)
* Requirement: Complete eradication requires targeting both stages

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the pharmacological components and the specific classification of the first-line ACT formulation known as Coartem.
back:
* Components: Consists of Artemether and Lumefantrine
* Strategy: Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT)
* Rational: Artemether clearance is rapid, while Lumefantrine prevents recrudescence due to its longer half-life
* Use: Standard first-line treatment for multidrug-resistant P. falciparum

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Antimalarials like Pyrimethamine and Proguanil belong to the [___] class and act by inhibiting the synthesis of tetrahydrofolate.
back:
* Classification: Antifolate drugs (Diaminopyrimidines and Biguanides)
* Enzymatic Target: Specifically inhibits the parasite enzyme dihydrofolate reductase
* Outcome: Prevents the conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate, halting DNA synthesis
* Synergy: Often combined with sulfonamides for enhanced metabolic blockade

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient presents with lethargy, high-grade fever, and 5% parasitemia on blood smear. Identify the rapidly acting class of drugs used as the preferred parenteral treatment.
back:
* Class: Sesquiterpene lactone endoperoxides (Artemisinins)
* Example: Intravenous Artesunate is the gold standard for severe disease
* Action: Most rapidly acting blood schizonticides available
* Advantage: Significantly reduces mortality compared to older quinoline-based parenteral therapies

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the sequential enzymatic blockade achieved by combining Sulfadoxine with Pyrimethamine in the treatment of resistant malaria.
back:
* Step 1: Sulfadoxine inhibits dihydropteroate synthase by competing with p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA)
* Step 2: Pyrimethamine subsequently inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
* Synergy: This sequential blockade effectively halts purine and nucleic acid synthesis
* Outcome: Provides enhanced killing in resistant strains

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between the clinical applications of 4-Aminoquinolines versus 8-Aminoquinolines in the context of lifecycle stage targeting.
back:
* 4-Aminoquinolines: Act as blood schizonticides; used to treat acute clinical malaria by targeting erythrocytic parasites (e.g., Chloroquine)
* 8-Aminoquinolines: Primarily act as tissue schizonticides; target liver stages to prevent relapses or provide causal prophylaxis (e.g., Primaquine)

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the chemical classification and primary clinical use of Quinine and Mefloquine.
back:
* Chemical Class: Quinoline Methanols
* Mechanism: Act as potent blood schizonticides against erythrocytic parasites
* Indications: Quinine is used for severe malaria; Mefloquine for prophylaxis and uncomplicated resistant P. falciparum
* Source: Quinine is traditionally derived from Cinchona bark

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The antimalarial drug chloroquine exerts its biocidal effect by interfering with the parasite's ability to sequester toxic free heme into a non-toxic polymer called [___].
back:
• Hemozoin
• By inhibiting heme polymerase, chloroquine causes the accumulation of free heme, which is toxic to the Plasmodium parasite.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A 24-year-old male treated for P. vivax malaria develops dark urine and sudden onset jaundice 48 hours after starting a new medication to prevent relapse. Identify the most likely drug and the underlying patient factor responsible.
back:
• Drug: Primaquine
• Patient Factor: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
• Primaquine induces oxidative stress, causing hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which artemisinin derivatives, such as artesunate, achieve rapid parasite clearance.
back:
• Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge
• This reaction generates toxic free radicals that damage parasite proteins and membranes.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the primary life-cycle stages targeted by Chloroquine versus Primaquine in the management of Plasmodium vivax.
back:
• Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide (targets erythrocytic stages to treat symptoms).
• Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide (targets hepatic hypnozoites to prevent relapses/radical cure).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the characteristic clinical constellation known as 'Cinchonism' associated with Quinine toxicity.
back:
• Tinnitus, headache, nausea, and dizziness
• Visual disturbances and flushing
• Severe cases may progress to cardiac arrhythmias and hypoglycemia.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The primary genetic mediator responsible for high-level resistance to chloroquine in Plasmodium falciparum is the [___] transporter mutation.
back:
• PfCRT (P. falciparum Chloroquine Resistance Transporter)
• Mutations in this transporter allow the parasite to efflux the drug from its food vacuole.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returns from a 3-week trip to Southeast Asia complaining of vivid nightmares, anxiety, and dizziness. He has been taking a weekly chemoprophylactic agent. Which drug is most likely responsible?
back:
• Mefloquine
• It is known for neuropsychiatric side effects, ranging from sleep disturbances to rare acute psychosis or seizures.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the biochemical synergy provided by the drug combination Malarone (Atovaquone and Proguanil).
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
• Proguanil: Enhances atovaquone's ability to collapse the mitochondrial membrane potential and inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the cardiotoxicity profiles of Halofantrine and Lumefantrine when used in Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT).
back:
• Halofantrine: Significant QT/PR prolongation; high risk of fatal arrhythmias.
• Lumefantrine: Minor, clinically insignificant QT prolongation; considered much safer for routine use.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the current World Health Organization (WHO) drug of choice for the treatment of severe or complicated falciparum malaria.
