back:
• Intravenous (IV) Artesunate
• It is superior to quinine/quinidine in reducing mortality and provides more rapid parasite clearance.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: In the pharmacological management of non-resistant *Plasmodium falciparum* and other species, the 4-aminoquinoline of choice for both treatment and prophylaxis is [___].
back:
• Chloroquine
• Mechanism: Blocks heme sequestration into non-toxic hemozoin crystals
• Potent blood schizonticide
• Ineffective against dormant liver stages (hypnozoites)

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A 28-year-old traveler with *Plasmodium vivax* malaria is treated with chloroquine. To prevent future relapses, a drug must be added to target the dormant liver stage known as the [___].
back:
• Hypnozoite
• Targeted by Primaquine (tissue schizonticide)
• Essential for "radical cure" of *P. vivax* and *P. ovale*
• Prevents clinical relapse from hepatic forms

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the distinct biochemical mechanism by which Artemisinins exert their rapid blood schizonticidal action compared to traditional quinolines.
back:
• Artemisinins: Produce toxic free radicals via endoperoxide bridge cleavage
• Quinolines: Prevent biocrystallization of toxic heme into hemozoin
• Artemisinins are the fastest-acting blood schizonticides available

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the preferred parenteral management of severe, complicated falciparum malaria with the historically used IV quinidine regarding efficacy and safety.
back:
• IV Artesunate: Current standard; superior survival rates and faster parasite clearance
• IV Quinidine: Historically used; requires continuous ECG monitoring for QT prolongation
• Artesunate is significantly less toxic than quinidine/quinine

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two specific enzymes inhibited by the combination of Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine (Fansidar) in the plasmodial folate synthesis pathway.
back:
• Dihydropteroate synthase: Inhibited by Sulfadoxine (sulfonamide)
• Dihydrofolate reductase: Inhibited by Pyrimethamine
• Sequential blockade results in synergistic interference with folate synthesis

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Before initiating therapy with [___], a drug essential for the radical cure of *P. vivax*, patients must be screened for G6PD deficiency to avoid drug-induced hemolysis.
back:
• Primaquine
• Class: 8-aminoquinoline
• Gametocidal against all four human malaria species
• Contraindicated in pregnancy due to fetal G6PD deficiency risk

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler heading to an area with chloroquine-resistant *P. falciparum* is prescribed a quinoline methanol for weekly prophylaxis. The drug most likely prescribed is [___].
back:
• Mefloquine
• Long terminal half-life (~20 days) allows weekly dosing
• Effective against many resistant strains
• Black box warning for potential neuropsychiatric toxicities

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the dual mechanism of action of the fixed-dose combination Malarone (Atovaquone plus Proguanil) against *Plasmodium* species.
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport (cytochrome bc1 complex)
• Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase via its metabolite cycloguanil
• Effective against both tissue and erythrocytic schizonts

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast "Tissue Schizonticides" with "Blood Schizonticides" regarding their target in the Plasmodium life cycle and clinical utility.
back:
• Tissue Schizonticides: Target liver stages (prophylaxis or radical cure); e.g., Primaquine
• Blood Schizonticides: Target erythrocytic stages to alleviate clinical symptoms; e.g., Chloroquine, Artemisinins
• Tissue stage drugs prevent initial blood infection or relapses

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Name two bacterial protein synthesis inhibitors commonly used as adjuncts to Quinine to enhance efficacy and shorten treatment duration for resistant falciparum malaria.
back:
• Doxycycline (Tetracycline) and Clindamycin (Lincosamide)
• Mechanism: Inhibit protein synthesis in the plasmodial apicoplast
• Act slowly; never used as monotherapy for malaria
• Useful for multidrug-resistant *P. falciparum*

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The only available antimalarial drug specifically effective against the dormant hypnozoite stages of *P. vivax* and *P. ovale* is [___].
back:
Primaquine.

*   An 8-aminoquinoline tissue schizonticide.
*   Essential for achieving "radical cure" to prevent relapses.
*   Also possesses significant gametocidal activity.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with *P. vivax* malaria is treated with chloroquine but develops dark urine and jaundice shortly after starting a second drug to prevent relapse. Identify the drug class and the likely genetic deficiency.
back:
8-Aminoquinolines (e.g., Primaquine).

*   Genetic Predisposition: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
*   Pathophysiology: Drug induces oxidative stress in RBCs leading to acute hemolysis.
*   Requirement: Must screen for G6PD status before prescribing.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role of the food vacuole in the mechanism of action of Chloroquine against sensitive Plasmodium species.
back:
Blocks heme biocrystallization.

*   Drug concentrates in the acidic parasite food vacuole.
*   Prevents the conversion of toxic free heme into non-toxic hemozoin.
*   Accumulated free heme elicits parasite toxicity and death.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical targets of 'Tissue Schizonticides' versus 'Blood Schizonticides' in the malarial life cycle.
back:
*   Tissue Schizonticides: Target developing or dormant (hypnozoite) liver forms; used for causal prophylaxis and radical cure.
*   Blood Schizonticides: Target asexual erythrocytic parasites; used to terminate clinical attacks and for suppressive prophylaxis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two distinct chemical classes and their pharmacological targets in the fixed-combination Malarone.
back:
Hydroxynaphthoquinone (Atovaquone) and Folate Antagonist (Proguanil).

*   Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
*   Proguanil: Inhibits plasmodial dihydrofolate reductase (via cycloguanil).
*   Use: Highly effective for both treatment and chemoprophylaxis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: To improve efficacy and limit the selection of resistant strains, the current international standard for uncomplicated *P. falciparum* malaria is [___].
back:
Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT).

*   Combines a rapid-acting artemisinin (Artesunate/Artemether) with a long-acting partner (Lumefantrine/Mefloquine).
*   Lumefantrine is used in the U.S. formulation (Coartem).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A lethargic child returns from Nigeria with *P. falciparum* parasitemia and renal dysfunction. Specify the preferred intravenous induction agent and its advantage over quinine.
back:
Intravenous Artesunate.

*   Advantage: Superior survival rates and faster parasite clearance.
*   Safety: Better tolerability than intravenous quinidine (no mandatory cardiac monitoring).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biological function of Proguanil and specify its active metabolite required for efficacy.
back:
Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.

*   Acts as a prodrug; must be converted to Cycloguanil.
*   Disrupts parasite DNA synthesis by inhibiting folate metabolism.
*   Active against both blood and liver stages.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast Quinine and Mefloquine regarding their clinical indications and primary route of administration.
back:
*   Quinine: Used orally (with antibiotics) for resistant infections or IV (as quinidine) for severe malaria.
*   Mefloquine: Oral only (irritating if parenteral); used for weekly chemoprophylaxis and treatment of resistant strains.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Classify the five major chemical groups of blood schizonticides used in malaria therapy.
back:
*   4-Aminoquinolines: Chloroquine, Amodiaquine.
*   Quinoline Methanols: Quinine, Mefloquine.
*   Artemisinin Derivatives: Artesunate, Artemether.
*   Phenanthrene Methanols: Halofantrine, Lumefantrine.
*   Antifolates: Pyrimethamine, Proguanil.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The only available antimalarial agent effective against the dormant hepatic hypnozoite stages of P. vivax and P. ovale is [___].
back: * Primaquine. * It is essential for radical cure and terminal prophylaxis. * Patients must be screened for G6PD deficiency before administration to avoid hemolysis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A 5-year-old traveler returning from Nigeria presents with lethargy, 103.6°F fever, and 1.5% P. falciparum parasitemia. Specify the preferred intravenous treatment.
back: * Intravenous Artesunate. * It is superior to intravenous quinine in survival rates and patient safety. * Acts rapidly as a blood schizonticide against all human malaria species.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Chloroquine exerts its blood schizonticidal effect within the parasite food vacuole.
back: * Prevents the biocrystallization of hemoglobin breakdown products (heme) into non-toxic hemozoin. * Results in the buildup of free heme, which is toxic to the parasite.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the chemoprophylactic administration schedules of Malarone (atovaquone-proguanil) and Mefloquine regarding duration required after leaving an endemic area.
back: * Malarone: Taken daily; discontinued 1 week after travel as it targets tissue schizonts. * Mefloquine: Taken weekly; must continue for 4 weeks post-travel due to lack of liver-stage activity.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Why are artemisinins typically administered in combination with longer-acting partner drugs (ACTs) rather than as monotherapy?
back: * To prevent the selection of artemisinin-resistant parasites. * To compensate for the very short half-lives of artemisinin derivatives. * To ensure total clearance and prevent clinical recrudescence.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The constellation of symptoms including tinnitus, headache, and visual disturbances commonly associated with therapeutic doses of Quinine is known as [___].
back: * Cinchonism. * Usually mild and does not warrant discontinuation unless symptoms become severe. * High doses can also lead to hypoglycemia or cardiac arrhythmias.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. vivax malaria requires radical cure but has a history of severe jaundice after eating fava beans. Identify the drug that must be avoided.
back: * Primaquine. * Causes acute hemolytic anemia in individuals with G6PD deficiency. * Patients of Mediterranean or Asian descent have the highest risk for severe deficiency.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the synergistic mechanism of action of the Fansidar combination (Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine) against P. falciparum.
back: * Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase. * Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase. * Result: Sequential blockade of the folic acid pathway necessary for DNA synthesis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between Lumefantrine and Halofantrine regarding their cardiac safety profile and dietary administration requirements.
back: * Lumefantrine: Safe profile with no dangerous arrhythmias; must be taken with fatty food. * Halofantrine: Serious risk of fatal arrhythmias/QT prolongation; food increases absorption to toxic levels.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the specific role of Doxycycline when used for the treatment of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum infection.
back: * Acts as a slow blood schizonticide by inhibiting protein synthesis in the apicoplast. * Used with Quinine to allow a shorter, better-tolerated course of Quinine.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Primaquine is the primary antimalarial classified as a tissue schizonticide used to target the dormant hepatic [___] stage of P. vivax and P. ovale.
back:
* Hypnozoite
* Eradication prevents clinical relapse of these species.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A 5-year-old traveler returning from Nigeria presents with lethargy, fever, and P. falciparum at 1.5% parasitemia. Identify the most appropriate first-line oral combination therapy for this uncomplicated resistant infection.
back:
* Coartem (Artemether-Lumefantrine)
* Alternative: Malarone (Atovaquone-Proguanil)

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role and mechanism of Artemisinin derivatives in the treatment of malaria.
back:
* Rapidly acting blood schizonticides against all species.
* Mechanism: Production of toxic free radicals following iron-catalyzed cleavage of the drug's endoperoxide bridge.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical role of "causal prophylactic" drugs with standard "blood schizonticides" in malaria prevention.
back:
* Causal Prophylactics: Kill parasites in the liver before they reach the blood (e.g., Malarone).
* Blood Schizonticides: Prevent clinical disease by killing parasites after they enter erythrocytes (e.g., Chloroquine, Mefloquine).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Assign Chloroquine to its chemical class and define its primary parasitic target stage.
back:
* Class: 4-Aminoquinoline
* Target: Blood schizonticide (effective against asexual erythrocytic stages).

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: The fixed combination Malarone consists of the hydroxynaphthoquinone [___] and the folate antagonist Proguanil.
back:
* Atovaquone
* Synergistic action disrupts mitochondrial electron transport and folate synthesis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient requiring radical cure for P. vivax develops acute hemolysis after starting a new medication. Identify the most likely drug and the underlying patient factor.
back:
* Drug: Primaquine
* Factor: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which 4-aminoquinolines like Chloroquine achieve parasite toxicity.
back:
* Accumulate in parasite food vacuoles.
* Prevent the biocrystallization of hemoglobin breakdown products (heme) into non-toxic hemozoin.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the spectrum of gametocidal activity between Quinine and Primaquine.
back:
* Quinine: Gametocidal only against P. vivax and P. ovale.
* Primaquine: Gametocidal against all four human malaria species, including P. falciparum.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the three main subclasses of quinoline-derived antimalarials and provide one example for each.
back:
* 4-Aminoquinolines: Chloroquine
* Quinoline Methanols: Mefloquine or Quinine
* 8-Aminoquinolines: Primaquine

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Antimalarial drugs that primarily target the asexual erythrocytic stage to alleviate clinical symptoms are functionally classified as [___].
back:
• Blood schizonticides.
• Key examples include Chloroquine, Quinine, Mefloquine, and Artemisinin derivatives.
• These drugs are essential for treating symptomatic clinical illness.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. vivax is treated with chloroquine but returns weeks later with a relapse. This occurs because chloroquine lacks activity against [___] stages in the liver.
back:
• Hypnozoites.
• Radical cure requires adding Primaquine, an 8-aminoquinoline.
• Primaquine is the only drug active against these dormant hepatic forms in P. vivax and P. ovale.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role of Chloroquine within the parasite food vacuole regarding heme metabolism.
back:
• Prevents the biocrystallization of toxic heme into non-toxic hemozoin.
• Causes the buildup of free heme, which is toxic to the parasite.
• This leads to membrane damage and parasite death.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the gametocidal spectrum of Quinine with that of Primaquine.
back:
• Quinine: Active against P. vivax and P. ovale gametocytes, but NOT P. falciparum.
• Primaquine: Potent gametocide against all human malaria species, including P. falciparum, preventing transmission to mosquitoes.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: List the two components of the fixed combination Malarone and their respective pharmacological mechanisms.
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport in plasmodia.
• Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (folate antagonist).
• Used for both treatment and chemoprophylaxis of resistant P. falciparum.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Quinine and Mefloquine belong to the [___] chemical class of antimalarial agents.
back:
• Quinoline methanols.
• Both are rapidly acting blood schizonticides.
• Primarily used to treat resistant P. falciparum infections.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returns from Africa with lethargy and a high parasite load of P. falciparum. Following current WHO standards, identify the preferred chemical class for initial rapid parasite clearance.
back:
• Artemisinins (e.g., IV Artesunate).
• Sesquiterpene lactone endoperoxides.
• Mechanism involves production of free radicals in the parasite food vacuole.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biological rationale for using Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT) over artemisinin monotherapy.
back:
• Artemisinins: Extremely fast-acting but have very short half-lives.
• Partner Drugs (e.g., Lumefantrine): Provide a long-acting "tail" to eliminate residual parasites.
• Prevents high recrudescence rates and delays drug resistance.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between the target sites of Pyrimethamine and Sulfadoxine in the parasite's metabolic pathway.
back:
• Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Together, they provide sequential blockade of folate synthesis.

category: Classify antimalarial drugs
front: Which group of antibiotics are utilized as adjunct blood schizonticides to treat resistant P. falciparum by targeting the plasmodial apicoplast?
back:
• Tetracyclines (e.g., Doxycycline) and Clindamycin.
• Act slowly against erythrocytic stages.
• Always used in combination with fast-acting agents like Quinine.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine prevents the biocrystallization of the hemoglobin breakdown product [___] into hemozoin, leading to parasite toxicity through the accumulation of free radicals.
back:
• Heme
• Free heme is toxic to the parasite food vacuole.
• Acts primarily as a blood schizonticide.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient treated for P. vivax malaria develops dark urine and back pain shortly after starting radical cure therapy. The biochemical mechanism of this reaction involves oxidative stress in cells deficient in [___].
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD)
• Primaquine causes hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients.
• Screening for G6PD status is mandatory before therapy.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical activation and resulting mechanism of action of Artemisinin derivatives (e.g., Artesunate).
back:
• Activation: Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge.
• Action: Production of toxic free radicals that damage parasite proteins.
• Result: Very rapid-acting blood schizonticidal activity.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the characteristic acute toxicity of Quinine (Cinchonism) with the long-term toxicity seen with Chloroquine.
back:
• Quinine (Cinchonism): Tinnitus, headache, nausea, and visual disturbances.
• Chloroquine (Long-term): Irreversible retinopathy, ototoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary neuropsychiatric contraindications and the FDA black box warning associated with Mefloquine.
back:
• Contraindications: History of epilepsy or psychiatric disorders.
• Black Box: Seizures, acute psychosis, depression, and hallucinations.
• Also avoided in cardiac conduction defects.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Resistance of P. falciparum to chloroquine is primarily mediated by mutations in a putative food-vacuole transporter protein called [___].
back:
• PfCRT (P. falciparum Chloroquine Resistance Transporter).
• Mutations lead to increased efflux of the drug from the food vacuole.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A child with severe P. falciparum infection presents with lethargy and high parasitemia. Identify the first-line intravenous drug of choice and its common late-onset adverse effect.
back:
• Drug: Intravenous Artesunate.
• Adverse Effect: Delayed hemolysis (typically 2–3 weeks post-treatment).
• Superior survival rates compared to IV Quinine.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: How does the combination of Atovaquone and Proguanil (Malarone) achieve its synergistic antimalarial effect?
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
• Proguanil (Cycloguanil): Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR).
• Combination acts against tissue and erythrocytic schizonts.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between the specific stages of Plasmodium targeted by Primaquine versus Chloroquine in the context of 'radical cure' for P. vivax.
back:
• Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide; eliminates asexual erythrocytic parasites (resolves symptoms).
• Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide; eliminates dormant liver hypnozoites (prevents relapses).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Name the two specific plasmodial enzymes inhibited by the combination of Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine (Fansidar).
back:
• Sulfadoxine: Dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS).
• Pyrimethamine: Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR).
• Sequential blockade of the folic acid pathway.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine exerts its antimalarial effect by concentrating in the parasite's acidic food vacuole and preventing the biocrystallization of toxic heme into [___].
back:
• Hemozoin
• Prevents the detoxification of reactive metabolic byproducts
• Results in parasite membrane damage and death due to free heme toxicity

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient treated for Plasmodium vivax malaria develops dark urine and a significant drop in hemoglobin on day 3 of therapy. The drug responsible for this oxidative hemolysis acts specifically on the [___] stage of the parasite.
back:
• Hypnozoite (dormant liver stage)
• Drug: Primaquine
• Toxicity: Oxidative stress in G6PD-deficient erythrocytes
• Essential for radical cure of P. vivax and P. ovale

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical activation and resulting cytotoxic mechanism of Artemisinin derivatives (e.g., Artesunate) within the Plasmodium parasite.
back:
• Activation: Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge
• Mechanism: Generation of toxic free radicals
• Target: Alkylation and damage of parasite proteins/lipids
• Role: Rapid clearance of high-density parasitemia

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the primary clinical indications and the most significant "black box" toxicities associated with Quinine versus Mefloquine.
back:
• Quinine: Used for severe/complicated malaria; causes cinchonism and hypoglycemia.
• Mefloquine: Used for prophylaxis; causes serious neuropsychiatric effects (psychosis, seizures).
• Both can alter cardiac conduction (QT prolongation).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the specific gene mutation and the resulting physiological change that mediates high-level resistance to Chloroquine in Plasmodium falciparum.
back:
• PfCRT gene mutation
• Encodes an altered transporter protein in the food vacuole membrane
• Mechanism: Increases efflux of the drug away from its target site

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: In the first-line combination therapy Coartem, the component [___] provides a long half-life to prevent recrudescence, while artemether ensures rapid initial parasite clearance.
back:
• Lumefantrine
• Aryl alcohol with a half-life of 3-4 days
• Prevents relapse by killing residual parasites surviving the artemether burst
• Must be taken with fatty food

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A pregnant woman being treated for severe malaria with intravenous Quinidine develops sudden confusion and diaphoresis despite improving parasitemia. This metabolic adverse effect is caused by [___].
back:
• Hyperinsulinemia (Drug-induced hypoglycemia)
• Mechanism: Quinine/Quinidine stimulates pancreatic beta cells to release insulin
• Requires continuous glucose monitoring, especially in severe cases and pregnancy

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from the Thai-Cambodian border presents with fever; blood smear confirms multidrug-resistant P. falciparum. Explain the selection of Atovaquone-Proguanil over Chloroquine based on biochemical targets.
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport (cytochrome bc1 complex)
• Proguanil: Synergistically collapses mitochondrial membrane potential
• Effective against PfCRT-mutated strains that efflux quinolines

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between the therapeutic roles of a "Blood Schizonticide" and a "Tissue Schizonticide" in the context of achieving a radical cure for Plasmodium vivax.
back:
• Blood Schizonticides (e.g., Chloroquine): Kill asexual erythrocytic stages to stop clinical illness.
• Tissue Schizonticides (e.g., Primaquine): Eradicate dormant liver hypnozoites to prevent future clinical relapses.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two parasite enzymes inhibited by the Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (Fansidar) combination and the metabolic pathway they disrupt.
back:
• Enzymes: Dihydropteroate synthase (Sulfadoxine) and Dihydrofolate reductase (Pyrimethamine)
• Pathway: Sequential blockade of Folic Acid Synthesis
• Disrupts production of purines and DNA synthesis

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine exerts its primary antimalarial effect by concentrating in the parasite's food vacuole and preventing the biocrystallization of [___] into hemozoin.
back:
• Toxic free heme
• Chloroquine binds to heme, preventing its conversion to non-toxic hemozoin, leading to oxidative damage and parasite death.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient treated for P. vivax malaria develops dark urine and jaundice. Microscopic examination of blood reveals Heinz bodies. Explain the pathophysiology of this drug reaction.
back:
• Primaquine-induced oxidative stress.
• In G6PD-deficient patients, primaquine causes depletion of glutathione, leading to hemoglobin oxidation and acute hemolytic anemia.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain how the iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge determines the biological activity of Artemisinin derivatives.
back:
• It generates highly reactive free radicals.
• These radicals damage parasite membranes and proteins within the erythrocytic stage.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the standard intravenous management of severe P. falciparum malaria with the oral management of uncomplicated multidrug-resistant strains in the USA.
back:
• Severe: Intravenous Artesunate (preferred) or Quinidine gluconate.
• Uncomplicated: Artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem) or Atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the synergistic metabolic blockade achieved by the combination of Sulfadoxine and Pyrimethamine (Fansidar).
back:
• Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Result: Sequential inhibition of the plasmodial folate synthesis pathway.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A clinical constellation of tinnitus, headache, dizziness, and visual disturbances resulting from therapeutic doses of cinchona alkaloids is termed [___].
back:
• Cinchonism
• It is a dose-related adverse effect specific to Quinine and Quinidine therapy.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. vivax is successfully cleared of erythrocytic parasites with Chloroquine but relapses three months later. Identify the specific parasite stage and the drug required to prevent this.
back:
• Stage: Hepatic hypnozoites.
• Required Drug: Primaquine (Tissue schizonticide).
• Chloroquine lacks activity against the dormant liver stages.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the primary molecular mechanism of resistance utilized by P. falciparum against Chloroquine.
back:
• Mutations in the PfCRT gene.
• This results in a mutant transporter that effuxes chloroquine out of the parasite food vacuole.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast Atovaquone and Proguanil in terms of their target site within the parasite's biochemical pathways.
back:
• Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport (cytochrome bc1 complex).
• Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (via its active metabolite cycloguanil).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Which antimalarial agent is uniquely contraindicated in patients with a history of epilepsy or psychiatric disorders due to potential neuropsychiatric toxicity?
back:
• Mefloquine
• It is associated with severe adverse effects like seizures, psychosis, and hallucinations.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine acts against susceptible plasmodia by concentrating in the parasite food vacuole and preventing the conversion of toxic heme into [___].
back:
• Hemozoin.
• This inhibits biocrystallization of hemoglobin breakdown products.
• The resulting buildup of free heme is toxic to the parasite.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from a region endemic for P. vivax is prescribed a drug for radical cure. Two days later, he develops dark urine and jaundice. The most likely underlying biochemical defect is [___].
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
• Oxidant stress from Primaquine induces hemolysis in these patients.
• Testing for G6PD status is mandatory before drug initiation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which artemisinin derivatives like artesunate exert their rapid antimalarial effect.
back:
• Production of free radicals.
• Triggered by the iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge.
• Results in irreversible damage to parasite proteins and membranes.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the primary clinical indications and safety profiles of Chloroquine versus Mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis.
back:
• Chloroquine: Used in sensitive regions (e.g., Hispaniola); generally safe in pregnancy and children.
• Mefloquine: Used in resistant regions; contraindicated in patients with psychiatric or cardiac conduction disorders.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: List the characteristic cluster of symptoms known as 'cinchonism' associated with therapeutic doses of Quinine.
back:
• Tinnitus and impaired hearing.
• Headache and dizziness.
• Nausea and flushing.
• Blurred vision or other visual disturbances.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The antimalarial drug [___] acts by disrupting mitochondrial electron transport and is highly effective for prophylaxis in chloroquine-resistant areas when combined with proguanil.
back:
• Atovaquone.
• Formulated as Malarone (with proguanil).
• Targets both tissue and erythrocytic schizonts.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. falciparum malaria presents with altered mental status and hyperparasitemia. Identify the preferred intravenous treatment and its primary advantage over IV quinidine.
back:
• Intravenous Artesunate.
• Superior survival rates in severe malaria.
• Significantly better safety profile with less risk of cardiotoxicity or hypoglycemia.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the unique pharmacological target of Doxycycline when utilized as an adjunct agent in the treatment of multidrug-resistant malaria.
back:
• Inhibition of protein synthesis in the apicoplast.
• This is a plasmodial prokaryote-like organelle.
• Acts slowly; must be combined with a fast-acting blood schizonticide like Quinine.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Distinguish between the specific parasitic stages targeted by Chloroquine and Primaquine in the management of Plasmodium vivax.
back:
• Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide; kills erythrocytic forms to terminate clinical illness.
• Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide; eradicates dormant hepatic hypnozoites to prevent relapse (radical cure).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary molecular mediator of resistance to Chloroquine in Plasmodium falciparum.
back:
• Mutations in the PfCRT (P. falciparum chloroquine resistance transporter) gene.
• This transporter is located in the parasite food vacuole membrane.
• Results in decreased drug accumulation at the site of action.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine exerts its antimalarial effect by concentrating in parasite food vacuoles and preventing the biocrystallization of [___] into non-toxic hemozoin.
back:
• Heme.
• This leads to a buildup of free heme which is toxic to the parasite.
• It specifically targets the erythrocytic (blood) stage of infection.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from an endemic region for P. vivax is prescribed Primaquine for radical cure. Two days later, he presents with dark, tea-colored urine and jaundice. This reaction most likely suggests a deficiency in [___].
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD).
• Primaquine causes oxidative stress leading to hemolysis in deficient patients.
• Mandatory screening for G6PD levels is required before clinical use.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical role of the endoperoxide bridge in the mechanism of action of Artemisinin derivatives like Artesunate.
back:
• The bridge is cleaved by parasite-derived iron.
• Cleavage generates highly reactive free radicals.
• These radicals damage parasite proteins and membranes, leading to rapid cell death.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical use of IV Artesunate versus IV Quinidine in the management of severe or complicated falciparum malaria.
back:
• IV Artesunate: Current standard of care; superior survival rates and better tolerability profile.
• IV Quinidine: Alternative choice; requires continuous cardiac monitoring due to risk of QT prolongation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary neuropsychiatric toxicities that led to the FDA 'black box' warning for Mefloquine.
back:
• Severe depression, anxiety, and psychosis.
• Hallucinations and suicidal ideation.
• Seizures.
• Contraindicated in patients with active or history of psychiatric disorders.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Malarone, a common prophylactic and therapeutic agent, achieves its synergistic effect through the combination of Proguanil and [___].
back:
• Atovaquone.
• Atovaquone disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
• Proguanil acts as a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A pregnant woman in her first trimester requires treatment for uncomplicated chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum. According to WHO guidelines, the preferred regimen is [___].
back:
• Quinine plus Clindamycin.
• Quinine is considered safe throughout pregnancy.
• Clindamycin is added to shorten the treatment course and limit quinine toxicity.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe how the combination drug Fansidar (Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine) inhibits the synthesis of essential parasite precursors.
back:
• Sulfadoxine inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Pyrimethamine inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• This results in sequential blockade of the folic acid synthesis pathway.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic role of Primaquine versus Chloroquine regarding the 'Radical Cure' of P. vivax and P. ovale.
back:
• Chloroquine: Acts as a blood schizonticide; eliminates erythrocytic stages but fails to prevent relapse.
• Primaquine: Acts as a tissue schizonticide; eradicates dormant hepatic hypnozoites to prevent future relapses.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: What molecular modification in P. falciparum is primarily responsible for resistance to Chloroquine?
back:
• Mutations in the PfCRT gene.
• Encodes a transporter that effluxes Chloroquine out of the parasite's food vacuole.
• Prevents drug accumulation at the target site.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine acts by inhibiting the parasite's biocrystallization process, thereby preventing the conversion of toxic free heme into the insoluble pigment [___].
back:
● Hemozoin
● This leads to the accumulation of toxic heme levels within the parasite food vacuole, causing cell death.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A 24-year-old traveler returning from a P. vivax endemic area develops jaundice and dark urine after starting a drug to prevent relapse. Blood smear reveals Heinz bodies. Identify the underlying enzyme deficiency and the drug class involved.
back:
● Enzyme: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
● Drug: 8-aminoquinoline (Primaquine)
● Pathophysiology: Primaquine-induced oxidative stress leads to acute hemolysis in deficient individuals.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the role of the endoperoxide bridge in the antimalarial activity of the artemisinin class (e.g., Artesunate).
back:
● Cleaved by intraparasitic iron/heme.
● Generates highly reactive free radicals.
● Radicals damage parasite proteins and membranes, providing rapid blood schizonticidal action.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A missionary on IV Quinidine for severe malaria requires monitoring for hypoglycemia, whereas a pilot on Mefloquine prophylaxis reports vivid hallucinations. Contrast the specific monitoring and contraindications required for these drugs.
back:
● Quinidine: Requires ECG (QT prolongation) and blood glucose (insulin-induced hypoglycemia) monitoring.
● Mefloquine: Contraindicated in patients with epilepsy or psychiatric disorders; requires monitoring for neuropsychiatric toxicity.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the significance of co-administering Lumefantrine with fatty meals.
back:
● Significantly increases oral bioavailability (up to 16-fold).
● Lumefantrine is highly lipophilic; adequate absorption is essential to prevent treatment failure in ACT regimens.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The only antimalarial agent capable of preventing relapses by targeting the dormant [___] stage of P. vivax and P. ovale is Primaquine.
back:
● Hypnozoite
● It is used for 'radical cure' to eliminate hepatic reservoirs after treating the acute erythrocytic infection.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler to the Southeast Asian border regions (Thailand/Cambodia) requires malaria prophylaxis. Identify the preferred agent in this region where mefloquine resistance is prevalent.
back:
● Doxycycline
● Rationale: High prevalence of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum in these border regions makes mefloquine or chloroquine unreliable.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the cellular mechanism of action of Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (Fansidar) synergy against malaria parasites.
back:
● Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
● Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
● Synergy: Causes sequential blockade of the folate synthesis pathway required for DNA production.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the physiological effects of Quinine and Mefloquine on pancreatic beta-cell function.
back:
● Quinine: Potent stimulator of insulin release, frequently leading to severe hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.
● Mefloquine: Lacks significant effect on insulin secretion; hypoglycemia is not a typical adverse effect.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: List the classic clinical components of the 'cinchonism' symptom complex associated with Quinine toxicity.
back:
● Tinnitus (most common)
● Visual disturbances (blurred vision/impaired hearing)
● Headache
● Dizziness and nausea

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine inhibits the biocrystallization of heme into [___], causing toxic buildup of free heme within the parasite food vacuole.
back:
• Hemozoin
• Prevents the conversion of toxic hemoglobin breakdown products
• Leads to oxidative damage and parasite death
• Only active against blood-stage schizonts

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler with P. vivax malaria is treated with chloroquine. To prevent relapse, a second drug is added, but the patient develops dark urine and jaundice. This second drug targets [___].
back:
• Liver-stage hypnozoites
• Drug: Primaquine
• Pathophysiology: Causes oxidative stress resulting in acute hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals
• Radical cure requirement for P. vivax and P. ovale

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biocatalytic step required for the antimalarial activity of the artemisinin class.
back:
• Cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge
• Catalyzed by heme-iron within the parasite food vacuole
• Results in the generation of toxic free radicals
• Radicals damage parasite proteins and membranes

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the gametocidal activity of Quinine with that of Primaquine.
back:
• Quinine: Gametocidal against P. vivax and P. ovale; NOT active against mature P. falciparum gametocytes.
• Primaquine: Active against gametocytes of all four human malaria species, including P. falciparum.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary psychiatric risk and corresponding 'Black Box Warning' associated with the use of Mefloquine.
back:
• Neuropsychiatric toxicities
• Includes anxiety, depression, hallucinations, and seizures
• Warning: Contraindicated in patients with active or history of psychiatric disorders or epilepsy

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The synergistic combination Malarone works by disrupting plasmodial [___] and inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase.
back:
• Mitochondrial electron transport
• Components: Atovaquone (transport inhibitor) and Proguanil (DHFR inhibitor)
• Effective for both prophylaxis and treatment of resistant P. falciparum

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. falciparum presents with 12% parasitemia and confusion. State the standard of care drug and the required route of administration.
back:
• Drug: Artesunate
• Route: Intravenous (IV)
• Indication: Severe or complicated malaria
• Note: Superior survival rates compared to IV Quinidine/Quinine

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which Plasmodium falciparum develops high-level resistance to chloroquine.
back:
• Mutations in the PfCRT gene
• Encodes a transporter in the food vacuole membrane
• Results in increased efflux of chloroquine away from its target
• Lowers drug concentration at site of heme accumulation

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic targets of Lumefantrine and Primaquine.
back:
• Lumefantrine: A blood schizonticide; kills erythrocytic parasites to treat acute clinical illness.
• Primaquine: A tissue schizonticide; targets dormant hypnozoites in the liver to prevent relapse.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: List the hallmark symptoms of 'Cinchonism' frequently associated with Quinine therapy.
back:
• Tinnitus and hearing impairment
• Headache and dizziness
• Nausea and visual disturbances (blurring)
• Occurs at therapeutic doses; usually reversible upon discontinuation

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine exerts its antimalarial effect by preventing the biocrystallization of the hemoglobin breakdown product heme into [___], causing toxic heme buildup in parasite vacuoles.
back:
* Hemozoin
* Prevents heme detoxification within the plasmodium
* Results in the accumulation of free heme, which is toxic to the parasite

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A 25-year-old traveler returns from Nigeria with high-grade fever, lethargy, and a Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia of 6%. According to WHO guidelines for severe malaria, the drug of choice is [___].
back:
* Intravenous Artesunate
* Superior survival benefit compared to intravenous quinine/quinidine
* Followed by a full oral course of artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT)

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the role of the endoperoxide bridge in the biological activation of Artemisinins against malaria parasites.
back:
* Bridge is cleaved by iron (from heme) in the parasite vacuole
* Produces toxic free radicals
* Rapidly kills asexual erythrocytic stages and reduces parasite biomass

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast Primaquine with Chloroquine regarding their ability to prevent relapse in Plasmodium vivax infections.
back:
* Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide; eliminates dormant liver hypnozoites to prevent relapse.
* Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide; kills erythrocytic forms but cannot touch hypnozoites.
* Radical cure requires both agents.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Name the primary molecular transporter responsible for Chloroquine resistance in Plasmodium falciparum and state its physiological effect.
back:
* PfCRT (P. falciparum Chloroquine Resistance Transporter)
* Functions by pumping chloroquine out of the parasite food vacuole
* Decreases drug concentration at the target site

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The characteristic adverse effect syndrome of Quinine, manifesting as tinnitus, reversible hearing loss, headache, and blurred vision, is termed [___].
back:
* Cinchonism
* Result of therapeutic or toxic doses of cinchona alkaloids
* Usually resolves upon discontinuation of the drug

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: An African-American male treated with Primaquine for P. vivax develops jaundice, dark urine, and a sharp decline in hemoglobin. Explain the underlying pathophysiology.
back:
* Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
* Primaquine induces oxidative stress in RBCs
* Lack of glutathione leads to hemoglobin denaturing and acute hemolysis

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the mechanism by which the combination drug Fansidar (Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine) achieves synergistic antimalarial activity.
back:
* Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase
* Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
* Blocks sequential steps in the folate synthesis pathway required for DNA replication

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the cardiac adverse effects of Halofantrine with the newer agent Lumefantrine when used to treat multidrug-resistant malaria.
back:
* Halofantrine: Causes dangerous, dose-related QT/PR prolongation and arrhythmias.
* Lumefantrine: Minor, clinically insignificant QT effects; much higher safety profile.
* Lumefantrine is always co-formulated with artemether (Coartem).

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary neuropsychiatric contraindications for Mefloquine when prescribed for malaria prophylaxis.
back:
* History of epilepsy or seizures
* History of psychiatric illness (psychosis, severe depression)
* Significant cardiac conduction defects

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine primarily acts by concentrating in the parasite's food vacuole and preventing the biocrystallization of the hemoglobin breakdown product [___] into non-toxic hemozoin.
back:
• Heme (ferriprotoporphyrin IX)
• Accumulation of free heme is toxic to the parasite
• Leads to oxidative damage and membrane lysis
• Only effective against erythrocytic stages

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A 24-year-old male traveler with Plasmodium vivax is started on a 14-day course of therapy. Three days later, he presents with dark urine, jaundice, and sudden-onset anemia. Identify the drug and the host deficiency.
back:
• Drug: Primaquine
• Deficiency: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
• Pathophysiology: Oxidative stress causes denaturation of hemoglobin and acute hemolysis

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism of action of Artemisinin derivatives (e.g., Artesunate) against Plasmodium falciparum.
back:
• Heme-iron catalyzes the cleavage of the drug's endoperoxide bridge
• Produces highly reactive carbon-centered free radicals
• These radicals alkylate and damage parasite proteins and membranes

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast Chloroquine and Mefloquine regarding their specific roles in the chemoprophylaxis of malaria based on resistance patterns.
back:
• Chloroquine: Reserved for areas with sensitive parasites (e.g., Central America west of Panama)
• Mefloquine: Recommended for regions with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum
• Dosing: Both are administered once weekly

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Define the syndrome known as 'Cinchonism' and list the triad of symptoms characteristic of early Quinine toxicity.
back:
• Toxic syndrome caused by cinchona alkaloids
• Symptom Triad: Tinnitus (ringing in ears), headache, and dizziness
• Often accompanied by nausea and visual disturbances

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The primary molecular mechanism of resistance to Chloroquine in Plasmodium falciparum involves mutations in a putative transporter protein called [___].
back:
• PfCRT (P. falciparum Chloroquine Resistance Transporter)
• Enhances efflux of the drug from the acidic food vacuole
• Prevents therapeutic drug accumulation at the site of action

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient presents with lethargy, high-grade fever, and 5% parasitemia with P. falciparum. According to WHO guidelines, what is the parenteral drug of choice for this condition?
back:
• Intravenous Artesunate
• Superior to quinine/quinidine in reducing mortality
• Preferred for severe or complicated malaria in all trimesters of pregnancy

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical pathway inhibited by Proguanil after it is converted into its active metabolite.
back:
• Active metabolite: Cycloguanil
• Inhibits bifunctional dihydrofolate reductase-thymidylate synthase
• Disrupts DNA synthesis by halting folate-dependent deoxythymidylate production

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the cardiac safety profiles of Halofantrine and Lumefantrine during the treatment of falciparum malaria.
back:
• Halofantrine: Causes significant, dose-related QT/PR prolongation and dangerous arrhythmias
• Lumefantrine: Lacks significant cardiac toxicity; considered much safer in fixed-dose combinations (e.g., Coartem)

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the only drug class capable of achieving a 'radical cure' by targeting the dormant liver hypnozoites of P. vivax and P. ovale.
back:
• 8-Aminoquinolines (e.g., Primaquine, Tafenoquine)
• Eradicates the extra-erythrocytic dormant stage
• Necessary to prevent clinical relapses of these specific species

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine exerts its antimalarial effect by concentrating in the parasite's food vacuole and inhibiting the biocrystallization of toxic heme into [___].
back:
* Hemozoin.
* The buildup of free heme is lethal to the plasmodium parasite.
* Primary drug for non-resistant species like P. malariae.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient treated for P. vivax malaria develops dark urine, jaundice, and sudden anemia. Laboratory findings confirm hemolysis. This reaction most likely resulted from [___] therapy in the setting of G6PD deficiency.
back:
* Primaquine.
* It induces oxidative stress in RBCs, leading to hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients.
* Screening for G6PD is mandatory before initiation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which artemisinin derivatives like artesunate induce rapid parasite death.
back:
* Cleavage of the drug's endoperoxide bridge by iron in the parasite.
* Production of lethal free radicals that damage parasite proteins.
* Potent activity against blood-stage schizonts.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: In a case of severe, complicated P. falciparum malaria, contrast the clinical preferences between intravenous artesunate and intravenous quinidine.
back:
* Artesunate: Current global standard; superior survival rates and better safety profile.
* Quinidine: Alternative used in USA; requires cardiac monitoring due to QT prolongation and risk of hypoglycemia.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the primary molecular mechanism utilized by Plasmodium falciparum to develop resistance against chloroquine.
back:
* Mutations in the PfCRT (Chloroquine Resistance Transporter) gene.
* Results in increased efflux of the drug from the parasite's food vacuole, preventing heme-hemozoin inhibition.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: The constellation of symptoms including tinnitus, headache, nausea, and visual disturbances resulting from quinine toxicity is known as [___].
back:
* Cinchonism.
* Caused by the cinchona alkaloid properties of quinine.
* Mild symptoms usually do not require drug discontinuation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler with a history of epilepsy and depression requires malaria prophylaxis. Why is Mefloquine contraindicated in this patient?
back:
* High risk of neuropsychiatric side effects, including seizures and psychosis.
* May exacerbate clinical depression.
* Doxycycline or Malarone are safer alternatives for this patient.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the synergistic biochemical pathway inhibited by the Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (Fansidar) combination.
back:
* Sequential blockade of plasmodial folic acid synthesis.
* Sulfadoxine: Competes with PABA to inhibit dihydropteroate synthase.
* Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
* Starves parasite of tetrahydrofolate needed for DNA synthesis.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the clinical roles of Chloroquine and Primaquine in the management of Plasmodium vivax infection.
back:
* Chloroquine: Blood schizonticide; treats active erythrocytic infection and resolves clinical symptoms.
* Primaquine: Tissue schizonticide; targets liver hypnozoites to provide a 'radical cure' and prevent relapse.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the two active components of Malarone and their respective cellular targets.
back:
* Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport.
* Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
* Effective for both prophylaxis and treatment of resistant P. falciparum.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine exerts its antimalarial effect by concentrating in parasite food vacuoles and preventing the biocrystallization of [___] into hemozoin.
back:
* Heme (ferriprotoporphyrin IX)
* Built-up free heme is highly toxic to Plasmodium species.
* The drug specifically disrupts heme detoxification, leading to parasite cell death.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A traveler returning from Thailand with P. falciparum malaria is treated with Quinine. He suddenly develops tinnitus, deafness, and visual disturbances. Identify the name of this toxic syndrome.
back:
* Cinchonism
* Classic cluster of auditory and visual toxicities from quinine/quinidine.
* Symptoms are usually dose-related and typically resolve upon drug discontinuation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the physiological rationale for performing a G6PD screen before initiating Primaquine therapy.
back:
* Primaquine induces oxidative stress within erythrocytes.
* G6PD-deficient patients cannot maintain reduced glutathione to buffer oxidative species.
* Resultant oxidative damage causes acute hemolytic anemia and Heinz body formation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the preferred oral treatment for uncomplicated chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum in a woman during her 1st trimester versus the 2nd trimester.
back:
* 1st Trimester: Quinine plus Clindamycin is the standard recommendation.
* 2nd/3rd Trimester: Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) are preferred.
* Severe malaria requires IV Artesunate regardless of the trimester.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the specific molecular change in the Plasmodium falciparum PfCRT protein that primarily mediates high-level resistance to chloroquine.
back:
* Point mutations in the PfCRT gene (P. falciparum Chloroquine Resistance Transporter).
* Mutated transporters actively pump chloroquine out of the parasite food vacuole.
* This prevents the drug from reaching toxic concentrations at its site of action.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: To achieve a 'radical cure' in Plasmodium vivax or ovale infections, [___] must be administered to eliminate the dormant hepatic hypnozoites.
back:
* Primaquine
* Hypnozoites are the dormant liver forms responsible for malaria relapse.
* Standard blood schizonticides (e.g., chloroquine) do not eradicate this hepatic stage.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. falciparum malaria is treated with intravenous artesunate. Two weeks after completion of therapy, his hemoglobin drops significantly with evidence of hemolysis. Identify the most likely drug-induced phenomenon.
back:
* Post-artemisinin delayed hemolysis.
* Occurs in approximately 13% of severe cases treated with IV artemisinins.
* Typically manifests 2–3 weeks post-treatment and may require blood transfusion.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the distinct mitochondrial mechanism by which Atovaquone inhibits plasmodial growth compared to its partner drug Proguanil in the Malarone combination.
back:
* Atovaquone: Disrupts the mitochondrial electron transport chain at the cytochrome bc1 complex.
* Proguanil: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) via its active metabolite, cycloguanil.
* Synergism prevents both parasite energy production and DNA synthesis.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the specific enzymes in the folate synthesis pathway targeted by Sulfadoxine versus Pyrimethamine in the Fansidar combination.
back:
* Sulfadoxine: Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS).
* Pyrimethamine: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR).
* Sequential blockade provides synergistic antimalarial activity against susceptible strains.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Specify the unique chemical functional group in artemisinins that is cleaved by parasite iron to produce lethal free radicals.
back:
* Endoperoxide bridge.
* Cleavage by intra-parasitic heme-iron generates toxic free radicals.
* These radicals cause rapid macromolecular damage to parasite membranes and proteins.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Chloroquine disrupts the detoxification of [___], leading to the accumulation of toxic ferriprotoporphyrin IX in Plasmodium species.
back: • Heme • Chloroquine prevents its conversion into non-toxic hemozoin within the food vacuole • The buildup of free heme is highly toxic to the parasite, leading to cell death.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient with P. vivax develops hemolytic anemia and dark urine shortly after starting Primaquine. Identify the underlying biochemical deficiency in the host.
back: • Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency • Primaquine metabolites cause oxidative stress to red blood cells • Without G6PD, RBCs cannot generate enough NADPH to neutralize oxidative damage, leading to hemolysis.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Explain the cellular mechanism by which Artemisinin analogs (e.g., Artesunate) exert their rapidly fungicidal effects against Plasmodium.
back: • Production of free radicals • Follows iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge in the drug molecule • These radicals damage parasite membranes and proteins through alkylation.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the mortality outcomes and primary adverse effects of intravenous Artesunate versus intravenous Quinidine for the treatment of severe malaria.
back: • Efficacy: Artesunate significantly reduces mortality and clears parasites faster than quinidine • Safety: Artesunate lacks the dangerous cardiotoxicity (QT prolongation) and hypoglycemia seen with quinidine therapy.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Identify the neuropsychiatric contraindications that mandate avoiding the use of Mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis.
back: • History of epilepsy or seizure disorders • History of major psychiatric disorders (e.g., depression, anxiety, psychosis) • It should also be avoided in patients with cardiac conduction defects.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: High-level resistance to chloroquine in P. falciparum is primarily mediated by point mutations in the [___] gene.
back: • PfCRT (P. falciparum Chloroquine Resistance Transporter) • The mutation facilitates the efflux of chloroquine from the parasite food vacuole • This prevents the drug from reaching toxic concentrations at its site of action.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: A patient treated with oral Quinine for resistant malaria develops tinnitus, nausea, and blurred vision. Identify this clinical syndrome and its associated metabolic complication.
back: • Cinchonism • Hypoglycemia • Quinine stimulates pancreatic beta cells to release insulin, requiring close glucose monitoring in severe cases.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Describe the distinct synergistic targets of the Atovaquone and Proguanil components in the Malarone formulation.
back: • Atovaquone: Disrupts mitochondrial electron transport (cytochrome bc1 complex) • Proguanil: Inhibits parasite dihydrofolate reductase (folate synthesis) • This combination is effective against both tissue and erythrocytic schizonts.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Contrast the dietary instructions for a patient taking Lumefantrine (in Coartem) versus a patient taking Halofantrine.
back: • Lumefantrine: Must be taken with high-fat food to ensure adequate absorption and efficacy • Halofantrine: Taken on an empty stomach because food-increased absorption drastically raises the risk of lethal arrhythmias.

category: Describe the mechanism of action and mechanism of resistance, clinical uses, adverse effects of Antimalarial drugs
front: Define the therapeutic role of 'radical cure' in the management of P. vivax and P. ovale infections.
back: • Elimination of dormant liver stages (hypnozoites) • Requires the use of Primaquine • Standard blood schizonticides (like chloroquine) alone cannot prevent relapses originating from these hepatic reservoirs.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The primary mechanism of [___] involves its chemical reduction in anaerobic cells to form reactive intermediates that bind to and disrupt bacterial DNA.
back:
• Metronidazole
• Also applies to Tinidazole
• Effective against tissue trophozoites in amoebiasis and giardiasis.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A 30-year-old traveler with East African sleeping sickness (T. brucei rhodesiense) is diagnosed with CNS involvement. Identify the first-line trivalent arsenical drug for this stage and its most lethal side effect.
back:
• Drug: Melarsoprol
• Side Effect: Fatal reactive encephalopathy (5–10% of patients)
• Mechanism: Likely due to disruption of trypanosomes in the CNS.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the essential ECG monitoring required for a patient receiving Sodium Stibogluconate for visceral leishmaniasis.
back:
• Monitor for T-wave changes
• Check for QT interval prolongation
• Discontinue if dangerous arrhythmias develop
• Toxicity increases over the 28-day course.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the clinical application and CNS penetration of Suramin with those of Eflornithine in African Trypanosomiasis.
back:
• Suramin: Used for early hemolymphatic stage; does not enter CNS.
• Eflornithine: First-line for advanced West African (T.b. gambiense) CNS disease; achieves good CNS levels.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: State the therapeutic advantage and the major contraindication for the use of Miltefosine in leishmaniasis.
back:
• Advantage: First effective oral drug for visceral leishmaniasis.
• Contraindication: Pregnancy (highly teratogenic; avoid for 2 months post-treatment).

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: To achieve a radical cure in asymptomatic Entamoeba histolytica carriers in non-endemic areas, a [___] amebicide such as paromomycin or iodoquinol must be used.
back:
• Luminal amebicide
• Kills cysts in the bowel lumen
• Prevents transmission and future invasive disease.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with Giardiasis takes a single dose of Tinidazole. That evening, after drinking one beer, they experience severe flushing, tachycardia, and vomiting. Identify the drug-induced reaction.
back:
• Disulfiram-like reaction
• Inhibition of aldehyde dehydrogenase
• Common to nitroimidazoles (Metronidazole/Tinidazole).

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the role of intravenous Pentamidine in treating African Trypanosomiasis and its primary limiting metabolic toxicity.
back:
• Role: First-line for early hemolymphatic West African sleeping sickness (T.b. gambiense).
• Toxicity: Pancreatic toxicity causing initial severe hypoglycemia followed by potential permanent diabetes.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the treatment protocols for American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) using Nifurtimox versus Benznidazole.
back:
• Nifurtimox: Administered for 60-90 days; often limited by GI/neurologic toxicity.
• Benznidazole: Often preferred; 60-day course; limited by severe dermatitis (rash in 30%) and peripheral neuropathy.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Name the specific aminoglycoside that is used both as an oral luminal amebicide and as a parenteral treatment for visceral leishmaniasis.
back:
• Paromomycin
• Oral: For intestinal amebiasis/giardiasis.
• Parenteral: Effective alternative for visceral leishmaniasis in India/Africa.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Benzimidazole drugs such as albendazole and mebendazole act against nematodes primarily by inhibiting [___].
back:
• Microtubule synthesis
• This leads to disruption of the parasite's cellular structure and metabolic processes.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A patient being treated for neurocysticercosis with praziquantel develops a sudden onset of headache and meningismus. Explain the pathophysiology behind these symptoms.
back:
• Symptoms are caused by inflammatory reactions around dying parasites
• It is not due to direct drug toxicity
