• Eflornithine: First-line for advanced *T.b. gambiense* (West Africa); safer toxicity profile.
• Melarsoprol: Used for advanced *T.b. rhodesiense* (East Africa); highly toxic with 5-10% risk of reactive encephalopathy.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Why is strict contraception required during and for at least two months after completing treatment with Miltefosine?
back:
• The drug is highly teratogenic.
• Its long half-life necessitates a significant washout period before pregnancy.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The oral nitroimidazole derivative considered the first-line alternative to Nifurtimox for the treatment of acute American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) is [___].
back: • Benznidazole

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with severe intestinal amoebiasis failing standard therapy is administered Emetine. The clinician must monitor for dose-limiting toxicity in the [___] system.
back:
• Cardiovascular system
• Major risks include cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and severe hypotension.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the metabolic mechanism behind the severe hypoglycemia observed in patients treated with Pentamidine.
back:
• Pentamidine causes inappropriate, rapid insulin release from the pancreas.
• This often manifests 5-7 days into treatment.
• May be followed by pancreatitis or permanent diabetes.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast Tinidazole with Metronidazole regarding their pharmacokinetics and standard dosing regimens in giardiasis.
back:
• Tinidazole has a longer half-life (12-14 hrs vs 7.5 hrs).
• It permits once-daily or single-dose regimens.
• Generally exhibits better gastrointestinal tolerability.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: State the primary clinical indication for Diloxanide Furoate in the treatment of amoebiasis.
back:
• Asymptomatic intestinal (luminal) infection.
• Used to eradicate carriage or following tissue amebicide therapy.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: In patients with hepatic insufficiency, the dose of [___] must be adjusted because it is primarily metabolized by the liver, despite its high bioavailability and excellent penetration into the CSF.
back:
• Metronidazole
• Undergoes oxidation and glucuronidation in the liver
• Metabolites may accumulate in patients with severe hepatic dysfunction

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A 40-year-old immigrant from South America presents with cardiomegaly and megacolon. Serology confirms *Trypanosoma cruzi*. The primary oral drug used to target the acute phase of this condition is [___].
back:
• Benznidazole (or Nifurtimox)
• Used to eliminate parasites in acute Chagas disease
• Side effects: Rash, peripheral neuropathy, and myelosuppression

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain why Miltefosine represents a major therapeutic shift in the clinical management of Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in endemic regions like India.
back:
• First effective **oral** agent for Visceral Leishmaniasis
• Replaces painful, toxic parenteral pentavalent antimonials
• Effective against antimonial-resistant strains

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetic half-lives and resulting dosing frequency of Metronidazole versus Tinidazole in the treatment of Giardiasis.
back:
• **Metronidazole:** Half-life ~7.5 hours; requires three daily doses for 5 days
• **Tinidazole:** Half-life ~12–14 hours; allows for effective **single-dose** therapy (2g)

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Identify the biphasic glycemic toxicity characteristic of parenteral Pentamidine administration and its underlying mechanism.
back:
• **Initial Hypoglycemia:** Caused by inappropriate insulin release due to pancreatic islet cell damage
• **Subsequent Hyperglycemia:** Can lead to permanent insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The halogenated hydroxyquinoline [___] is an effective luminal amebicide, but its use is limited by the risk of severe neurotoxicity known as Subacute Myelo-Optic Neuropathy (SMON).
back:
• Iodoquinol (Diiodohydroxyquin)
• Can cause permanent optic atrophy and vision loss
• Should be taken with meals to reduce GI upset

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A female patient with confirmed *Trichomonas vaginalis* fails to respond to a standard course of Metronidazole. Specify the preferred alternative drug and its primary clinical advantage in this scenario.
back:
• **Tinidazole**
• Shows cross-activity against many metronidazole-resistant strains
• Features a superior toxicity profile and simpler dosing

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Describe the specific role of Leucovorin (Folinic acid) when using high-dose Pyrimethamine for the treatment of Toxoplasmosis in immunocompromised patients.
back:
• Acts as a **nutritional rescue** for host cells
• Bypasses the inhibited Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR) enzyme
• Specifically prevents drug-induced bone marrow suppression (pancytopenia)

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the administration and toxicity of Emetine with Metronidazole in the management of severe amebic liver abscess.
back:
• **Metronidazole:** Oral/IV route; low toxicity; drug of choice
• **Emetine:** SC/IM route only; highly cardiotoxic (arrhythmias, heart failure); reserve drug

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Describe the metabolic processing of Diloxanide Furoate that occurs within the human gastrointestinal tract after oral ingestion.
back:
• Splits into **diloxanide** and **furoic acid**
• 90% of diloxanide is absorbed and conjugated
• **Unabsorbed diloxanide** remains in the gut as the active amebicide

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The primary drug for extraluminal amebiasis, [___], acts by being nonenzymatically reduced by parasite ferredoxin to form toxic intermediates that disrupt DNA.
back:
• Metronidazole (or Tinidazole)
• Selective for anaerobic protozoa/bacteria
• Reduction products accumulate only in anaerobic cells
• Causes DNA strand breakage and instability

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A 28-year-old patient presents with foul-smelling, fatty stools and bloating after drinking stream water. Identify the nitroimidazole that offers the advantage of a single-dose 2 g regimen for this condition.
back:
• Tinidazole
• Used for Giardiasis and Trichomoniasis
• Longer half-life (12–14 hours) than Metronidazole
• Avoid alcohol due to disulfiram-like reaction

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the essential biochemical step that Pentavalent Antimonials (e.g., Sodium stibogluconate) must undergo within the host to achieve leishmanicidal activity.
back:
• Reduction to the trivalent state (Sb3+)
• Occurs within macrophages or the parasite
• Inhibits parasite glycolysis and fatty acid oxidation
• Standard therapy for visceral and cutaneous leishmaniasis

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the route of administration and primary clinical application of oral Paromomycin versus its parenteral formulation in protozoal therapy.
back:
• Oral: Non-absorbed aminoglycoside used as a luminal amebicide for intestinal amebiasis.
• Parenteral: Used systemically for the treatment of visceral leishmaniasis.
• Acts by inhibiting protein synthesis

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Which specific organ-system toxicity is the most significant limiting factor for the use of Pentamidine in treating West African Sleeping Sickness?
back:
• Pancreatic toxicity
• Causes inappropriate insulin release (hypoglycemia)
• May follow with secondary hyperglycemia/diabetes
• Also associated with reversible renal insufficiency

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The luminal amebicide [___] is a halogenated hydroxyquinoline that must be used with caution due to the risk of severe neurotoxicity and optic atrophy with prolonged use.
back:
• Iodoquinol
• Effective against intestinal trophozoites and cysts
• Contraindicated in patients with iodine intolerance
• Taken with meals to limit GI toxicity

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with acute American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) is started on Benznidazole. Identify the most frequent adverse reaction that occurs in approximately 30% of patients.
back:
• Skin rash (maculopapular)
• Usually reversible upon discontinuation
• Other effects include peripheral neuropathy and GI symptoms
• Suboptimal efficacy in the chronic disease stage

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Describe how Diloxanide furoate is processed in the gastrointestinal tract to exert its effect against *Entamoeba histolytica* cysts.
back:
• Splits into diloxanide and furoic acid in the gut
• 90% of diloxanide is absorbed and conjugated
• The unabsorbed 10% is the active substance
• Acts strictly as a luminal amebicide

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
coreConcept: Differential Toxicity of Trypanocidals and Antimonials
front: Contrast the primary adverse effects of Nifurtimox and Sodium stibogluconate during long-term antiprotozoal therapy.
back:
• Nifurtimox: GI distress, restlessness, insomnia, and seizures.
• Sodium stibogluconate: Myalgia, arthralgia, and ECG changes (QT prolongation).
• Both require careful monitoring during long courses

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Which macrolide antibiotic is specifically utilized to treat primary toxoplasmosis in pregnant women to reduce the risk of congenital transmission?
back:
• Spiramycin
• Concentrates in the placenta
• Used only for first-trimester/maternal infection
• Does not reliably cross the placenta to treat the fetus

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The first-line drug for the treatment of American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) that is administered orally for 60 days and is generally better tolerated than nifurtimox is [___].
back:
• Benznidazole
• Acts by reductive activation and DNA damage
• Most common side effect is skin rash

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient receiving Sodium Stibogluconate for visceral leishmaniasis develops T-wave inversion and prolonged QT interval on an electrocardiogram. Describe the appropriate clinical management.
back:
• Monitor ECG closely
• Discontinue or reduce dose if dangerous arrhythmias occur
• Cardiotoxicity is dose-dependent and typically reversible

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the mechanistic difference between Sodium Stibogluconate and Miltefosine in the treatment of Visceral Leishmaniasis.
back:
• Sodium Stibogluconate: Pentavalent antimonial; inhibits parasite glycolysis and bioenergetics
• Miltefosine: Alkylphosphocholine analog; interferes with phospholipid metabolism and induces apoptosis

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient presents with T. brucei rhodesiense (East African Sleeping Sickness). Contrast the pharmacological treatment if the disease is in the hemolymphatic stage versus the CNS stage.
back:
• Hemolymphatic Stage: Suramin (does not cross BBB)
• CNS Stage: Melarsoprol (trivalent arsenical; crosses BBB)
• Pentamidine is inferior for rhodesiense early stage

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: State the primary contraindication for Miltefosine and the required duration of contraceptive use following treatment.
back:
• Contraindication: Pregnancy (highly teratogenic)
• Contraception: Women must avoid pregnancy for 2 to 5 months after the 28-day course

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The oral drug used in India as a 28-day course for visceral leishmaniasis, representing the first effective oral agent for this disease, is [___].
back:
• Miltefosine
• Effective against resistant strains in India
• Adverse effects include vomiting and diarrhea

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with advanced West African Sleeping Sickness is treated with Melarsoprol. Describe the presentation and etiology of the most serious immediate adverse reaction.
back:
• Reactive Encephalopathy
• presentation: Cerebral edema, seizures, and coma
• etiology: Rapid disruption of trypanosomes in the CNS

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism by which Nifurtimox selectively targets Trypanosoma cruzi.
back:
• Intracellular reduction produces toxic free radicals
• T. cruzi is deficient in protective catalase and peroxidase
• Results in oxidative damage to parasite structures

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the terminal elimination half-life and primary excretion route of Suramin with those of Pentamidine.
back:
• Suramin: Half-life ~50 days; slow renal excretion
• Pentamidine: Half-life ~12 days; persists in tissues (liver/kidney) for months

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Specify the primary risk to the central nervous system associated with the use of the luminal amebicide Iodoquinol.
back:
• Neurotoxicity (Subacute Myelo-optic Neuropathy)
• Characterized by optic atrophy and permanent vision loss
• Occurs with prolonged use or high doses

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Benzimidazole drugs like albendazole and mebendazole exert their primary anti-helmintic effect by inhibiting [___] synthesis.
back:
* Microtubule
* This disrupts the parasite's structural integrity and glucose uptake, leading to death.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 30-year-old shepherd presents with a large, fluid-filled hepatic cyst on ultrasound. Serology is positive for Echinococcus granulosus. Identify the first-line medical therapy and its active metabolite.
back:
* Drug: Albendazole
* Active Metabolite: Albendazole sulfoxide
* It is often used as an adjunct to surgery or PAIR procedure.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Ivermectin induces paralysis in nematodes such as Strongyloides stercoralis.
back:
* It intensifies γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated transmission of signals in peripheral nerves.
* This results in the neuromuscular paralysis and expulsion of the parasite.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the drug of choice for Schistosoma haematobium with the specific organophosphate alternative that acts as a cholinesterase inhibitor.
back:
* Drug of Choice: Praziquantel (increases calcium permeability).
* Alternative: Metrifonate (only active against S. haematobium; ineffective against S. mansoni/japonicum).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the drug of choice for Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness) and its primary limitation regarding the parasite life cycle.
back:
* Drug: Ivermectin.
* Limitation: It is microfilaricidal only; it does not effectively kill the adult (macrofilaria) worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Praziquantel induces paralysis and dislodgement in trematodes and cestodes by increasing the cell membrane's permeability to [___].
back:
* Calcium ions (Ca²⁺)
* This causes strong muscular contraction and subsequent spastic paralysis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 6-year-old child presents with intense perianal pruritus at night. Tape test confirms Enterobius vermicularis. Identify a non-benzimidazole over-the-counter option and its mechanism.
back:
* Drug: Pyrantel pamoate.
* Mechanism: Neuromuscular blocking agent that causes release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase, resulting in worm paralysis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: How does Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) facilitate the destruction of microfilariae in Wuchereria bancrofti infections?
back:
* It immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure.
* This renders the parasites more susceptible to the host's own immune defense mechanisms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical application of Paromomycin in intestinal infections versus its parenteral use in protozoal disease.
back:
* Intestinal: Used as a luminal amebicide for E. histolytica (not absorbed).
* Parenteral: Used to treat visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the specific second-line agent for most tapeworm infections (T. saginata, T. solium) that acts by inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation.
back:
* Niclosamide
* It is effective only against the adult worms in the lumen, not against eggs or cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The antihelminthic drug [___] is classified as a benzimidazole carbamate and is the primary treatment for both hydatid disease and neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Albendazole
• Inhibits microtubule synthesis
• Broad-spectrum coverage against intestinal nematodes and larval cestodes (tapeworms).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with Strongyloides stercoralis infection is prescribed a macrocyclic lactone. Identify the drug and its primary physiological effect on the parasite.
back:
• Ivermectin
• Paralysis of nematodes via intensification of GABA-mediated signal transmission in peripheral nerves
• Also drug of choice for Onchocerca volvulus.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of action of Praziquantel against trematodes (flukes) and cestodes (tapeworms).
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium ions
• Results in spastic paralysis and detachment from host tissues
• Ultimately leads to parasite death and expulsion.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic application of Albendazole with Mebendazole in the context of tissue-dwelling versus intraluminal parasites.
back:
• Albendazole: Better absorption with fatty meals; active sulfoxide metabolite penetrates tissues (Hydatid cysts, neurocysticercosis)
• Mebendazole: Low absorption (<10%); primarily used for intraluminal nematodes (Ascariasis, Pinworm).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary clinical indication for Diethylcarbamazine and its effect on microfilariae.
back:
• Lymphatic filariasis and Loiasis
• Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structures
• Facilitates host immune system destruction of the parasite.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent that causes the release of [___], leading to the spastic paralysis of intestinal nematodes.
back:
• Acetylcholine
• Also inhibits cholinesterase
• Highly effective against Pinworms, Ascaris, and Hookworms within the bowel lumen.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with River Blindness (Onchocerca volvulus). State the drug of choice and whether it possesses macrofilaricidal or microfilaricidal activity.
back:
• Ivermectin
• Primarily microfilaricidal
• Does not effectively kill adult (macro) worms but blocks release of microfilariae for several months.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe how the antibiotic Doxycycline exerts a therapeutic effect in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis caused by W. bancrofti.
back:
• Indirectly kills the parasite by targeting Wolbachia
• Wolbachia is an intracellular bacterial symbiont required for filarial survival
• Results in sterility and death of adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the mechanisms by which Niclosamide and Praziquantel target adult tapeworms (Cestodes).
back:
• Niclosamide: Inhibits oxidative phosphorylation/ATPase activity in the worm
• Praziquantel: Induces calcium-mediated spastic paralysis
• Niclosamide is a second-line agent for Taenia species.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Name the primary drug of choice for all species of Schistosomiasis (bilharziasis) including S. mansoni and S. haematobium.
back:
• Praziquantel
• Safe and effective as a single oral dose
• Used extensively in mass treatment programs for disease control.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of action for benzimidazoles like Albendazole involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis in helminths.
back:
• Inhibits microtubule synthesis
• Binds to parasite β-tubulin
• Prevents polymerization of tubulin dimers

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 25-year-old patient presents with perianal itching, and a scotch tape test confirms Enterobius vermicularis. Identify the two primary drug classes used for first-line treatment.
back:
• Benzimidazoles (e.g., Mebendazole, Albendazole)
• Tetrahydropyrimidines (e.g., Pyrantel pamoate)
• Dose is typically repeated in 2 weeks

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Ivermectin carries out its biological function to induce paralysis in nematodes.
back:
• Intensifies GABA-mediated signal transmission
• Binds to glutamate-gated chloride channels
• Causes hyperpolarization and tonic paralysis of muscles

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic targets of Praziquantel with those of Diethylcarbamazine regarding the classification of helminths they treat.
back:
• Praziquantel: Cestodes (tapeworms) and Trematodes (flukes)
• Diethylcarbamazine: Filarial nematodes (W. bancrofti, Loa loa)
• Praziquantel acts on calcium channels; DEC immobilizes microfilariae

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the drug of choice for the radical cure of Strongyloides stercoralis and Onchocerca volvulus.
back:
• Ivermectin
• Microfilaricidal in onchocerciasis
• Standard for strongyloidiasis to prevent hyperinfection syndrome

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Praziquantel acts by increasing the permeability of the parasite's cell membrane to [___], leading to persistent contraction and paralysis.
back:
• Calcium ions (Ca2+)
• Results in tegumental damage and vacuolization
• Causes parasite dislodgement from host tissues

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient from a sheep-farming region presents with a large, fluid-filled hepatic cyst. If Echinococcus granulosus is suspected, name the first-line benzimidazole and the necessary dietary instruction.
back:
• Albendazole
• Take with a high-fat meal to increase systemic absorption
• Often used as an adjunct to surgical aspiration

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain how Doxycycline carries out its indirect antihelminthic biological function in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis.
back:
• Targets Wolbachia (intracellular bacterial symbiont)
• Depletion of bacteria leads to sterility of adult worms
• Exhibits macrofilaricidal activity against W. bancrofti

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the physiological effect of Pyrantel pamoate with that of Piperazine on the helminth neuromuscular system.
back:
• Pyrantel pamoate: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker; induces spastic paralysis via ACh release
• Piperazine: GABA agonist; induces flaccid paralysis by hyperpolarizing the muscle

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the specific anti-trematode drug used as the primary alternative to Praziquantel for Fasciola hepatica (sheep liver fluke) infections.
back:
• Bithionol
• Alternative: Triclabendazole
• Praziquantel is notably ineffective against Fasciola species

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The drug of choice for the medical management of hydatid disease (Echinococcus granulosus) and symptomatic neurocysticercosis is [___].
back:
Albendazole.
* Acts by inhibiting microtubule synthesis.
* Requires a fatty meal to enhance absorption for tissue infections.
* Metabolized to active albendazole sulfoxide.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with a disseminated threadworm infection (Strongyloides stercoralis). Identify the drug of choice and its primary physiological effect on the parasite.
back:
Ivermectin.
* Intensifies GABA-mediated transmission of signals in peripheral nerves.
* Leads to nematode paralysis and death.
* Avoid in patients taking other GABA-enhancing drugs.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of calcium permeability in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against Schistosomes.
back:
Praziquantel increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
* Results in strong muscle contraction and tegumental damage.
* Causes parasite paralysis and dislodgement from tissue.
* Followed by parasite death and expulsion.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic preference between Albendazole and Mebendazole in the treatment of tissue-based versus strictly intraluminal helminthic infections.
back:
* Albendazole: Preferred for tissue infections (e.g., Hydatid cysts, neurocysticercosis) due to active metabolites and superior tissue penetration.
* Mebendazole: Primarily used for intraluminal intestinal nematodes due to very low (<10%) systemic absorption.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary clinical indication for Diethylcarbamazine and its effect on microfilariae.
back:
Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) and Loiasis.
* Rapidly kills microfilariae.
* Displaces them from tissues, making them susceptible to host immune destruction.
* Slower activity against adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate acts as a [___] blocking agent that induces persistent activation of nicotinic receptors, resulting in spastic paralysis of intestinal worms.
back:
Neuromuscular.
* Causes release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase.
* Effective against pinworms and roundworms.
* Acts primarily within the intestinal lumen.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with multiple parenchymal brain cysts due to Taenia solium is started on Albendazole. Which adjunctive medication is necessary to prevent neurological deterioration?
back:
Corticosteroids (e.g., Dexamethasone).
* Reduces inflammation triggered by the immune response to dying larvae.
* Prevents cerebral edema and seizures.
* Note: Steroids increase albendazole plasma levels.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the unique indirect macrofilaricidal mechanism of Doxycycline in the treatment of Wuchereria bancrofti.
back:
Doxycycline kills Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial symbiont essential for the worm's fertility and survival.
* Depletion of bacteria leads to sterility and eventual death of adult filarial worms.
* Represents a novel target in filariasis control.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the standard therapy for Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm) with the therapy for standard Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm).
back:
* Hymenolepis nana: Praziquantel is the drug of choice; requires a higher dose or repeat course due to the internal autoinfection cycle.
* Taenia saginata: Praziquantel or Niclosamide (alternative); single dose is usually curative.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: List the four primary intestinal nematodes that are broadly susceptible to the benzimidazole drug class.
back:
* Ascaris lumbricoides (Roundworm)
* Trichuris trichiura (Whipworm)
* Necator americanus/Ancylostoma duodenale (Hookworms)
* Enterobius vermicularis (Pinworm)

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The benzimidazole class of anthelmintics, including albendazole and mebendazole, exerts its primary effect by inhibiting [___] synthesis in nematodes.
back:
• Microtubule.
• Prevents polymerization of tubulin.
• Impairs glucose uptake and motility.
• Leads to gradual parasite death and expulsion.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with intense pruritus, skin thickening, and ocular lesions (Onchocerciasis). The first-line microfilaricidal agent for this condition is [___].
back:
• Ivermectin.
• Drug of choice for Onchocerca volvulus.
• Also first-line for Strongyloides stercoralis.
• Acts by intensifying GABA-mediated neurotransmission.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of Praziquantel in inducing paralysis within schistosomes and cestodes.
back:
• Increases calcium permeability.
• Causes rapid influx of calcium ions into parasite cells.
• Leads to immediate muscular contraction and spastic paralysis.
• Exposes parasite antigens to host immune destruction.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the neuromuscular effects of Pyrantel pamoate with those of Piperazine in the treatment of Ascaris lumbricoides.
back:
• Spastic vs. Flaccid paralysis.
• Pyrantel: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker; induces spastic paralysis via acetylcholine release.
• Piperazine: GABA agonist; induces flaccid paralysis by blocking acetylcholine at myoneural junctions.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the two primary clinical indications for Albendazole in tissue-invasive helminthic infections.
back:
• Hydatid disease and Neurocysticercosis.
• Choice for Echinococcus granulosus.
• Preferred over Praziquantel for Taenia solium larval brain infection.
• Absorption increases significantly when taken with fatty meals.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Diethylcarbamazine is considered the specific drug of choice for the treatment of [___] and loiasis.
back:
• Lymphatic Filariasis.
• Effectively kills microfilariae of W. bancrofti and B. malayi.
• Alters surface structure to facilitate host immune clearance.
• Can cause severe Mazzotti-like hypersensitivity reactions.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A traveler returning from the Nile region presents with hematuria and is diagnosed with Schistosoma haematobium. The appropriate treatment is [___].
back:
• Praziquantel.
• Drug of choice for all Schistosoma species.
• Increases parasite cell membrane permeability to calcium.
• Generally administered in two or three doses over one day.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the specific inhibitory action of Ivermectin on the nervous system of susceptible nematodes.
back:
• GABA-mediated flaccid paralysis.
• Targets glutamate-gated chloride channels.
• Increases chloride ion influx, causing hyperpolarization.
• Paralyzes the worm, allowing expulsion from the host.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Niclosamide and Praziquantel regarding their clinical utility in treating tapeworm (cestode) infections.
back:
• Adult vs. Larval stages.
• Niclosamide: Kills adult intestinal worms; ineffective against cysticercosis.
• Praziquantel: Kills both adult worms and larval stages (cysticercosis).
• Niclosamide requires thorough chewing of tablets.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary clinical application of Bithionol.
back:
• Fascioliasis and Paragonimiasis.
• First-line for sheep liver fluke (Fasciola hepatica).
• Alternative for lung fluke (Paragonimus westermani).
• Acts by uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: In the treatment of Leishmaniasis, the pentavalent antimonial [___] is a first-line agent that requires monitoring with an electrocardiogram due to the risk of QT prolongation.
back:
* Sodium stibogluconate (or Meglumine antimoniate)
* Mechanism: Unknown; possibly disrupts parasite bioenergetics.
* Toxicity: Nausea, myalgias, and reversible T-wave changes.
* Administered intravenously or intramuscularly for 20-28 days.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with a diagnosed amebic liver abscess fails to show clinical improvement after 5 days of Metronidazole. In addition to abscess aspiration, which specific drug is added to the repeat regimen due to its high hepatic concentration?
back:
* Chloroquine
* Reaches high liver-to-plasma ratios.
* Used strictly for extraintestinal amebiasis failing primary nitroimidazoles.
* Not effective against intestinal luminal parasites.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Nitazoxanide exerts its antiprotozoal effects against *Giardia lamblia* and *Cryptosporidium parvum*.
back:
* Active metabolite (tizoxanide) inhibits pyruvate-ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR).
* Disrupts anaerobic energy metabolism pathway.
* Lacks the mutagenic risk associated with nitroimidazoles.
* Approved for pediatric and adult use in the USA.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the therapeutic management of advanced (CNS-involved) West African Trypanosomiasis versus the advanced stage of the East African variety.
back:
* West (T.b. gambiense): Eflornithine (inhibits ornithine decarboxylase).
* East (T.b. rhodesiense): Melarsoprol (toxic trivalent arsenical).
* Eflornithine is better tolerated but ineffective against the rhodesiense species.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Identify the pharmacological property of Paromomycin that dictates its specific clinical utility in the management of asymptomatic *E. histolytica* carriers.
back:
* Non-absorbable aminoglycoside.
* Acts strictly within the intestinal lumen.
* Effectively eradicates cysts (nitroimidazoles only kill trophozoites).
* Drug of choice for luminal-only infections in the USA.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: During the parenteral treatment of Leishmaniasis or Trypanosomiasis, Pentamidine frequently causes [___] toxicity, characterized by an initial massive insulin release followed by symptomatic diabetes.
back:
* Pancreatic
* Causes hypoglycemia 5-11 days into therapy.
* Can lead to irreversible islet cell damage.
* Requires monitoring of blood glucose and renal function.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A traveler returns from Tanzania with fever and lymphadenopathy. Blood film confirms the hemolymphatic stage of *Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense*. Specify the preferred intravenous agent for this patient.
back:
* Suramin
* First-line for early-stage East African Sleeping Sickness.
* Does not cross the blood-brain barrier.
* Major toxicities include nephrotoxicity and rare anaphylactic shock.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain why Metronidazole monotherapy is considered insufficient for the curative treatment of amebic colitis, even if clinical symptoms resolve.
back:
* Metronidazole is highly effective against invasive trophozoites.
* It is poorly active against luminal parasites.
* Luminal amebicides (e.g., Iodoquinol) must follow to eradicate cysts.
* Prevents asymptomatic carriage and subsequent transmission.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Distinguish between the administration and half-life of Tinidazole compared to Metronidazole in the treatment of Giardiasis.
back:
* Tinidazole: 12-14 hour half-life; allows single-dose therapy.
* Metronidazole: 7.5 hour half-life; requires multiple doses over 5 days.
* Tinidazole generally has a superior tolerability profile.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Identify the specific protozoal infection for which Benznidazole or Nifurtimox are indicated, and specify the most common dose-limiting toxicity.
back:
* American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas Disease).
* Caused by *Trypanosoma cruzi*.
* Toxicity: Severe peripheral neuropathy and dermatitis/rash.
* Most effective in acute phase; limited efficacy in chronic disease.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: The nitrothiazolyl-salicylamide agent [___] is the first-line FDA-approved treatment for *Cryptosporidium parvum* and acts by inhibiting the pyruvate-ferredoxin oxidoreductase pathway.
back:
• Drug: Nitazoxanide.
• Acts as a prodrug rapidly converted to active tizoxanide.
• Unlike metronidazole, it is not associated with significant mutagenic effects in humans.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient being treated for *T. brucei rhodesiense* (East African) sleep sickness with CNS involvement develops seizures and cerebral edema. Identify the causative drug and the preventive pharmacological adjunct.
back:
• Drug: Melarsoprol (trivalent arsenical).
• Preventive Adjunct: Co-administration of corticosteroids.
• Pathogenesis: Reactive encephalopathy due to trypanosome disruption (occurs in 5-10% of cases).

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the role of serial electrocardiography (ECG) during the 28-day administration of Sodium stibogluconate for visceral leishmaniasis.
back:
• Monitors for T-wave changes and dose-related QT interval prolongation.
• Prevents progression to dangerous, potentially fatal cardiac arrhythmias.
• Toxicity typically increases cumulatively over the standard treatment duration.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the clinical utility and primary adverse effect profiles of Benznidazole versus Nifurtimox in the management of American trypanosomiasis.
back:
• Benznidazole: Nitroimidazole; preferred for acute Chagas; most common side effect is skin rash (20-30%).
• Nifurtimox: Nitrofuran; alternative agent; frequently requires discontinuation due to severe neuropsychiatric symptoms (restlessness, insomnia).

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Specify the administration routes and corresponding clinical indications for the aminoglycoside Paromomycin in protozoal management.
back:
• Oral: Not absorbed; used as a luminal amebicide for intestinal *E. histolytica* carriage.
• Intramuscular: Systemic therapy used for visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar), showing high efficacy in India.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: In the management of advanced West African sleeping sickness (*T. brucei gambiense*), [___] is the drug of choice because it inhibits ornithine decarboxylase and penetrates the CNS.
back:
• Drug: Eflornithine.
• Specificity: Effective for West African but not East African disease.
• Toxicity: Causes reversible anemia, thrombocytopenia, and occasional seizures.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with amebic dysentery experiences severe flushing, vomiting, and tachycardia after a single drink of alcohol. Identify the drug responsible and the specific biochemical mechanism.
back:
• Drug: Metronidazole (or Tinidazole).
• Reaction: Disulfiram-like effect.
• Mechanism: Inhibition of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase, leading to the toxic accumulation of acetaldehyde.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Describe the unique pharmacokinetic distribution and clearance of Suramin in the treatment of early-stage hemolymphatic trypanosomiasis.
back:
• Exhibits extremely tight protein binding and cannot enter the CNS.
• Mechanism of action remains unknown.
• Features a very long terminal elimination half-life of approximately 50 days.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the metabolic fate and primary clinical contraindications of the luminal amebicide Diloxanide furoate with Iodoquinol.
back:
• Diloxanide: Split in the gut into active unabsorbed diloxanide; contraindicated in pregnancy.
• Iodoquinol: Halogenated hydroxyquinoline; contraindicated in patients with iodine intolerance or preexisting optic neuropathy.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Identify the primary pancreatic toxicity and the associated blood glucose derangement seen 5-7 days after initiating systemic Pentamidine therapy.
back:
• Causes inappropriate insulin release from the pancreas.
• Leads to symptomatic hypoglycemia initially (after 5-7 days).
• May eventually result in permanent hyperglycemia (diabetes) due to pancreatic cell damage.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Nitazoxanide, a prodrug used for giardiasis and cryptosporidiosis, inhibits the [___] enzyme pathway essential for anaerobic energy metabolism in protozoa.
back:
• Pyruvate-ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR).
• The active metabolite tizoxanide interferes with the electron transfer reaction necessary for anaerobic survival.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A 40-year-old migrant from rural Brazil presents with an acute fever and signs of an infected bug bite (Romaña sign). Identify the oral nitroimidazole drug of choice to eliminate the circulating *Trypanosoma cruzi* parasites.
back:
• Benznidazole.
• It is used to eliminate parasites and prevent progression in the acute phase of Chagas disease.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the clinical utility of paromomycin in intestinal amebiasis versus visceral leishmaniasis management.
back:
• Amebiasis: Used orally as a non-absorbed luminal agent to clear cysts.
• Leishmaniasis: Used parenterally (IM) as a protein synthesis inhibitor to treat visceral disease.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with severe amebic colitis cannot tolerate metronidazole. Contrast the clinical preference for dehydroemetine over emetine in this rescue scenario.
back:
• Emetine is a natural ipecac alkaloid; dehydroemetine is a synthetic analog.
• Dehydroemetine is preferred due to its slightly reduced potential for cumulative cardiac toxicity.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Identify the specific pancreatic complication and subsequent glucose abnormality often observed 5–7 days after initiating IV Pentamidine therapy.
back:
• Inappropriate insulin release.
• Results in severe hypoglycemia, often followed by persistent hyperglycemia or chemical diabetes mellitus.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Compared to metronidazole, the agent [___] is often preferred for trichomoniasis because its 12–14 hour half-life allows for high adherence via a single-dose regimen.
back:
• Tinidazole.
• A single 2-gram oral dose provides efficacy similar to a multi-day course of metronidazole.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: A patient with late-stage East African Sleeping Sickness develops sudden cerebral edema and seizures after his first melarsoprol infusion. Name this life-threatening complication.
back:
• Reactive encephalopathy.
• Occurs in 5–10% of patients; believed to be triggered by the rapid disruption of CNS trypanosomes.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Eflornithine targets the advanced CNS stage of West African Sleeping Sickness.
back:
• Irreversibly inhibits the enzyme ornithine decarboxylase.
• Depletes polyamines essential for parasite cell division and survival in the central nervous system.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Contrast the therapeutic preference and chemical classification of the two primary agents used for American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease).
back:
• Benznidazole (Nitroimidazole): Preferred agent due to superior efficacy and slightly better safety profile.
• Nifurtimox (Nitrofuran): Frequently discontinued due to significant gastrointestinal and neurologic toxicity.

category: Discuss mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses and adverse effects of antiprotozoal drugs used for the treatment of amoebiasis, giardiasis, Leishmaniasis, and Trypanosomiasis
front: Identify the primary sensory structure permanently damaged by high-dose or prolonged administration of halogenated hydroxyquinolines such as iodoquinol.
back:
• Optic nerve.
• Overdose or prolonged use can cause optic neuropathy and irreversible visual field loss.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Classify Albendazole into its chemical pharmacological group and identify its two primary high-yield FDA-approved indications.
back:
• Class: **Benzimidazole carbamate**
• Indication 1: Hydatid disease (*Echinococcus granulosus*)
• Indication 2: Neurocysticercosis (*Taenia solium* larvae)

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 29-year-old patient presents with a large cystic liver mass confirmed as hydatid disease. The primary broad-spectrum oral agent that inhibits microtubule synthesis in this parasite is [___].
back:
• **Albendazole**
• Acts by inhibiting microtubule assembly.
• Penetrates well into hydatid cysts when taken with a fatty meal.
• Also possesses larvicidal and ovicidal effects.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism of action for Praziquantel against trematodes (flukes) and cestodes (tapeworms).
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to **calcium**.
• Induces massive contraction and spastic paralysis of the worm.
• Leads to vacuolization and disintegration of the parasite tegument.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical application and target stages of Ivermectin versus Diethylcarbamazine in filarial infections.
back:
• **Ivermectin**: First-line for Onchocerciasis; strictly microfilaricidal; intensifies GABA-mediated paralysis.
• **Diethylcarbamazine**: First-line for lymphatic filariasis and Loiasis; kills microfilariae and some adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the pharmacological classification of Pyrantel Pamoate and its primary physiological effect on target helminths.
back:
• Class: **Tetrahydropyrimidine derivative**.
• Effect: Neuromuscular blocking agent.
• Causes acetylcholine release and cholinesterase inhibition, resulting in spastic paralysis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Broad-spectrum benzimidazoles like Mebendazole and Albendazole exert their anti-helminthic effect primarily by inhibiting the synthesis of [___].
back:
• **Microtubules** (specifically by binding to β-tubulin).
• Prevents glucose uptake and energy depletion.
• Effectively kills eggs in *Ascaris* and *Ancylostoma*.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient diagnosed with Strongyloidiasis (threadworm) is prescribed a drug that intensifies GABA-mediated transmission. Name the drug and its primary contraindication regarding blood-brain barrier permeability.
back:
• Drug: **Ivermectin**.
• Contraindication: Avoid with drugs that enhance GABA activity (e.g., benzodiazepines, valproic acid).
• Generally contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the indirect anti-filarial mechanism of Doxycycline and how it differs from traditional microfilaricidal agents.
back:
• Targets **Wolbachia**, an intracellular bacterial symbiont.
• Killing the bacteria leads to sterility and death of adult worms.
• Provides macrofilaricidal activity unlike Ivermectin.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Niclosamide and Praziquantel regarding their efficacy against tapeworm ova and the resulting risk of cysticercosis.
back:
• **Niclosamide**: Kills adults but not ova; theoretically risk of cysticercosis if *T. solium* eggs are released.
• **Praziquantel**: Kills both adults and larvae; drug of choice for cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the chemical classification of Metronidazole and its clinical role in treating protozoal versus helminthic-associated conditions.
back:
• Class: **Nitroimidazole**.
• Protozoa: Drug of choice for amebiasis, giardiasis, and trichomoniasis.
• Helminths: Useful for *Dracunculus medinensis* (guinea worm).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
coreConcept: First-line therapy for systemic helminthic infections
front: The benzimidazole antihelminthic that serves as the drug of choice for the treatment of both hydatid disease and neurocysticercosis is [___].
back:
• Albendazole
• It is a broad-spectrum agent administered with a fatty meal for tissue infections to improve absorption.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with multiple parenchymal brain cysts and seizures. The clinician opts for Albendazole over Praziquantel. What pharmacological interaction between Albendazole and corticosteroids supports this choice?
back:
• Dexamethasone increases the plasma levels of Albendazole's active metabolite (sulfoxide).
• Conversely, corticosteroids decrease the bioavailability of Praziquantel by up to 50%.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the mechanism of action by which Ivermectin causes paralysis in nematodes such as Strongyloides stercoralis.
back:
• It intensifies gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated neurotransmission.
• This results in the immobilization and paralysis of the parasite.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical use of Diethylcarbamazine and Ivermectin in the management of Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness).
back:
• Ivermectin: Drug of choice; microfilaricidal and safer.
• Diethylcarbamazine: No longer used for onchocerciasis due to risk of severe inflammatory (Mazzotti) reactions.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary antihelminthic agent that acts by increasing the permeability of trematode and cestode cell membranes to calcium, leading to paralysis and death.
back:
• Praziquantel
• It is the drug of choice for all Schistosoma species and most tapeworm infections.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Before initiating therapy with Primaquine for the radical cure of P. vivax or treatment of Pneumocystis, the patient must be screened for [___] deficiency to prevent acute hemolysis.
back:
• Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
• Primaquine is an 8-aminoquinoline that causes oxidative stress in deficient erythrocytes.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 30-year-old immigrant from Southeast Asia presents with eosinophilia and abdominal pain. Stool microscopy confirms a Strongyloides stercoralis infection. Specify the first-line pharmacological treatment.
back:
• Ivermectin
• Dosage: 200 mcg/kg once daily for 2 days.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Doxycycline exerts a macrofilaricidal effect in patients with Wuchereria bancrofti or Onchocerca volvulus.
back:
• It targets and kills Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial symbiont.
• Depletion of Wolbachia leads to sterility and death of the adult (macrofilarial) worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the oral administration requirements for Albendazole when treating intraluminal parasites (e.g., Ascariasis) versus tissue parasites (e.g., Echinococcosis).
back:
• Intraluminal: Taken on an empty stomach to minimize systemic absorption.
• Tissue: Taken with a fatty meal to maximize absorption and systemic bioavailability.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: What is the mechanism by which Pyrantel Pamoate facilitates the expulsion of Ascaris lumbricoides from the gastrointestinal tract?
back:
• It acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent.
• It induces persistent activation of nicotinic receptors, causing spastic paralysis of the worm.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary antihelminthic drug of choice for treating all species of Schistosomes and most other trematode infections is [___].
back:
Praziquantel.

*   Mechanism: Increases calcium permeability causing paralysis.
*   Standard dose: 20 mg/kg (2–3 doses).
*   Notable for: Rapid first-pass metabolism.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with epigastric pain and stool findings of *Strongyloides stercoralis*. Identify the first-line pharmacological treatment for this infection.
back:
Ivermectin.

*   Dosage: 200 mcg/kg once daily for 2 days.
*   Mechanism: GABA-mediated signal intensification.
*   Contraindication: Avoid in pregnancy.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Pyrantel pamoate induces the expulsion of intestinal roundworms.
back:
Neuromuscular blockade.

*   Action: Stimulates acetylcholine release and inhibits cholinesterase.
*   Result: Paralysis of the worm.
*   Outcome: Worm is expelled by normal host peristalsis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the treatment efficacy of Mebendazole versus Albendazole specifically for managing *Trichuris trichiura* (whipworm).
back:
Mebendazole is generally more effective than Albendazole.

*   Mebendazole: Preferred for whipworm; dose 100 mg bid for 3 days.
*   Albendazole: Lower cure rates for this specific parasite.
*   Combination therapy: Often required for improved outcomes.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Specify the clinical role of Diethylcarbamazine and its primary effect on microfilariae.
back:
Primary drug for Filariasis, Loiasis, and Tropical Eosinophilia.

*   Action: Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure.
*   Outcome: Facilitates host immune destruction of the parasite.
*   Caution: May cause severe allergic reactions (Mazzotti reaction).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The drug of choice for treating cystic hydatid disease caused by *Echinococcus granulosus* is [___].
back:
Albendazole.

*   Mechanism: Inhibits microtubule synthesis.
*   Dosing: 400 mg twice daily with fatty meals.
*   Monitoring: Requires liver function tests and blood counts.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A traveler returns from Southeast Asia with lymphatic filariasis. If the goal is to kill the *Wolbachia* symbionts within the parasite, which drug is indicated?
back:
Doxycycline.

*   Target: *Wolbachia* intracellular bacteria.
*   Effect: Indirectly causes sterility and death of adult worms.
*   Significance: Superior macrofilaricidal activity against W. bancrofti.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the pharmacokinetic justification for preferring Albendazole over Praziquantel in patients requiring co-administration of corticosteroids for Neurocysticercosis.
back:
Drug-drug interactions with corticosteroids.

*   Albendazole: Corticosteroids *increase* its active sulfoxide levels.
*   Praziquantel: Corticosteroids *decrease* its bioavailability by 50%.
*   Result: Albendazole offers more reliable therapeutic levels.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Niclosamide and Praziquantel regarding their effectiveness against the eggs (ova) of *Taenia solium*.
back:
Neither drug kills the eggs.

*   Niclosamide: Kills adult worms only; requires purging to avoid cysticercosis risk.
*   Praziquantel: Kills adult worms and larval stages (cysticercus).
*   Shared failure: Viable ova remain a theoretical hazard for autoinfection.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary mechanism of action for Benzimidazole drugs like Mebendazole.
back:
Inhibition of microtubule synthesis.

*   Target: Binds to fungal β-tubulin.
*   Effect: Blocks microtubule assembly and disrupts glucose uptake.
*   Spectrum: Broad-spectrum (Ascariasis, Hookworm, Pinworm).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The benzimidazole class of anti-helmintics, including albendazole and mebendazole, exerts its primary effect by inhibiting [___] synthesis.
back:
* Microtubule synthesis.
* Binds to β-tubulin, preventing its polymerization.
* Leads to immobilization and eventual death of the nematode.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
coreConcept: Albendazole Clinical Utility in Hydatid Disease
front: A 29-year-old Peruvian immigrant presents with a 10-cm cystic hepatic mass discovered incidentally. His family has a history of sheepskin trading. What is the pharmacological drug of choice?
back:
* Albendazole.
* Used for Hydatid disease (Echinococcus granulosus).
* Often utilized as an adjunct to surgical removal or aspiration of cysts.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Ivermectin induces paralysis in susceptible nematodes and arthropods.
back:
* Intensifies γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated transmission.
* Occurs in peripheral nerves of the parasite.
* Results in tonic paralysis and hyperpolarization of the nerve/muscle cell.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic indications of Praziquantel and Niclosamide in the management of cestode (tapeworm) infections.
back:
* Praziquantel: Broad-spectrum; drug of choice for Hymenolepis nana and cysticercosis.
* Niclosamide: Second-line luminal agent; effective against beef/pork tapeworms but not cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the antibiotic that acts indirectly against filarial parasites by targeting the bacterial symbiont Wolbachia.
back:
* Doxycycline.
* Kills intracellular bacteria essential for parasite survival.
* Results in sterility and significant macrofilaricidal activity against W. bancrofti.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: In the treatment of lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti or Loa loa, the specific drug of choice is [___].
back:
* Diethylcarbamazine (DEC).
* Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure.
* Displaces them from tissues, making them susceptible to host immune defenses.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient diagnosed with Schistosoma mansoni infection in West Africa is unable to take Praziquantel. What alternative tetrahydroquinoline agent should be prescribed?
back:
* Oxamniquine.
* Active against mature and immature stages of S. mansoni.
* Note: It is not effective against S. haematobium or S. japonicum.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biochemical basis for the synergism observed when using Albendazole and Praziquantel together in the treatment of Neurocysticercosis.
back:
* Pharmacokinetic enhancement.
* Praziquantel increases the plasma concentration of albendazole.
* Albendazole remains the preferred agent due to better CNS penetration.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the species-specific targets of Metrifonate and Oxamniquine within the Schistosoma genus.
back:
* Metrifonate: Only active against S. haematobium.
* Oxamniquine: Only active against S. mansoni.
* Praziquantel covers all Schistosoma species.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Name the tetrahydropyrimidine derivative used as an over-the-counter neuromuscular blocking agent to expel ascaris and pinworms.
back:
* Pyrantel pamoate.
* Causes release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase.
* Results in spastic paralysis and expulsion from the intestinal tract.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The broad-spectrum benzimidazole that is considered the drug of choice for Hydatid disease and neurocysticercosis is [___].
back:
● **Albendazole**
● Acts by inhibiting microtubule synthesis in nematodes.
● Absorption is significantly increased when administered with a fatty meal.
● Rapidly converted to an active sulfoxide metabolite via first-pass hepatic metabolism.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 30-year-old immigrant from West Africa presents with subcutaneous swellings and a sensation of worms crawling in his eye. After a diagnosis of Loiasis is made, the physician initiates treatment with [___].
back:
● **Diethylcarbamazine**
● Drug of choice for *Loa loa* and tropical eosinophilia.
● Immobilizes microfilariae, making them susceptible to host immune destruction.
● Mazotti-like reactions can occur due to rapid parasite killing.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of action and primary clinical indications for Ivermectin.
back:
● **Mechanism**: Potentiates GABA-mediated signals, causing flaccid paralysis in the parasite.
● **DOC**: Strongyloidiasis and Onchocerciasis.
● **Contraindication**: Avoid in pregnancy and with other GABA-active drugs (e.g., benzodiazepines).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Praziquantel and Pyrantel pamoate regarding their physiological effects on worms and their primary clinical targets.
back:
● **Praziquantel**: Increases Ca2+ permeability causing tetanic contraction; targets Trematodes (Schistosomes) and Cestodes (Tapeworms).
● **Pyrantel pamoate**: Neuromuscular blocker causing ACh release and paralysis; targets luminal Nematodes (Ascaris, Pinworm).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the drug class and primary clinical utility of Niclosamide in parasitic infections.
back:
● **Class**: Salicylamide derivative.
● **Utility**: Second-line agent for tapeworms (*T. saginata*, *T. solium*, *D. latum*).
● **Mechanism**: Kills adult worms by inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation; not effective for cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The antibiotic [___] is used to treat lymphatic filariasis by targeting *Wolbachia*, an essential intracellular bacterial symbiont of filarial parasites.
back:
● **Doxycycline**
● Possesses significant macrofilaricidal activity against *W. bancrofti*.
● Indirectly leads to sterility and death of female worms.
● Often used in conjunction with other filaricides.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with hematuria and is found to have *Schistosoma haematobium* eggs in the urine. Specify the preferred treatment and its efficacy against adult worms versus eggs.
back:
● **Drug**: Praziquantel (20 mg/kg for 2 doses).
● **Effect**: Rapidly kills adult worms via paralysis and tegumental damage.
● **Egg pass**: Live eggs continue to pass for months until dead adults are cleared.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the anti-schistosomal mechanism of Metrifonate and its specific parasitic target.
back:
● **Mechanism**: Organophosphate that inhibits cholinesterase, inducing temporary worm paralysis.
● **Target**: Exclusively *Schistosoma haematobium*.
● **Consequence**: Paralyzed worms are swept into the lungs and destroyed by the host.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the amebicidal spectrum of Metronidazole with that of Paromomycin.
back:
● **Metronidazole**: Tissue amebicide; kills trophozoites in liver/gut wall but not cysts in the lumen.
● **Paromomycin**: Luminal amebicide (aminoglycoside); acts exclusively on intraluminal parasites and is the luminal agent of choice.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Classify the three major groups of helminths and name the first-line drug for the most common member of each group.
back:
● **Nematodes (Roundworms)**: Albendazole/Mebendazole (Ascariasis).
● **Trematodes (Flukes)**: Praziquantel (Schistosomiasis).
● **Cestodes (Tapeworms)**: Praziquantel (Taeniasis).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary biochemical target for benzimidazole carbamates like albendazole and mebendazole is the helminthic structural protein [___].
back:
• β-tubulin.
• Inhibition of microtubule polymerization.
• Results in blocked glucose uptake and impaired parasite cell division.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 29-year-old Peruvian sheepskin trader presents with a large, cystic 10x8cm liver mass on CT scan. He is diagnosed with Hydatid disease. Identify the drug of choice for medical management.
back:
• Drug: Albendazole.
• Pathogen: Echinococcus granulosus.
• Clinical Use: Preferred over other benzimidazoles for superior tissue and cyst penetration.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of GABA-mediated transmission in the mechanism by which Ivermectin treats Strongyloides stercoralis.
back:
• Intensifies GABA-mediated neurotransmission.
• Increases chloride ion permeability in peripheral nerves.
• Leads to hyperpolarization and flaccid paralysis of the nematode.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Praziquantel and Niclosamide regarding their activity against the larval stages of Taenia solium (Cysticercosis).
back:
• Praziquantel: Effective against larvae; increases calcium permeability causing spastic paralysis.
• Niclosamide: Ineffective against larvae; only kills adult intestinal segments via oxidative phosphorylation inhibition.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the biological rationale for using Doxycycline in the long-term management of lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti.
back:
• Targets Wolbachia.
• This intracellular bacterial symbiont is essential for filarial fertility.
• Depletion of Wolbachia leads to macrofilaricidal (adult-killing) effects.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) citrate is primarily classified as the drug of choice for treating [___] and Loa loa (loiasis).
back:
• Lymphatic Filariasis.
• Mechanism: Alters microfilarial surface structure to facilitate host immune destruction.
• Note: Replaced by Ivermectin for Onchocerciasis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient being treated for Onchocerca volvulus develops a high fever, hypotension, and bronchospasm within 48 hours of the first dose. Identify this reaction.
back:
• Mazzotti reaction.
• Cause: Host inflammatory response to antigens released by dying microfilariae.
• Management: Requires systemic corticosteroids and close monitoring.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the pharmacodynamic action of Pyrantel pamoate at the helminthic myoneural junction.
back:
• Acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker.
• Induces persistent activation of nicotinic receptors.
• Causes spastic paralysis, leading to the expulsion of worms by peristalsis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the species-specificity of Oxamniquine and Metrifonate in the treatment of Schistosomiasis.
back:
• Oxamniquine: Specifically used for Schistosoma mansoni.
• Metrifonate: An organophosphate specifically used for Schistosoma haematobium.
• Praziquantel: Broad-spectrum drug of choice for all Schistosoma species.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the specific neuromuscular effect of Piperazine on Ascaris lumbricoides that results in the expulsion of living worms.
back:
• Flaccid paralysis.
• Mechanism: Blocks acetylcholine at the myoneural junction.
• Result: Worms lose their grip and are expelled by normal bowel movements.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The broad-spectrum benzimidazole carbamate that is the drug of choice for hydatid disease and cysticercosis by inhibiting microtubule synthesis is [___].
back:
• Albendazole.
• Converted to active metabolite albendazole sulfoxide in the liver.
• Larvicidal in hydatid disease and neurocysticercosis.
• Absorption is significantly increased with a fatty meal.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 4-year-old child presents with intense perianal pruritus, especially at night. A cellulose tape test reveals Enterobius vermicularis eggs. Identify two primary drug classes/agents recommended for treatment.
back:
• Benzimidazoles (Mebendazole or Albendazole).
• Pyrimidines (Pyrantel Pamoate).
• Treatment is a single dose repeated at 2 weeks to prevent reinfection.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of Ivermectin in the treatment of Strongyloides stercoralis and Onchocerca volvulus.
back:
• Intensifies γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated transmission.
• Causes paralysis of the nematode by disrupting peripheral nerve signals.
• Microfilaricidal in onchocerciasis; doesn't effectively kill adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient in a region endemic for both Schistosoma haematobium and S. mansoni requires treatment. Contrast the clinical utility of Praziquantel versus Oxamniquine for this mixed infection.
back:
• Praziquantel: Broad-spectrum; drug of choice for all Schistosoma species (haematobium, mansoni, japonicum).
• Oxamniquine: Narrow-spectrum; active only against S. mansoni.
• Praziquantel is preferred for mixed species coverage.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Assign Diethylcarbamazine to its chemical class and define its primary role in filarial management.
back:
• Class: Synthetic piperazine derivative.
• Role: Drug of choice for Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi, and Loa loa.
• Mechanism: Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface to trigger host defense destruction.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The anti-helmintic [___] acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent that stimulates acetylcholine release and inhibits cholinesterase, resulting in the paralysis and expulsion of Ascaris lumbricoides.
back:
• Pyrantel pamoate.
• Active against luminal organisms only (not migratory stages or ova).
• Moderately effective against hookworms; ineffective against whipworms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with a heavy burden of Onchocerca volvulus microfilariae develops high fever, hypotension, and bronchospasm within 24 hours of starting treatment. Name this reaction and the drug responsible.
back:
• Mazzotti reaction.
• Triggered by Ivermectin.
• Caused by the immune response to proteins released from dying microfilariae.
• Managed with corticosteroids.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: During mass chemotherapy for lymphatic filariasis, Doxycycline is sometimes used. Describe the distinct biological target through which it achieves macrofilaricidal activity.
back:
• Target: Wolbachia bacteria.
• Wolbachia is an intracellular bacterial symbiont essential for filarial survival.
• Indirectly leads to sterility and death of adult (macrofilarial) worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the utility of Niclosamide and Praziquantel in treating Taenia solium regarding the risk of cysticercosis.
back:
• Niclosamide: Kills adult worms but released viable ova can theoretically cause cysticercosis (larval disease).
• Praziquantel: Highly effective against both adult segments and the larval stages (cysticercosis).
• Praziquantel is generally preferred for systemic safety.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
