front: List the drug of choice and a common alternative for treating Fasciola hepatica (sheep liver fluke).
back:
• Drug of Choice: Triclabendazole (or Bithionol).
• Alternative: Bithionol (standard 30–50 mg/kg on alternate days).
• Note: Praziquantel is uniquely ineffective against Fasciola species.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Benzimidazole anthelmintics like albendazole and mebendazole exert their primary physiological effect by inhibiting the synthesis of [___] in parasitic nematodes.
back:
• Microtubules
• Blocks polymerization of tubulin dimers
• Disrupts parasite glucose uptake and intracellular transport

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 40-year-old African immigrant presents with progressive vision loss and subcutaneous nodules. The drug of choice that acts by intensifying GABA-mediated neurotransmission is [___].
back:
• Ivermectin
• Paralyzes microfilariae by opening chloride channels
• Drug of choice for Onchocerciasis (River Blindness) and Strongyloidiasis

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of Pyrantel pamoate in the expulsion of intestinal roundworms from the human host.
back:
• Neuromuscular blocking agent
• Causes persistent release of acetylcholine
• Inhibits cholinesterase
• Results in spastic paralysis of the worm followed by expulsion

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Niclosamide and Praziquantel regarding their primary site of action and efficacy against the larval stages of Taenia solium.
back:
• Niclosamide: Only acts on intraluminal adult worms; not effective for cysticercosis.
• Praziquantel: Systemic absorption; drug of choice for cysticercosis (larval stages).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the standard drug of choice for treating Loiasis (Loa loa) and its primary effect on the parasite structure.
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine
• Immobilizes microfilariae and alters surface structures
• Enhances destruction by host immune defenses

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The drug of choice for treating Schistosoma haematobium that uniquely increases cell membrane permeability to calcium is [___].
back:
• Praziquantel
• Leads to muscular contraction and paralysis
• Effective against all species of Schistosoma

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient from a sheep-farming region in Peru presents with a large liver cyst. If pharmacological treatment is used to supplement surgery, the most appropriate agent is [___].
back:
• Albendazole
• Drug of choice for Hydatid disease (Echinococcus granulosus)
• Absorption is significantly enhanced by fatty meals

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the interaction caution required when prescribing Ivermectin to patients on benzodiazepines or barbiturates.
back:
• Potentiation of GABAergic signals
• Ivermectin intensifies GABA-mediated transmission
• Avoid concurrent use to prevent potential CNS toxicity

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Albendazole and Mebendazole in terms of their gastrointestinal absorption and clinical utility for tissue-based helminths.
back:
• Albendazole: Better absorption (especially with fat); converted to active sulfoxide; preferred for tissue infections.
• Mebendazole: Very low absorption (<10%); primarily for intraluminal parasites.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Which organophosphate agent is used as a low-cost alternative specifically for Schistosoma haematobium but is ineffective against S. mansoni?
back:
• Metrifonate (Trichlorfon)
• Cholinesterase inhibitor
• Paralyzes adult worms

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of action for benzimidazoles like albendazole and mebendazole involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis in nematodes.
back:
* Microtubule synthesis inhibition.
* Leads to impaired glucose uptake and depletion of glycogen stores.
* Results in parasite immobilization and death.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with disseminated threadworm (Strongyloides) infection presenting with 'hyperinfection syndrome' requires a drug that paralyzes nematodes via GABA-mediated transmission. The drug of choice is [___].
back:
* Ivermectin.
* Intensifies GABA-mediated signals in peripheral nerves.
* Causes paralysis of the nematode.
* Not to be used in pregnancy.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Praziquantel acts against schistosomes and cestodes.
back:
* Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
* Causes marked contraction and spastic paralysis of worm musculature.
* Leads to vacuolization and disintegration of the parasite tegument.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic utility of Albendazole versus Mebendazole regarding tissue-based helminthic infections like hydatid disease.
back:
* Albendazole: Active metabolite (sulfoxide) distributes well to tissues; drug of choice for hydatid cysts.
* Mebendazole: Minimal absorption (<10%); limited to intraluminal parasites like Ascaris or Trichuris.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the drug of choice for Loa loa (loiasis) and its effect on microfilariae.
back:
* Diethylcarbamazine.
* Immobilizes microfilariae and alters surface structure.
* Facilitates destruction by host defense mechanisms.
* Can cause severe allergic reactions from dying parasites.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The over-the-counter antihelminthic [___] acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent that causes release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase, resulting in spastic paralysis of worms.
back:
* Pyrantel pamoate.
* Acts primarily within the intestinal lumen (poor absorption).
* Effective against pinworms (Enterobius) and Ascaris.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with symptomatic brain cysts from Taenia solium is started on Albendazole. Explain why corticosteroids are co-administered in this scenario.
back:
* Decreases inflammatory response to dying parasites.
* Reduces risk of seizures and intracranial hypertension.
* Increases plasma levels of albendazole sulfoxide.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain how Doxycycline exerts a 'macrofilaricidal' effect against Wuchereria bancrofti despite being an antibacterial agent.
back:
* Targets Wolbachia, an endosymbiotic bacteria in the worms.
* Loss of Wolbachia leads to sterility in females.
* Eventually results in the death of adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Niclosamide and Praziquantel regarding their effect on tapeworm eggs and the risk of cysticercosis in Taenia solium infection.
back:
* Niclosamide: Kills adults but not eggs; risks cysticercosis if eggs hatch in gut.
* Praziquantel: Kills adult worms; currently preferred for T. solium to minimize egg-related risks.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the broad-spectrum drug of choice for all species of Schistosoma (flukes).
back:
* Praziquantel.
* Active against S. mansoni, S. haematobium, and S. japonicum.
* Standard regimen involves two or three doses in a single day.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism by which benzimidazole derivatives like Albendazole and Mebendazole exert their antihelminthic effect is the inhibition of [___] synthesis.
back:
• Inhibition of microtubule synthesis.
• Specifically binds to parasite β-tubulin.
• Prevents glucose uptake and depletes glycogen stores.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with symptomatic parenchymal neurocysticercosis is prescribed Albendazole. To mitigate the neurologic damage caused by the inflammatory response to dying parasites, the clinician must co-administer [___].
back:
• Corticosteroids (e.g., Dexamethasone).
• Helps reduce intracranial pressure.
• Prevents seizures during acute treatment.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of calcium ions in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against trematodes and cestodes.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
• Results in massive calcium influx.
• Causes muscular contraction and spastic paralysis of the worm.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic coverage of Praziquantel versus Niclosamide regarding the larval stages of Taenia solium.
back:
• Praziquantel: Active against both adult worms and larval stages (cysticercosis).
• Niclosamide: Only active against adult intestinal worms; no effect on cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary microfilaricidal agent utilized in mass chemotherapy programs for the control of Onchocerciasis (River Blindness).
back:
• Ivermectin.
• Intensifies GABA-mediated signals in peripheral nerves.
• Causes paralysis of the microfilariae.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The antihelminthic drug of choice for the treatment of Loiasis (Loa loa) and Tropical Pulmonary Eosinophilia is [___].
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine (DEC).
• Immobilizes microfilariae to increase susceptibility to host defenses.
• Kills adult worms of L. loa.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 40-year-old male with chronic pruritic dermatitis and eosinophilia is diagnosed with Strongyloidiasis. The first-line drug of choice is [___].
back:
• Ivermectin.
• Given as a single dose for two days.
• Superior tolerability compared to older agents like Thiabendazole.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the physiological mechanism by which Pyrantel pamoate induces the expulsion of Ascaris lumbricoides from the host intestine.
back:
• Acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent.
• Stimulates acetylcholine release and inhibits cholinesterase.
• Causes spastic paralysis followed by expulsion via peristalsis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the drug choice for Schistosoma haematobium versus Schistosoma mansoni in clinical settings where Praziquantel is unavailable.
back:
• S. haematobium: Metrifonate (organophosphate).
• S. mansoni: Oxamniquine (tetrahydroquinoline).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the rationale for using Doxycycline as an adjunct in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti).
back:
• Targets Wolbachia (intracellular bacterial symbiont).
• Deprives the adult filarial parasite of essential survival factors.
• Leads to sterilization and death of adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary anti-helminthic class of benzimidazoles, such as albendazole and mebendazole, exert their lethal effect by inhibiting [___] synthesis in parasites.
back:
• Microtubule synthesis.
• Prevents parasite growth and reproduction.
• Leads to gradual depletion of energy reserves.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 29-year-old Peruvian man presents with a 10-cm hepatic cyst on CT scan after contact with sheepskins. The medical treatment of choice for this condition is [___].
back:
• Albendazole.
• Targets Echinococcus granulosus (Hydatid disease).
• Often used as an adjunct to surgery or aspiration.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA) in the mechanism of action of Ivermectin.
back:
• Intensifies GABA-mediated signal transmission.
• Causes chloride channel activation in peripheral nerves.
• Results in neuromuscular paralysis and death of the nematode.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical utility and metabolic targets of Praziquantel versus Niclosamide in tapeworm (cestode) infections.
back:
• Praziquantel: Kills adults and larvae (cysticercosis); increases calcium permeability.
• Niclosamide: Luminal activity only; kills adult worms only; inhibits oxidative phosphorylation.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the drug of choice for the treatment of lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) and Loa loa (loiasis).
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine (DEC).
• Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure.
• Enhances susceptibility to host immune destruction.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate acts as a [___] agent, effectively treating intraluminal parasites like Ascaris and Pinworm while being poorly absorbed from the gut.
back:
• Neuromuscular blocking agent.
• Causes acetylcholine release and cholinesterase inhibition.
• Leads to spastic paralysis and worm expulsion.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with Onchocerca volvulus infection develops fever, headache, and hypotension 48 hours after starting Ivermectin. Identify this clinical reaction and its cause.
back:
• Mazzotti Reaction.
• Caused by host immune response to dying microfilariae.
• Managed with corticosteroids if severe.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: How does Doxycycline achieve a macrofilaricidal effect in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis?
back:
• Kills Wolbachia bacteria.
• These are essential intracellular symbionts for filarial survival.
• Indirectly leads to sterility and death of adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetics of Albendazole and Mebendazole regarding their use in systemic versus luminal infections.
back:
• Albendazole: Rapidly converted to active sulfoxide; good tissue/CSF levels (systemic use).
• Mebendazole: Less than 10% absorbed; remains in gut (primarily luminal use).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: List the standard triple-drug regimen currently recommended by the WHO for the radical cure of lepromatous leprosy.
back:
• Dapsone.
• Rifampin.
• Clofazimine.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The mechanism of action of benzimidazole anti-helmintic drugs like albendazole involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis, leading to parasite immobilization.
back:
* Microtubule synthesis
* Selectively binds to parasite β-tubulin
* Prevents polymerization and blocks glucose uptake
* Results in eventual parasite death and clearance

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 30-year-old immigrant presents with new-onset seizures. Imaging reveals multiple calcified parenchymal brain cysts. The preferred drug of choice to treat these symptomatic cysts is [___].
back:
* Albendazole
* Administered for 8–21 days
* Often combined with corticosteroids to reduce inflammatory response to dying larvae
* Superior to praziquantel due to better CNS penetration

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Praziquantel exerts its effect on trematodes and cestodes.
back:
* Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium
* Causes muscle contraction and spastic paralysis
* Results in tegumental damage
* Facilitates parasite dislodgement and host immune clearance

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the physiological mechanisms of muscle paralysis caused by Pyrantel pamoate versus Piperazine in Ascaris infections.
back:
* Pyrantel pamoate: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker; stimulates nicotinic receptors causing spastic paralysis.
* Piperazine: GABA agonist/hyperpolarizing agent; blocks acetylcholine at the myoneural junction causing flaccid paralysis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary mechanism of action of Ivermectin and its two most significant therapeutic indications in human medicine.
back:
* Mechanism: Intensifies GABA-mediated transmission, causing flaccid paralysis of the parasite.
* Indications: Drug of choice for Strongyloides stercoralis and Onchocerca volvulus (River Blindness).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Diethylcarbamazine is considered the first-line treatment for infections caused by [___], specifically targeting microfilariae.
back:
* Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) and Loiasis (Loa loa)
* Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure
* Makes them susceptible to host defense destruction
* Kills adult worms more slowly

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with biliary colic and jaundice. Stool microscopy identifies large eggs of the sheep liver fluke, Fasciola hepatica. Name the appropriate therapeutic agent.
back:
* Bithionol (or Triclabendazole)
* Used because praziquantel is ineffective for this specific fluke species
* Dosage: 30–50 mg/kg on alternate days
* Adverse effects include diarrhea and nausea

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain how Doxycycline acts as an indirect anti-filarial agent in the treatment of Wuchereria bancrofti.
back:
* Kills Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial symbiont of filarial parasites
* Bacterial loss leads to decreased worm fertility
* Results in macrofilaricidal activity (death of adult worms)
* Emerging as an alternative to standard agents

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Distinguish between Albendazole and Mebendazole regarding their systemic absorption and clinical utility for tissue-based infections.
back:
* Albendazole: Better systemic absorption (enhanced by fatty meals); active metabolite treats tissue parasites (hydatid/neurocysticercosis).
* Mebendazole: Poor absorption (<10%); primarily used for intraluminal parasites (pinworm/whipworm).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: List the specific helminthic stage targeted by Niclosamide and its primary clinical application.
back:
* Target: Adult tapeworms in the intestinal lumen
* Use: Taenia saginata (beef), Taenia solium (pork), and Diphyllobothrium latum (fish) tapeworms
* Limitation: Not effective for tissue cysticercosis

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The broad-spectrum anthelmintic agent Albendazole acts by inhibiting [___] synthesis, leading to the immobilization and death of the parasite.
back:
• Microtubule (specifically binds to β-tubulin)
• Prevents glucose uptake in nematodes
• Exhibits larvicidal and ovicidal effects in various infections

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient from sub-Saharan Africa presents with subcutaneous nodules and 'river blindness.' The treatment of choice for this condition paralyzes microfilariae by intensifying [___] transmission.
back:
• GABA (γ-aminobutyric acid)
• Targets glutamate-gated chloride channels
• Drug: Ivermectin

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of Praziquantel in the treatment of schistosome infections regarding cell membrane ion flux.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to Calcium
• Induces strong contraction and paralysis of worm musculature
• Leads to vacuolization and disintegration of the parasite tegument

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the treatment of neurocysticercosis with Albendazole versus Praziquantel when administered alongside corticosteroids.
back:
• Albendazole: Plasma levels increase with corticosteroids; preferred drug due to better CNS penetration
• Praziquantel: Bioavailability decreases by 50% with corticosteroids
• Indication: Symptomatic parenchymal brain cysts

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary clinical indication for Bithionol and its status as an alternative agent.
back:
• Primary indication: Fascioliasis (Sheep liver fluke)
• Status: Alternative to Triclabendazole
• Also used for pulmonary Paragonimiasis

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate acts as a [___] blocking agent, causing release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase to paralyze intestinal worms.
back:
• Neuromuscular
• Results in spastic paralysis and expulsion via peristalsis
• Effective for pinworm, ascaris, and hookworm

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: An HIV-positive patient develops persistent Strongyloides stercoralis infection. The preferred drug for this condition is [___].
back:
• Ivermectin
• Dosage: 200 mcg/kg once daily for 2 days
• Alternative: Albendazole or Thiabendazole

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the indirect mechanism by which Doxycycline exerts macrofilaricidal activity against Wuchereria bancrofti.
back:
• Targets Wolbachia (obligate intracellular bacterial symbiont)
• Wolbachia are essential for filarial fertility and survival
• Bacterial depletion leads to sterility and death of adult worms

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the oral absorption and metabolic fate of Albendazole with those of Mebendazole.
back:
• Albendazole: Erratic absorption (increased by fatty meals); rapidly converted to active sulfoxide metabolite
• Mebendazole: Minimal absorption (<10%); converted to inactive metabolites during first-pass

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the mechanism of Niclosamide in killing adult tapeworms in the intestinal lumen.
back:
• Inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation
• Stimulation of ATPase activity
• Note: Not effective against cysticercosis or ova

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The benzimidazole carbamate of choice for the medical management of both hydatid disease and neurocysticercosis is [___].
back:
• Albendazole.
• It rapidly undergoes first-pass metabolism to the active metabolite albendazole sulfoxide.
• It exhibits better tissue and CSF penetration than other benzimidazoles.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 40-year-old patient from an endemic region presents with intense pruritus and 'river blindness' (corneal opacities). Skin snips reveal microfilariae. Identify the treatment of choice and its primary mechanism.
back:
• Ivermectin.
• Paralyzes nematodes by intensifying γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated transmission.
• Causes immobilization of microfilariae in Onchocerciasis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Pyrantel Pamoate induces the expulsion of Ascaris lumbricoides from the gastrointestinal tract.
back:
• Acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent.
• Induces the release of acetylcholine and inhibits cholinesterase.
• Results in spastic paralysis of the worm followed by expulsion.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical utility and limitations of Praziquantel versus Niclosamide in the treatment of Taenia solium (pork tapeworm).
back:
• Praziquantel: Drug of choice; kills adult worms; effective against cysticercosis.
• Niclosamide: Second-line; kills adults only; no activity against cysticercosis or hydatid disease.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the standard drug for Loa loa (loiasis) and the strategy used to manage severe reactions in patients with high microfilarial loads.
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine (DEC).
• Adjunctive corticosteroids are used to limit allergic inflammatory responses.
• Apheresis may be used to reduce microfilarial burden before drug administration.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Praziquantel increases the permeability of trematode and cestode cell membranes to [___], resulting in paralysis and death.
back:
• Calcium ions (Ca2+).
• Increased intracellular calcium causes rapid contraction and dislodgement of the parasite.
• It is effective against all Schistosoma species.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 30-year-old patient presents with a 10cm liver cyst on CT scan. Serology confirms Echinococcus granulosus. Identify the drug used as an adjunct to surgical aspiration.
back:
• Albendazole.
• Often administered in doses of 400 mg twice daily.
• May be combined with Praziquantel to enhance plasma concentrations and efficacy.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the physiological pathway targeted by Ivermectin in arthropods and nematodes that results in flaccid paralysis.
back:
• Targets glutamate-gated chloride channels.
• Intensifies GABA-mediated signal transmission.
• Leads to hyperpolarization of the nerve or muscle cell.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the bioavailability and administration requirements for Albendazole when treating intraluminal parasites versus tissue parasites.
back:
• Intraluminal (e.g., Pinworm): Take on an empty stomach to limit absorption.
• Tissue (e.g., Hydatid): Take with a fatty meal to increase absorption.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the indirect mechanism by which Doxycycline exerts macrofilaricidal activity against Wuchereria bancrofti.
back:
• Kills Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial symbiont.
• Loss of Wolbachia leads to sterility and death of the adult filarial worms.
• Represents a novel target in filariasis control.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of action for the benzimidazole drug class, such as [___], is the inhibition of microtubule synthesis in nematodes.
back: • Albendazole or Mebendazole. • Blocks microtubule assembly by binding to beta-tubulin. • Leads to impaired glucose uptake and eventual parasite death.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
coreConcept: Drug of Choice for Hydatid Disease
front: A 25-year-old patient from Peru presents with a large hepatic cyst. CT scan and serology suggest Echinococcus granulosus. The drug of choice for medical management is [___].
back: • Albendazole. • Active against hydatid disease and cysticercosis. • Often used as an adjunct to surgical aspiration or PAIR procedures.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Ivermectin induces paralysis in organisms like Strongyloides stercoralis.
back: • Intensifies GABA-mediated signal transmission. • Specifically targets glutamate-gated chloride channels. • Causes flaccid paralysis of the nematode peripheral nervous system.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the impact of concomitant corticosteroid administration on the plasma levels of Praziquantel versus Albendazole during neurocysticercosis therapy.
back: • Praziquantel: Bioavailability is significantly decreased by corticosteroids. • Albendazole: Bioavailability is increased by corticosteroids. • Impacts choice of therapy in CNS infections.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the primary therapeutic effect of Diethylcarbamazine on the microfilarial stage of Wuchereria bancrofti.
back: • Immobilizes microfilariae and alters surface structure. • Displaces them from tissues. • Renders parasites susceptible to host immune destruction.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: [___] is a tetrahydropyrimidine derivative that acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent to expel Ascaris lumbricoides.
back: • Pyrantel pamoate. • Causes release of acetylcholine and inhibits cholinesterase. • Results in spastic paralysis and worm expulsion via peristalsis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with hematuria and terminal dysuria. Urine microscopy reveals Schistosoma haematobium eggs. The isoquinoline-pyrazine derivative used as the drug of choice is [___].
back: • Praziquantel. • Increases calcium permeability of parasite membranes. • Causes rapid contraction and paralysis of the fluke.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the unique 'indirect' anti-filarial mechanism of Doxycycline in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis.
back: • Targets Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial symbiont. • Wolbachia is essential for filarial survival and reproduction. • Results in sterility and death of adult macrofilariae.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the anti-schistosomal spectrum of Oxamniquine with that of Praziquantel.
back: • Oxamniquine: Narrow spectrum; active only against Schistosoma mansoni. • Praziquantel: Broad spectrum; active against all major Schistosoma species. • Both target trematodes.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the biochemical target inhibited by Niclosamide when treating Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm) infections.
back: • Inhibits oxidative phosphorylation. • Stimulates ATPase activity. • Kills the adult worm and scolex upon contact in the intestinal lumen.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary drug of choice for the medical management of hydatid disease caused by *Echinococcus granulosus* is [___].
back:
• Albendazole
• It functions by inhibiting microtubule synthesis in the parasite.
• Larvicidal and ovicidal effects are also observed.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient from an endemic region presents with intense pruritus and skin thickening. Skin snips reveal *Onchocerca volvulus* microfilariae. The mechanism of the first-line drug for this condition is [___].
back:
• Ivermectin acts as a GABA agonist.
• It intensifies signal transmission in peripheral nerves.
• This results in the paralysis of the nematode microfilariae.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of Praziquantel in altering the ionic balance of trematodes like *Schistosoma* species.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium ions.
• Induces immediate muscular contraction and paralysis.
• Causes parasite dislodgement from blood vessel walls to be destroyed by host defenses.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical rationale for choosing Albendazole over Praziquantel in the management of neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Albendazole has superior CNS penetration.
• It requires a shorter treatment course at a lower cost.
• Concomitant corticosteroids increase Albendazole levels but decrease Praziquantel levels.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary indications for Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) and its specific effect on microfilariae.
back:
• Indications: Lymphatic filariasis (*W. bancrofti*), loiasis, and tropical eosinophilia.
• Effect: Immobilizes microfilariae and alters surface structures, facilitating destruction by host immune mechanisms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate functions as a [___] agent, causing worm expulsion via acetylcholine release and cholinesterase inhibition.
back:
• Neuromuscular blocking agent.
• Effective against pinworms, ascaris, and hookworms.
• Poorly absorbed from the GI tract, acting primarily on luminal organisms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A pediatric patient with a heavy whipworm (*Trichuris trichiura*) infection fails to respond to standard Mebendazole. Adding [___] to the regimen is clinically recommended to enhance cure rates.
back:
• Ivermectin or Oxantel pamoate.
• Combination therapy is increasingly required for *Trichuris* because benzimidazole monotherapy often results in low cure rates.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the unique indirect mechanism by which Doxycycline acts as a macrofilaricidal agent.
back:
• Kills *Wolbachia*, an essential intracellular bacterial symbiont of filarial parasites.
• Its eradication leads to sterility and eventual death of the adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the systemic availability and clinical distribution of Mebendazole versus Albendazole.
back:
• Albendazole: Prodrug converted to an active sulfoxide with wide tissue distribution (useful for hydatid disease/cysticercosis).
• Mebendazole: Very low oral absorption (<10%), limiting its effect mainly to intestinal parasites.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Specify the role of Niclosamide in tapeworm treatment and its primary disadvantage regarding *Taenia solium*.
back:
• Role: Second-line agent for *T. saginata*, *T. solium*, and *D. latum*.
• Disadvantage: It is not ovicidal; viable eggs released from digested segments may theoretically cause cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism by which benzimidazole anti-helmintics like albendazole treat nematode infections is the inhibition of [___] synthesis.
back:
* Microtubule.
* This disrupts cellular structure and glucose uptake in the parasite.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 35-year-old patient from an endemic region presents with pruritus, dermatitis, and 'river blindness' symptoms. Skin snips confirm the presence of microfilariae. Identify the drug of choice.
back:
* Ivermectin.
* Mechanism: Paralyzes nematodes by intensifying GABA-mediated transmission.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of calcium permeability in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against schistosomes and cestodes.
back:
* Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
* Results in persistent muscular contraction followed by paralysis, vacuolization, and parasite death.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast Albendazole and Praziquantel regarding their pharmacokinetic interactions with corticosteroids during the treatment of neurocysticercosis.
back:
* Albendazole: Serum levels are increased by dexamethasone.
* Praziquantel: Bioavailability is markedly reduced (up to 50%) by corticosteroids.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the drug of choice for the treatment of Loa loa (loiasis) and tropical eosinophilia.
back:
* Diethylcarbamazine.
* It immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure to enhance host immune destruction.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker in helminths by stimulating [___] release and inhibiting cholinesterase.
back:
* Acetylcholine (ACh).
* This results in spastic paralysis and expulsion of the worm from the host.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with suspected Paragonimus westermani (lung fluke) infection fails to respond to Praziquantel. Which alternative agent is used to treat this trematode infection?
back:
* Bithionol.
* Dose: 30–50 mg/kg on alternate days for 10–15 doses.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe how Doxycycline exerts a macrofilaricidal effect against Wuchereria bancrofti and Onchocerca volvulus.
back:
* Indirectly kills the filarial parasites by targeting Wolbachia.
* Wolbachia is an essential intracellular bacterial symbiont required for parasite survival and fertility.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the physiological effects on parasite musculature produced by Pyrantel pamoate versus Piperazine.
back:
* Pyrantel: Spastic paralysis (depolarizing neuromuscular blocker).
* Piperazine: Flaccid paralysis (GABA agonist/ACh block at the myoneural junction).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: State the primary metabolic process inhibited by Niclosamide in the treatment of T. saginata or T. solium.
back:
* Oxidative phosphorylation.
* Note: It is effective against the adult worm in the gut but not against cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
coreConcept: Benzimidazole drug of choice for tissue helminths
front: The broad-spectrum drug of choice for hydatid disease and neurocysticercosis, which acts by inhibiting microtubule synthesis, is [___].
back:
• Albendazole
  • It is a benzimidazole carbamate.
  • Requires conversion to active metabolite: albendazole sulfoxide.
  • Absorption increases significantly with a fatty meal.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 7-year-old child presents with intense perianal pruritus at night. The Scotch tape test reveals eggs of Enterobius vermicularis. Which two drugs are first-line options for this condition?
back:
• Mebendazole or Pyrantel pamoate.
  • Treatment is usually a single dose repeated in 2 weeks.
  • Mebendazole inhibits microtubules; Pyrantel causes spastic paralysis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the role of calcium permeability in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against trematodes and cestodes.
back:
• Praziquantel increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
  • Leads to massive influx of calcium.
  • Results in strong contraction and spastic paralysis of the parasite.
  • Causes parasite dislodgement and death.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the specific filarial species targeted by Diethylcarbamazine with those primarily targeted by Ivermectin.
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine (DEC): Drug of choice for W. bancrofti, B. malayi, and L. loa.
  • Ivermectin: Drug of choice for Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness).
  • DEC kills microfilariae and adults; Ivermectin is primarily microfilaricidal.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
coreConcept: Indirect mechanism of action for filariasis
front: Name the specific antibiotic used in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis that acts by targeting the endosymbiotic Wolbachia bacteria.
back:
• Doxycycline
  • Targets intracellular Wolbachia symbionts.
  • Deprives filarial worms of essential factors, leading to sterility or death.
  • Shows significant macrofilaricidal activity.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Niclosamide, used primarily for tapeworm infections, acts by inhibiting mitochondrial [___] in the parasite.
back:
• Oxidative phosphorylation
  • Kills adult worms but not the ova.
  • Not absorbed from the GIT; acts locally on the worm.
  • Not effective against cysticercosis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient being treated for Onchocerciasis develops high fever, hypotension, and bronchospasm 24 hours after the first dose of therapy. Identify this reaction and the drug responsible.
back:
• Mazzotti reaction
  • Occurs with Ivermectin (or DEC).
  • Caused by immune response to dying microfilariae.
  • Managed with corticosteroids.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
coreConcept: Flaccid vs Spastic paralysis in anti-helmintics
front: How does the pharmacological mechanism of Piperazine differ from that of Pyrantel pamoate regarding worm paralysis?
back:
• Piperazine: GABA agonist; causes flaccid paralysis of Ascaris.
  • Pyrantel pamoate: Nicotinic agonist/cholinesterase inhibitor; causes spastic paralysis.
  • Both lead to expulsion by peristalsis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the systemic bioavailability and therapeutic utility of Mebendazole versus Albendazole.
back:
• Mebendazole: Low absorption (<10%); used for luminal intestinal worms.
  • Albendazole: Erratic absorption; first-pass metabolism to active sulfoxide.
  • Albendazole is preferred for tissue parasites (cysts).

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary antihelminthic agent that acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker, stimulating nicotinic receptors in nematodes.
back:
• Pyrantel pamoate
  • Causes release of acetylcholine and inhibits cholinesterase.
  • Effective against Ascaris and hookworms.
  • Poorly absorbed, acting mainly on luminal organisms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of the benzimidazole class (e.g., albendazole and mebendazole) involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis within the helminth.
back:
• Microtubule synthesis
• Resulting in disrupted cellular structure and function.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 29-year-old shepherd presents with a large, incidentally found liver cyst on CT. Serology confirms Echinococcus granulosus. Identify the first-line medical agent for this condition.
back:
• Albendazole
• Often used as an adjunct to surgery or percutaneous aspiration.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the neuro-pharmacological mechanism by which Ivermectin induces paralysis in susceptible nematodes.
back:
• Intensifies Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA)-mediated transmission
• Leads to hyperpolarization and tonic paralysis of the parasite.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the effect of concomitant corticosteroid administration on the plasma levels of Praziquantel versus Albendazole in neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Praziquantel: Bioavailability is markedly reduced by corticosteroids.
• Albendazole: Bioavailability (levels of active sulfoxide) is actually increased.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the primary oral antihelminthic that acts as the drug of choice for all species of Schistosoma flukes.
back:
• Praziquantel
• Effective against S. haematobium, S. mansoni, and S. japonicum.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The drug [___] is the first-line choice for treating Strongyloides stercoralis (threadworm) and Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness).
back:
• Ivermectin
• Acts as a microfilaricidal agent in onchocerciasis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A mother reports her child has nocturnal perianal itching. Clinical findings suggest Enterobius vermicularis. Which non-prescription tetrahydropyrimidine derivative can be used as a single-dose treatment?
back:
• Pyrantel Pamoate
• Acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent to expel worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the cellular mechanism of Praziquantel against adult trematodes and cestodes.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to Calcium ions
• Causes rapid contraction/paralysis, tegumental damage, and dislodgment.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the spectrum of activity for Diethylcarbamazine with that of Ivermectin in filarial infections.
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine: Highly effective against adult L. loa and microfilariae of W. bancrofti.
• Ivermectin: Primarily microfilaricidal; standard for O. volvulus.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Name the specific tetrahydropyrimidine derivative that is an analog of pyrantel and shows superior efficacy specifically against Trichuris trichiura (whipworm).
back:
• Oxantel Pamoate
• Often used in combination with albendazole for improved outcomes.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: In the treatment of Schistosoma haematobium, the organophosphate [___] acts by inhibiting cholinesterase, resulting in the paralysis and death of adult worms.
back: Metrifonate.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 28-year-old sheep farmer is diagnosed with a large, symptomatic liver cyst caused by Echinococcus granulosus. Describe the medical management strategy and the primary drug's mechanism.
back:
• Albendazole is the drug of choice.
• Inhibits parasite microtubule synthesis.
• Administered for 1–6 months as an adjunct to surgery or aspiration.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the role of calcium ions in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against trematodes and cestodes.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
• Causes rapid muscle contraction and paralysis.
• Leads to tegumental vacuolization and parasite disintegration.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the primary clinical indications for Bithionol with those of Praziquantel in the context of fluke infections.
back:
• Bithionol: First-line for Fasciola hepatica (sheep liver fluke).
• Praziquantel: First-line for Schistosomiasis and most other trematodes.
• Bithionol serves as an alternative for Paragonimus westermani.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the specific pharmacological effect of Piperazine on the musculature of Ascaris lumbricoides.
back:
• Blocks acetylcholine at the myoneural junction.
• Induces flaccid paralysis in the worm.
• Facilitates expulsion of live worms via host intestinal peristalsis.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate serves as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent that stimulates the release of [___] and inhibits cholinesterase in susceptible helminths.
back: Acetylcholine.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient presenting with loiasis and a very high microfilarial burden (>2500/mL) requires treatment. What is the risk of initiating immediate Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) therapy and how is it mitigated?
back:
• Risk: Severe encephalopathy and retinal hemorrhage.
• Cause: Massive inflammatory response to dying microfilariae.
• Mitigation: Initial load reduction via apheresis or low-dose albendazole.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: How does Doxycycline achieve its macrofilaricidal effect against Wuchereria bancrofti and Onchocerca volvulus despite being an antibiotic?
back:
• Kills Wolbachia, an endosymbiotic bacteria.
• Deprives the parasite of essential metabolic support.
• Results in parasite sterility and eventual adult worm death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the species-specific efficacy of Oxamniquine and Metrifonate in the management of Schistosomiasis.
back:
• Oxamniquine: Effective only against Schistosoma mansoni.
• Metrifonate: Effective only against Schistosoma haematobium.
• Neither drug is active against Schistosoma japonicum.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: State the clinical limitation of Niclosamide regarding the viability of Taenia solium ova and the associated theoretical risk.
back:
• Effectively kills adult worms but not the ova.
• Risk: Released ova could cause cysticercosis via autoinfection.
• Precaution: Use of a laxative post-treatment to clear dead segments.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of action for benzimidazole antihelminthics, such as albendazole and mebendazole, involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis in the parasite.
back:
* Inhibition of microtubule synthesis.
* Binding to beta-tubulin prevents dimer polymerization.
* Results in impaired glucose uptake and eventual parasite death.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient with multiple brain cysts due to Taenia solium larvae is started on albendazole. Why is the co-administration of corticosteroids mandated in this clinical scenario?
back:
* Dying larvae release antigens that trigger host inflammation.
* Corticosteroids reduce cerebral edema and seizure risk.
* Dexamethasone increases plasma levels of the active albendazole sulfoxide.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Explain the pharmacological mechanism by which Ivermectin induces paralysis in nematodes like Strongyloides stercoralis and how it differs from host GABA receptors.
back:
* Intensifies GABA-mediated transmission via glutamate-gated chloride channels.
* Causes hyperpolarization and flaccid paralysis of the worm.
* Highly selective for parasite receptors; does not easily cross the human blood-brain barrier.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A patient presents with Taenia solium (pork tapeworm). Contrast the clinical rationale for choosing Praziquantel over Niclosamide in this specific infection.
back:
* Praziquantel: Kills both adult worms and larvae (cysticercosis).
* Niclosamide: Kills only adult worms; carries a theoretical risk of ova release and subsequent cysticercosis.
* Praziquantel is more effective for small tapeworms like H. nana.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Identify the mandatory clinical precaution necessary before administering Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) to a patient with suspected Loiasis.
back:
* Microfilarial burden must be assessed (usually <2500/mL).
* High loads risk severe encephalopathy or retinal hemorrhage upon rapid killing.
* Pre-treatment with albendazole or apheresis may be required for high burdens.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate acts as a [___] agent that causes the release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase, resulting in spastic paralysis of the worm.
back:
* Neuromuscular blocking agent.
* Induces spastic paralysis in Ascaris and hookworms.
* Paralysis leads to expulsion of the parasite via normal host peristalsis.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: A 29-year-old immigrant from Peru presents with a large liver cyst. If Echinococcus granulosus is suspected, which drug is used to reduce cyst pressure and prevent secondary seeding before surgical aspiration?
back:
* Albendazole is the drug of choice.
* It is often used for at least 1 month prior to surgery.
* Praziquantel may be added to increase albendazole serum concentrations.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Describe the unique indirect mechanism by which Doxycycline exerts macrofilaricidal activity against Wuchereria bancrofti compared to traditional antihelminthics.
back:
* Targets Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial symbiont.
* Wolbachia are essential for filarial fertility and larval survival.
* Depletion of bacteria leads to sterility and death of the adult worms.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Contrast the dietary instructions for Albendazole administration when treating an intraluminal Ascaris infection versus a systemic Hydatid cyst.
back:
* Intraluminal: Taken on an empty stomach to maximize local concentration.
* Systemic: Taken with a fatty meal to enhance absorption.
* Mebendazole follows a similar fatty-meal absorption enhancement pattern.

category: Classify anti-helmintic drugs
front: Name the drug of choice for all species of Schistosoma and its primary biochemical effect on the parasite's integument.
back:
* Praziquantel is the drug of choice.
* Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium ions.
* Causes rapid muscle contraction, spastic paralysis, and tegumental damage.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Following oral administration, albendazole is rapidly converted in the liver to its active metabolite, [___], which achieves therapeutic levels in the CSF and hydatid cysts.
back:
• Albendazole sulfoxide
• Primary active form against tissue parasites
• Reaches high concentrations in bile and cystic structures.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 25-year-old traveler returns from Lake Malawi with hematuria. Urine microscopy reveals eggs with a terminal spine. The drug of choice for this condition acts by increasing membrane permeability to [___].
back:
• Calcium ions
• Causes parasite contraction and paralysis
• Leads to dislodgement from the vascular system and death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Niclosamide exerts its lethal effect on adult tapeworms.
back:
• Inhibits oxidative phosphorylation
• Stimulates ATPase activity
• Kills adult worms on contact within the bowel lumen.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetic properties of Albendazole and Mebendazole regarding their distribution to systemic tissues.
back:
• Albendazole: High systemic absorption (especially with fatty meals); widely distributed to CSF and tissues
• Mebendazole: Very low absorption (<10%); primarily used for intraluminal parasites.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the specific species of Schistosoma for which Oxamniquine serves as an alternative to Praziquantel.
back:
• Schistosoma mansoni
• Ineffective against S. haematobium and S. japonicum
• Causes contraction and detachment of worms from mesenteric venules.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Metrifonate is a safe, low-cost organophosphate that treats S. haematobium by inhibiting the enzyme [___].
back:
• Cholinesterase
• Paralyzes adult worms temporarily
• Paralyzed worms are carried from bladder vasculature to the lungs.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 6-year-old child presents with perianal pruritus and 'pinworms' are confirmed by tape test. The drug of choice is [___] given in a single dose and repeated in two weeks.
back:
• Mebendazole or Pyrantel Pamoate
• Pyrantel acts as a neuromuscular blocking agent
• Repetition is necessary to kill newly hatched larvae.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Describe how Piperazine induces the expulsion of Ascaris worms from the gastrointestinal tract.
back:
• Blocks acetylcholine at the myoneural junction
• Induces flaccid paralysis of the worm
• Parasites are expelled alive by normal peristalsis.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the therapeutic indications for Bithionol versus Praziquantel in the management of fluke infections.
back:
• Bithionol: Drug of choice for Fasciola hepatica (sheep liver fluke)
• Praziquantel: Drug of choice for Schistosomiasis and Paragonimus (lung fluke).

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: State the primary embryotoxic concern associated with the use of Benzimidazole drugs during the first trimester.
back:
• High teratogenic potential
• Generally contraindicated in pregnancy
• Use with extreme caution in children under 2 years.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Benzimidazole drugs like Albendazole exert their antihelminthic effect by specifically binding to beta-tubulin and inhibiting [___].
back:
- Microtubule polymerization.
- This disruption leads to impaired glucose uptake and depletion of glycogen stores in the worm.
- Eventually causes parasite immobilization and subsequent death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient with symptomatic parenchymal neurocysticercosis is started on Albendazole. Explain why corticosteroids must be co-administered in this clinical scenario.
back:
- Inflammation control: Decreases the host immune response to antigens released by dying larvae.
- Symptom prevention: Reduces the risk of seizures or neurological deterioration caused by peri-lesional edema.
- Pharmacokinetics: Corticosteroids increase plasma levels of Albendazole sulfoxide.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which Ivermectin induces paralysis in susceptible nematodes.
back:
- GABA agonism: Binds to glutamate-gated chloride channels and intensifies GABA-mediated inhibitory signals.
- Hyperpolarization: Increases chloride ion influx into parasite nerves and muscles.
- Outcome: Leads to neuromuscular blockade and paralysis, resulting in parasite expulsion.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical utility and safety profiles of Ivermectin versus Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) in the treatment of Onchocerciasis.
back:
- Ivermectin: First-line agent; effectively kills microfilariae without inducing severe systemic reactions.
- DEC: Rapidly kills microfilariae but is avoided due to the 'Mazzotti reaction' (severe fever, hypotension, and ophthalmic damage).

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Provide the pharmacologic justification for prescribing Albendazole with a high-fat meal when treating tissue-based helminthic infections like hydatid disease.
back:
- Absorption: Significantly increases systemic bioavailability compared to administration on an empty stomach.
- Tissue penetration: Higher plasma concentrations are required to reach effective therapeutic levels within liver or lung cysts.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: The therapeutic agent of choice for most trematode (flukes like Schistosoma) and cestode (tapeworm) infections is [___].
back:
- Praziquantel.
- It acts by increasing the cell membrane permeability to calcium.
- It is effective as a single oral dose for several species including Taenia saginata.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 10-year-old child presents with perianal pruritus, especially at night. For the treatment of this Enterobius vermicularis infection, Mebendazole is given as a single dose and then repeated after [___].
back:
- 2 weeks.
- Rationale: The drug targets adult worms but is not ovicidal (does not kill eggs).
- Timing: The second dose ensures elimination of worms that matured from surviving eggs.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Describe the specific ion-channel disruption caused by Praziquantel and its subsequent effect on the parasite tegument.
back:
- Calcium influx: Induces rapid membrane permeability to calcium ions, causing immediate spastic muscular paralysis.
- Tegumental damage: Causes vacuolization and blebbing of the outer layer, exposing parasite antigens to host immune destruction.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Distinguish between the mechanisms of parasite expulsion used by Pyrantel Pamoate and Piperazine in Ascaris infections.
back:
- Pyrantel Pamoate: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker (nicotinic agonist) causing spastic paralysis.
- Piperazine: Hyperpolarizing agent (GABA agonist) at the myoneural junction causing flaccid paralysis.
- Both prevent the worm from maintaining its position in the gut.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the primary pregnancy-related contraindication associated with the use of Benzimidazoles (e.g., Albendazole, Mebendazole).
back:
- Teratogenicity: These agents are embryotoxic in animals and generally contraindicated during pregnancy.
- Caution: Use is also restricted in children under 2 years of age due to limited safety data.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Following oral administration, the broad-spectrum antihelminthic Albendazole is rapidly converted in the liver to its primary active metabolite, [___].
back:
Albendazole sulfoxide.
- Bioavailability is significantly increased when taken with a fatty meal.
- Sulfoxide reaches therapeutic levels in bile, CSF, and hydatid cysts.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 40-year-old immigrant from Southeast Asia with chronic corticosteroid use develops abdominal pain and eosinophilia; larvae are found in the stool. The drug of choice for this infection acts by [___].
back:
Intensifying GABA-mediated signal transmission in peripheral nerves.
- Causes paralysis of the nematode.
- Effective for Strongyloides stercoralis and Onchocerca volvulus.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Describe the primary molecular mechanism by which Praziquantel induces paralysis and dislodgement in schistosomes and other trematodes.
back:
Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium.
- Resulting calcium influx causes tetanic contraction of parasite musculature.
- Leads to vacuolization and subsequent parasite death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the side effect profile of Albendazole when used for a 3-day course (e.g., ascariasis) versus a 6-month course (e.g., hydatid disease).
back:
• Short-term: Mild GI distress, headache, and dizziness.
• Long-term: Risk of pancytopenia, alopecia, and significant elevation of liver enzymes.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain how the antibiotic Doxycycline exerts a macrofilaricidal effect in the treatment of lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti.
back:
Indirect action by killing Wolbachia.
- Wolbachia are intracellular bacterial symbionts essential for the survival and reproduction of filarial parasites.
- Leads to sterility and death of adult worms.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Pyrantel pamoate functions as a [___] agent by releasing acetylcholine and inhibiting cholinesterase, resulting in the expulsion of Ascaris worms.
back:
Neuromuscular blocking.
- Causes spastic paralysis in the worms.
- Minimally absorbed from the GI tract; active mainly against luminal organisms.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient with loiasis (Loa loa) is treated with Diethylcarbamazine. Within 24 hours, they develop fever, malaise, and headache. This reaction is primarily caused by [___].
back:
The release of foreign proteins from dying microfilariae.
- Represents an inflammatory response rather than direct drug toxicity.
- Can be severe in cases with high microfilarial burdens.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the physiological mechanism by which Metrifonate clears Schistosoma haematobium despite having no direct effect on the parasite's eggs.
back:
Inhibits cholinesterase.
- Temporarily paralyzes adult worms.
- Causes worms to transit from bladder vasculature to the lungs where they are killed.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetic interaction of corticosteroids with Albendazole versus Praziquantel in the treatment of neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Albendazole: Corticosteroids increase active sulfoxide metabolite levels.
• Praziquantel: Corticosteroids decrease plasma drug levels by up to 50%.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the biochemical pathway inhibited by Niclosamide in the treatment of Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm).
back:
Inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation.
- Also stimulates ATPase activity.
- Effectively kills adult worms but has no effect on ova.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of benzimidazole anthelminthics like albendazole involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis by binding specifically to parasite β-tubulin.
back:
* Microtubule synthesis inhibition
* Prevents glucose uptake in the helminth
* Results in gradual depletion of glycogen stores and immobilization/death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient presents with new-onset generalized seizures. Brain imaging reveals multiple small, non-calcified parenchymal cysts with minimal surrounding edema. The pharmacological drug of choice for this condition is [___].
back:
* Albendazole
* Commonly administered with corticosteroids (e.g., dexamethasone) to reduce inflammatory response to dying parasites.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which Ivermectin achieves flaccid paralysis in nematodes like Strongyloides stercoralis.
back:
* Intensifies γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated signal transmission
* Binds to glutamate-gated chloride channels
* Leads to hyperpolarization and paralysis of the parasite.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the clinical application of Albendazole versus Mebendazole based on their systemic absorption profiles for treating tissue-based helminthic infections.
back:
* Albendazole: Erratically but better absorbed (increased with fat), active metabolite (sulfoxide) penetrates cysts/tissues well.
* Mebendazole: Poorly absorbed (<10%), primarily used for intraluminal intestinal nematodes.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the characteristic severe systemic reaction that may occur when Diethylcarbamazine is used to treat Onchocerca volvulus infection.
back:
* Mazzotti reaction
* Features: Fever, headache, pruritus, tachycardia, and hypotension
* Pathophysiology: Host immune response to antigens from dying microfilariae.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Praziquantel acts by increasing the permeability of trematode and cestode cell membranes to [___] ions, leading to rapid muscle contraction and subsequent paralysis.
back:
* Calcium (Ca²⁺)
* Causes vacuolization and disintegration of the parasite tegument
* Facilitates dislodgement from tissue.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient presents with hematuria and eggs with terminal spines in the urine. Contrast the standard dosing regimen of Praziquantel for S. haematobium with that required for S. japonicum.
back:
* S. haematobium: 20 mg/kg per dose, total of two doses.
* S. japonicum: 20 mg/kg per dose, total of three doses (due to higher resistance/burden).

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain how Doxycycline acts as a macrofilaricidal agent in the management of Wuchereria bancrofti despite being a bacterial protein synthesis inhibitor.
back:
* Targets Wolbachia, an intracellular bacterial endosymbiont of the filarial worms
* Bacterial death results in impaired worm fertility and gradual adult worm death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the risk of developing secondary cysticercosis when treating Taenia solium intestinal infection with Praziquantel versus Niclosamide.
back:
* Praziquantel: Low risk; kills adult worms but not eggs; minimal luminal egg release.
* Niclosamide: Higher theoretical risk; kills segments but releases viable eggs into the lumen; requires purge to prevent cysticercosis.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the primary neuromuscular mechanism of Pyrantel pamoate in the treatment of Ascaris lumbricoides.
back:
* Depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent
* Induces release of acetylcholine and inhibits cholinesterase
* Causes spastic paralysis and expulsion of the live worm by peristalsis.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Benzimidazoles, such as albendazole and mebendazole, exert their primary antihelminthic effect by binding to ̢-tubulin and inhibiting the synthesis of [___].
back:
Microtubules
• This disruption prevents microtubule-dependent processes such as glucose uptake.
• Leads to glycogen depletion and eventual death of the parasite.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 5-year-old child presents with perianal itching, especially at night. A Scotch tape test confirms Enterobius vermicularis. Identify the primary drug used and its necessary follow-up administration.
back:
• Pyrantel pamoate or Mebendazole.
• A single dose is given initially, then repeated after 2 weeks to kill any larvae hatched from surviving eggs.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain how Ivermectin achieves paralysis in nematodes such as Strongyloides stercoralis according to its primary neuro-pharmacodynamic effect.
back:
• Intensifies ̣-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-mediated transmission in peripheral nerves.
• This causes hyperpolarization and tonic paralysis of the worm's musculature, leading to its expulsion or death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the treatment of Intestinal Taeniasis versus Neurocysticercosis regarding the specific drugs and the role of adjunctive therapy.
back:
• Intestinal Taeniasis: Single dose Praziquantel to eliminate luminal adult worms.
• Neurocysticercosis: Albendazole (preferred) + Corticosteroids to kill tissue larvae and reduce inflammatory responses to dying parasites.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the standard drug of choice for Schistosomiasis and describe the common effect seen when it is used to treat patients with neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Praziquantel.
• In neurocysticercosis, it may trigger seizures or meningismus due to host inflammatory reactions around dying parasites.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: The drug [___] is utilized in filariasis not by targeting the worm directly, but by killing the endosymbiotic bacteria Wolbachia.
back:
Doxycycline
• Removal of Wolbachia leads to sterility and eventual death of adult filarial worms (e.g., Wuchereria bancrofti).

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient with Onchocerciasis develops high fever, hypotension, and bronchospasm 24 hours after initiating Ivermectin. Identify this clinical reaction.
back:
Mazzotti Reaction
• Triggered by the host's immune response to antigens released from the rapid destruction of microfilariae.
• Severe cases require management with corticosteroids.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which Praziquantel induces tegumental damage in trematodes and cestodes.
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to Calcium ions.
• Causes tetanic contraction and tegumental vacuolization, exposing the parasite to host immune attack.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast Pyrantel pamoate and Albendazole regarding their gastrointestinal absorption and primary anatomic sites of action.
back:
• Pyrantel pamoate: Poorly absorbed; active against luminal parasites (e.g., Ascaris, hookworms).
• Albendazole: Orally absorbed (enhanced by fat); active against tissue-dwelling parasites (e.g., hydatid cysts).

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Which antihelminthic agent is notorious for causing irreversible liver failure and Stevens-Johnson syndrome, making it an alternative rather than a first-line choice?
back:
Thiabendazole
• Much more toxic than other benzimidazoles (like Albendazole).
• Use is largely limited to strongyloidiasis or cutaneous larva migrans when other drugs fail.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Benzimidazole derivatives like albendazole and mebendazole exert their primary anthelminthic effect by binding to free β-tubulin, thereby inhibiting [___] synthesis in parasites.
back:
* Microtubule polymerization inhibition.
* Leads to impaired glucose uptake and glycogen depletion.
* Results in parasite immobilization and death.
* Provides larvicidal and ovicidal effects in many species.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A sheepskin trader presents with a large, fluid-filled hepatic cyst. If surgical aspiration is planned, identify the preferred pharmacological adjunct and its primary mechanism of action.
back:
* Albendazole.
* Mechanism: Inhibits microtubule synthesis.
* Use: Prevents secondary seeding of hydatid disease (*E. granulosus*).
* Administered weeks before and after surgical intervention.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the role of Calcium permeability in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against Schistosomes.
back:
* Increases cell membrane permeability to Calcium ions.
* Results in massive Calcium influx.
* Causes rapid muscular contraction and spastic paralysis.
* Facilitates tegumental damage and subsequent immune destruction.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast Ivermectin and Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) in the management of *Onchocerca volvulus* (River Blindness).
back:
* Ivermectin: Drug of choice; better tolerated; microfilaricidal.
* DEC: Avoided in onchocerciasis due to severe inflammatory reactions.
* DEC: Primary use is for *Wuchereria* and *Loa loa*.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the pharmacological mechanism of action and the specific nicotinic effect of Pyrantel Pamoate.
back:
* Mechanism: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent.
* Action: Acts as a nicotinic agonist to stimulate acetylcholine release.
* Effect: Causes spastic paralysis and expulsion of the worm.
* Use: OTC drug for pinworm and ascaris.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: The severe inflammatory response characterized by fever, hypotension, and pruritus occurring after treating microfilarial infections is known as the [___] reaction.
back:
* Mazzotti reaction.
* Caused by immune response to dying parasites.
* Commonly associated with Diethylcarbamazine treatment.
* Managed clinically with corticosteroids.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient with symptomatic brain cysts (Neurocysticercosis) is prescribed Albendazole. Why is the concurrent administration of Dexamethasone clinically indicated?
back:
* Decreases inflammatory response to dying larvae.
* Prevents neurological deterioration/seizures from cerebral edema.
* Dexamethasone increases plasma levels of the active albendazole sulfoxide metabolite.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Describe the cellular pathway targeted by Ivermectin to induce parasite hyperpolarization.
back:
* Target: Glutamate-gated chloride channels.
* Mechanism: Intensifies GABA-mediated transmission.
* Effect: Increases chloride influx leading to hyperpolarization and muscle paralysis.
* Benefit: High selectivity for parasites over human GABA receptors.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast Niclosamide and Praziquantel regarding their clinical utility and risk in the treatment of *Taenia solium*.
back:
* Niclosamide: Kills adults but not ova; carries theoretical risk of cysticercosis from ova release.
* Praziquantel: Drug of choice; kills both adults and larvae.
* Niclosamide is not absorbed; Praziquantel is systemic.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Identify the drug of choice for treating *Strongyloides stercoralis* and its primary route of excretion.
back:
* Drug of Choice: Ivermectin.
* Excretion: Almost exclusively in the feces.
* Duration: 200 mcg/kg once daily for 2 days.
* Superior to thiabendazole due to lower toxicity.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: The primary mechanism of action for benzimidazoles like albendazole involves the inhibition of [___] synthesis, leading to impaired glucose uptake and parasite death.
back:
• Microtubule (Beta-tubulin) synthesis.
• Prevents polymerization of tubulin dimers.
• Immobilizes and kills susceptible nematodes by disrupting cellular structure and transport.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A 10-year-old child presents with perianal itching, especially at night. Cellophane tape test confirms Enterobius vermicularis. Identify the first-line oral agent that acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent.
back:
• Pyrantel Pamoate.
• Induces persistent activation of nicotinic receptors.
• Causes spastic paralysis of the worm.
• Live worms are expelled from the gut via normal peristalsis.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain the role of glutamate-gated chloride channels in the mechanism of action of Ivermectin.
back:
• Ivermectin binds to glutamate-gated chloride channels.
• Increases membrane permeability to chloride ions.
• Leads to hyperpolarization of nerve and muscle cells.
• Resulting flaccid paralysis causes parasite death.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the administration requirements for Albendazole when treating intraluminal parasites (e.g., Ascaris) versus tissue parasites (e.g., Hydatid cyst).
back:
• Intraluminal: Administer on an empty stomach to minimize systemic absorption.
• Tissue-invasive: Take with high-fat meals to significantly increase bioavailability.
• Goal: Fat enhances absorption of the active metabolite, albendazole sulfoxide.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: How does Praziquantel induce the disintegration of the schistosome parasite tegument?
back:
• Increases cell membrane permeability to Calcium.
• Triggers massive contraction and spastic paralysis of worm muscle.
• Causes vacuolization and subsequent disintegration of the tegument.
• Exposes parasite antigens to host immune destruction.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: In the management of lymphatic filariasis and loiasis, the drug of choice that renders microfilariae susceptible to host immune destruction is [___].
back:
• Diethylcarbamazine.
• Immobilizes microfilariae and alters their surface structure.
• Displaces them from tissues into the circulation.
• Effective against both microfilariae and adult L. loa worms.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: A patient being treated for Onchocerca volvulus with Ivermectin develops fever, pruritus, and tender lymphadenopathy within 48 hours. Identify this reaction and its underlying cause.
back:
• Mazzotti Reaction.
• Caused by the host's inflammatory response to dying microfilariae.
• Common in onchocerciasis treatment.
• Managed with antipyretics or corticosteroids in severe cases.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Explain why Praziquantel is superior to Niclosamide for the treatment of Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm).
back:
• H. nana has an extra-intestinal larval phase in the intestinal wall.
• Praziquantel is absorbed systemically and kills these larval stages.
• Niclosamide is non-absorbable and only targets intraluminal adult worms.
• Praziquantel ensures a higher cure rate.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action, clinical uses, adverse effects of anthelminthic drugs
front: Contrast the spectrum and mechanism of Mebendazole versus Thiabendazole regarding toxicity and clinical preference.
back:
• Mebendazole: High therapeutic index, low absorption, preferred for intestinal nematodes.
• Thiabendazole: Significant systemic toxicity (dizziness, liver failure), less commonly used.
• Both inhibit microtubule assembly; Mebendazole is safer in pediatric populations.
