front: Describe the specific biochemical step blocked by HIV Protease Inhibitors (PIs) and the morphological result on progeny viruses.
back:
• Prevent proteolytic cleavage of the Gag-Pol polyprotein precursor
• Inhibit late-stage viral maturation
• Result in the production of immature, non-infectious budding particles

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Oseltamivir and Zanamivir act by inhibiting the influenza enzyme [___], which is responsible for the release of progeny virions from the host cell.
back:
• Neuraminidase
• Prevents clumping of newly released virions to the host membrane
• Effective against both Influenza A and B strains

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A patient co-infected with HIV and Hepatitis B (HBV) requires a single agent that targets both viruses. Identify the first-line nucleotide analog used for this dual activity.
back:
• Tenofovir (Disoproxil Fumarate or Alafenamide)
• Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and HBV DNA polymerase
• High genetic barrier to resistance for HBV

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain how the fusion inhibitor Enfuvirtide carries out its biological function during viral entry.
back:
• Binds specifically to the gp41 subunit of the HIV envelope
• Prevents conformational changes needed for viral-cellular membrane fusion
• Administered via subcutaneous injection in treatment-experienced patients

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the standard therapeutic goals of Nucleoside Analogs for HBV with Direct-Acting Antivirals (DAAs) for HCV.
back:
• HBV therapy: Aim for long-term suppression and seroconversion; rarely curative
• HCV therapy: Aim for viral eradication (Sustained Viral Response/SVR) using finite oral courses

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Identify the nonstructural protein targeted by anti-HCV agents with the suffix '-asvir' (e.g., Ledipasvir, Velpatasvir).
back:
• NS5A protein
• Involved in viral RNA replication and virion assembly
• Essential component of all-oral, interferon-free combination regimens

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Among the triazole antifungal class, [___] is unique for having a significantly long terminal elimination half-life of approximately 130 hours.
back:
* Isavuconazole
* Long terminal half-life reduces dosing frequency to once-daily
* Effective against both invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis
* Administered as the water-soluble prodrug Isavuconazonium sulfate

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: A patient with candidemia is switched from Amphotericin B to an echinocandin. During the first infusion, they experience minor flushing and GI upset. Explain the pathophysiology of this infusion reaction.
back:
* Histamine release during intravenous infusion (especially with Anidulafungin)
* Non-allergic, infusion-rate related phenomenon
* Echinocandins generally have the fewest side effects of systemic antifungals
* Class works by inhibiting β(1–3)-glucan cell wall synthesis

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Describe the specific impact of Rifamycins (e.g., Rifampin) on the clinical efficacy and serum concentrations of Itraconazole.
back:
* Significantly decreases Itraconazole serum levels
* Mechanism: Potent induction of hepatic microsomal enzymes (CYP450)
* Leads to subtherapeutic drug exposure and high risk of treatment failure

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Contrast the primary clinical indications for which Voriconazole and Caspofungin are respectively considered first-line or preferred agents.
back:
* Voriconazole: Drug of choice for Invasive Aspergillosis
* Caspofungin: Preferred for Disseminated Candidiasis (especially in neutropenic patients)
* Distinction depends on mold-specific (Voriconazole) versus yeast-specific (Caspofungin) efficacy profiles

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Which systemic triazole requires administration with a high-fat meal to significantly increase its oral bioavailability to therapeutic levels?
back:
* Posaconazole (oral suspension and delayed-release tablets)
* Bioavailability is highly dependent on gastric pH and fatty food intake
* Critical for achieving levels necessary to treat invasive mold infections

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: To gauge the severity of potential infusion-related reactions, many clinicians first administer a [___] mg test dose of intravenous Amphotericin B.
back:
* 1 mg test dose
* Used to assess the intensity of rigors, chills, or hypotension
* Guides the need for premedication with antipyretics or corticosteroids

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: A patient with a history of cardiac arrhythmias requires triazole therapy. Which agent is specifically preferred because it is associated with shortening, rather than prolongation, of the QTc interval?
back:
* Isavuconazole
* The only azole shown to shorten the QT interval
* Preferred in patients at risk for torsades de pointes
* Unlike Voriconazole and Posaconazole which lengthen the QTc interval

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which some Candida species develop secondary resistance to Flucytosine when used as monotherapy.
back:
* Altered drug metabolism via enzyme mutations
* Specifically, mutations in enzymes responsible for converting 5-FC to its active form (5-fluorouracil)
* Occurs rapidly, necessitating combination therapy (e.g., with Amphotericin B)

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Contrast the hepatic elimination pathways of Caspofungin and Micafungin.
back:
* Caspofungin: Eliminated via hydrolysis and N-acetylation; requires dose reduction in hepatic insufficiency
* Micafungin: Metabolized by arylsulfatase and catechol-O-methyltransferase; no adjustment needed for liver failure
* Neither drug is significantly cleared by the kidneys

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Identify the systemic imidazole that is administered specifically as a lozenge (troche) for the treatment of oropharyngeal thrush.
back:
* Clotrimazole
* Troche formulation allows local mucosal delivery with minimal systemic absorption
* Provides a more pleasant-tasting alternative to Nystatin liquid suspensions
* Effective for mild to moderate mucocutaneous candidiasis

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) [___] is unique among its class because it is an acyclic phosphonate that requires only two intracellular phosphorylation steps for activation.
back:
• Drug: Tenofovir (Disoproxil or Alafenamide).
• Mechanism: Competitively inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and causes chain termination.
• Clinical Use: Potent activity against both HIV and Hepatitis B virus (HBV).

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A 34-year-old HIV-positive patient is scheduled to begin a new regimen. The physician orders HLA-B*5701 screening to avoid a potential multi-organ systemic hypersensitivity reaction. This testing is mandatory before prescribing [___].
back:
• Drug: Abacavir.
• Class: NRTI (Guanosine analog).
• Clinical Pearl: Testing has a 100% negative predictive value; rechallenge is strictly contraindicated if a reaction occurs.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of the viral neuraminidase enzyme as a target for anti-influenza medications like Oseltamivir and Zanamivir.
back:
• Action: Neuraminidase inhibitors competitively block the viral enzyme site.
• Result: Prevents cleavage of sialic acid residues on the host cell.
• Outcome: Progeny virions clump together and to the cell membrane, stopping viral spread.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the activation requirements of Acyclovir versus Cidofovir in the treatment of DNA virus infections.
back:
• Acyclovir: Requires initial phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase; effective against HSV and VZV.
• Cidofovir: Activation is independent of viral enzymes; maintains activity against thymidine kinase-deficient or mutated strains of CMV and HSV.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Identify the primary mechanism of action and the specific HIV life cycle step targeted by the drug Maraviroc.
back:
• Class: CCR5 Co-receptor Antagonist.
• Target: Binds selectively to host CCR5 receptors on CD4 cells.
• Life Cycle Step: Blocks viral entry by preventing the gp120 protein from accessing the host co-receptor.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The inorganic pyrophosphate analog [___] is classified as a non-nucleoside DNA polymerase inhibitor that does not require activation by viral or host cell kinases.
back:
• Drug: Foscarnet.
• Mechanism: Directly inhibits viral DNA polymerase, RNA polymerase, and HIV reverse transcriptase.
• Use: Primarily for ganciclovir-resistant CMV retinitis and acyclovir-resistant HSV/VZV.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: An HIV patient co-infected with Hepatitis B (HBV) develops a severe flare of hepatitis after discontinuing their antiretroviral regimen. This is most likely due to the withdrawal of which two specific NRTIs active against both viruses?
back:
• Drugs: Lamivudine (3TC) or Tenofovir.
• Mechanism: Both drugs inhibit HBV DNA polymerase.
• Clinical Warning: Discontinuation can lead to rebound HBV replication and acute hepatic decompensation.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Describe how the HIV Protease Inhibitor (PI) class (e.g., Atazanavir) carries out its biological function during the final stages of viral replication.
back:
• Target: Viral aspartyl protease enzyme.
• Action: Prevents cleavage of Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors into functional proteins.
• Outcome: Results in the production of immature, noninfectious viral particles that cannot infect new cells.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the three main Hepatitis C (HCV) Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) classes by their characteristic drug suffixes.
back:
• NS3/4A Protease Inhibitors: Suffix "-previr" (e.g., Simeprevir).
• NS5A Inhibitors: Suffix "-asvir" (e.g., Ledipasvir).
• NS5B Polymerase Inhibitors: Suffix "-buvir" (e.g., Sofosbuvir).

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Name the two distinct classes of antiviral drugs used to treat Influenza A and provide one example for each.
back:
• Neuraminidase Inhibitors: Oseltamivir, Zanamivir, or Peramivir (Active against A and B).
• Adamantanes: Amantadine or Rimantadine (Block M2 proton channel; active only against A; high current resistance).

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The nucleoside analog [___] is a prodrug that requires initial phosphorylation by virus-specific thymidine kinase, making it selectively active against HSV and VZV.
back:
* Acyclovir
* Competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase
* Incorporates into viral DNA causing chain termination
* Valacyclovir is its high-bioavailability l-valyl ester prodrug

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A patient with AIDS and CMV retinitis fails Ganciclovir therapy due to a UL97 mutation. Identify the drug of choice that works by directly inhibiting viral DNA polymerase without requiring activation by viral kinases.
back:
* Foscarnet
* Inorganic pyrophosphate analog
* Blocks pyrophosphate binding site on DNA polymerase
* Also active against acyclovir-resistant HSV

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain the biochemical difference in the mechanism of action between HIV Non-nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs) and Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs).
back:
* NNRTIs: Allosteric inhibition (bind directly to a site near the active site)
* NRTIs: Competitive inhibition (incorporated as 'false' building blocks)
* NNRTIs: Do not require intracellular phosphorylation
* NRTIs: Cause DNA chain termination

category: Classify antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Antiretroviral Class Comparison and Metabolic Side Effects
front: Contrast the clinical application and common class toxicities of HIV Protease Inhibitors (PIs) with Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs).
back:
* PIs: Target Gag-Pol cleavage; associated with lipodystrophy, hyperlipidemia, and insulin resistance
* INSTIs: Target provirus integration; generally well-tolerated with fewer metabolic effects
* PIs: Often require 'boosting' with Ritonavir (CYP3A4 inhibitor)
* INSTIs: Preferred in modern first-line regimens

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Identify the specific viral protein targeted by Raltegravir and describe the replication step it blocks.
back:
* Integrase enzyme
* Blocks strand transfer (third step of integration)
* Prevents HIV DNA integration into host chromosomes
* Inhibits both HIV-1 and HIV-2

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: In the treatment of Chronic Hepatitis C, the direct-acting antiviral [___] acts as an NS5B nucleoside polymerase inhibitor to cause viral RNA chain termination.
back:
* Sofosbuvir
* Activated to uridine analog triphosphate
* Pangenotypic activity (effective across all HCV genotypes)
* Often combined with NS5A inhibitors like Ledipasvir

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A patient on HIV therapy requires a change in medication due to a positive HLA-B*5701 screen. Identify the drug responsible and the clinical risk associated with this genotype.
back:
* Abacavir
* Risk: Fatal hypersensitivity reaction
* Symptoms: Fever, rash, GI upset, and respiratory distress
* Mechanism: Guanosine analog (NRTI)

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Describe the physiological target of Maraviroc and explain why a 'tropism' test is mandatory before initiating therapy.
back:
* Target: Human CCR5 receptor (host cell co-receptor)
* Blocks gp120 binding and viral entry
* Tropism test: Ensures the virus is CCR5-tropic
* Ineffective against CXCR4-tropic or dual-tropic strains

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the mechanisms of the anti-influenza agents Oseltamivir and Amantadine.
back:
* Oseltamivir: Neuraminidase inhibitor; prevents viral release from host cells
* Amantadine: M2 ion channel blocker; prevents viral uncoating
* Oseltamivir: Active against Influenza A and B
* Amantadine: Active only against Influenza A (high resistance rates)

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Which group of anti-HCV drugs includes agents such as Simeprevir and Paritaprevir, and what is their primary enzyme target?
back:
* NS3/4A Protease Inhibitors
* Target: Serine protease
* Function: Blocks post-translational processing of viral polyproteins
* Simeprevir: Often requires screening for Q80K polymorphism

category: Classify antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Nucleoside vs Nucleotide Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors
front: In the classification of antiretrovirals, the drug [___] is a nucleotide analog (NtRTI) that requires only two phosphorylation steps instead of three for intracellular activation.
back:
• Tenofovir
• Classified as a Nucleotide Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor
• Bypasses the initial rate-limiting phosphorylation step
• Competitively inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and causes chain termination.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A 40-year-old HIV-positive male with a CD4 count of 40 presents with floaters and blurred vision. Fundoscopy shows white fluffy retinal infiltrates. Identify the class and preferred oral drug for this condition.
back:
• Condition: CMV Retinitis
• Class: DNA Polymerase Inhibitor
• Drug: Valganciclovir
• L-valyl ester prodrug with high oral bioavailability compared to ganciclovir.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of viral neuraminidase inhibition by agents such as Oseltamivir in the treatment of Influenza A and B.
back:
• Target: Viral neuraminidase enzyme
• Mechanism: Prevents cleavage of sialic acid residues on host cell membranes
• Effect: Newly formed virions clump together and fail to release from the cell
• Result: Halts the spread of infection within the respiratory tract.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the genetic barrier to resistance and typical mutation patterns of first-generation NNRTIs (e.g., Nevirapine) versus Protease Inhibitors (PIs).
back:
• NNRTI: Low genetic barrier; resistance arises from a single point mutation (e.g., K103N)
• PI: High genetic barrier; requires accumulation of multiple mutations (e.g., codons 10, 46, 54, 82)
• NRTIs lack cross-resistance with NNRTIs.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: List the three primary enzymatic or protein targets utilized by Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) agents in the classification of Hepatitis C therapy.
back:
• NS3/4A Protease (e.g., Simeprevir, Grazoprevir)
• NS5A Protein (e.g., Ledipasvir, Velpatasvir)
• NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (e.g., Sofosbuvir, Dasabuvir).

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: [___] is a synthetic 36-amino-acid peptide classified as a Fusion Inhibitor that prevents HIV entry by binding to the gp41 subunit of the viral envelope.
back:
• Enfuvirtide
• Blocks conformational changes required for membrane fusion
• Only parenterally administered (subcutaneous) antiretroviral agent
• Lacks cross-resistance with other antiretroviral classes.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A patient with chronic HBV is started on a cyclopentyl guanosine analog that inhibits base priming and DNA strand synthesis. Identify the drug and its major advantage over Lamivudine.
back:
• Drug: Entecavir
• Classification: Nucleoside Analog
• Advantage: Significantly higher genetic barrier to resistance in treatment-naïve patients
• Clinical Use: First-line oral therapy for chronic HBV.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism that ensures the selective toxicity of Acyclovir toward HSV-infected cells while sparing healthy host cells.
back:
• Activation: Requires virus-specified thymidine kinase for the first phosphorylation step
• Selectivity: Active drug only accumulates in virally infected cells
• Action: Triphosphate form competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase and causes chain termination.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the mechanisms of action between Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) and CCR5 Co-receptor Antagonists.
back:
• INSTI (e.g., Raltegravir): Interferes with the integration of reverse-transcribed HIV DNA into the host chromosome
• CCR5 Antagonist (e.g., Maraviroc): Binds to the host CCR5 receptor to block viral attachment/entry
• Maraviroc requires tropism testing before use.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Categorize the anti-influenza drug Amantadine based on its viral target and current clinical utility.
back:
• Class: Adamantane
• Target: M2 proton ion channel (inhibits viral uncoating)
• Specificity: Influenza A only
• Status: No longer recommended for use due to >99% resistance in circulating strains.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Transient visual disturbances, including blurring and changes in color perception (photopsia), are a characteristic dose-related adverse effect of the triazole [___].
back:
* Voriconazole
* Occurs in approximately 30% of patients
* Symptoms typically resolve within 30 minutes of dosing
* Does not usually require discontinuation

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: A renal transplant recipient on Cyclosporine is diagnosed with invasive Candidemia. The clinician avoids Caspofungin due to a significant risk of [___].
back:
* Hepatotoxicity (elevated liver enzymes)
* Cyclosporine increases Caspofungin plasma exposure
* Combination is generally contraindicated in clinical guidelines

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Explain why Nystatin's clinical application is strictly limited to topical or oral luminal use, despite its broad spectrum against Candida species.
back:
* High systemic toxicity (precludes parenteral administration)
* Negligible absorption from skin, mucous membranes, or GI tract
* Safely used only for suppression of local or superficial infections

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Contrast the primary molecular mechanisms of fungal resistance against polyenes (e.g., Amphotericin B) versus the triazole class.
back:
* Polyenes: Reduction in membrane ergosterol concentration or modification of the target sterol to reduce binding affinity.
* Triazoles: Mutations in 14-α-demethylase enzyme, enzyme overexpression, or activation of multidrug efflux pumps.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Identify the unique pharmacokinetic property of Fluconazole regarding its elimination that differentiates it from most other systemic azoles.
back:
* Predominantly renal excretion (cleared as unchanged drug)
* High water solubility compared to other lipophilic azoles
* Requires mandatory dosage adjustment in patients with renal failure

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: To attenuate the prerenal component of nephrotoxicity during Amphotericin B therapy, clinicians routinely perform [___] before each dose.
back:
* Sodium loading (Normal saline infusion)
* Maintains renal perfusion to reduce reversible azotemia
* Does not completely prevent irreversible renal tubular injury

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: A patient with severe hepatic failure requires therapy for esophageal Candidiasis. The clinician selects [___] because its elimination depends on non-enzymatic chemical degradation in the blood.
back:
* Anidulafungin
* Undergoes slow, non-enzymatic chemical degradation
* Avoids hepatic P450 metabolism and renal clearance
* Safest echinocandin for multi-organ failure patients

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Describe the mechanism of synergistic action between Amphotericin B and Flucytosine in the treatment of Cryptococcal meningitis.
back:
* Amphotericin B creates membrane pores
* Increases fungal cell permeability to Flucytosine
* Enhances intracellular access for Flucytosine to inhibit DNA/RNA synthesis

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Contrast Isavuconazole and Voriconazole regarding their pharmacological impact on the cardiac QTc interval.
back:
* Voriconazole: Associated with QTc interval prolongation (arrhythmia risk).
* Isavuconazole: Associated with shortening of the QTc interval.
* Isavuconazole is preferred in patients with existing cardiac conduction risks.

category: Discuss mechanisms of action and resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, adverse effects of antifungal drugs
front: Identify the recommended peak serum concentration range for Flucytosine to ensure efficacy while minimizing the risk of bone marrow toxicity.
back:
* 50 to 100 mcg/mL
* Levels >100 mcg/mL are associated with severe marrow suppression
* Toxicity results from conversion to 5-fluorouracil by intestinal flora

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The initial and rate-limiting step in the activation of acyclovir requires the presence of the virus-specified enzyme [___].
back:
• Thymidine kinase
• Converts acyclovir to acyclovir monophosphate
• Selective for HSV and VZV-infected cells
• Host cell enzymes complete the triphosphorylation.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A 40-year-old male with AIDS and a CD4 count of 40 presents with vision loss and is diagnosed with CMV retinitis. If treatment is initiated with the drug of choice, what dose-limiting toxicity is most common?
back:
• Myelosuppression (Neutropenia)
• Associated with Ganciclovir/Valganciclovir
• Reversible upon discontinuation
• Often compounded by other bone-marrow-suppressing drugs.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of phosphorylation in the activation and function of Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs).
back:
• Requires three intracellular phosphorylations
• Activated triphosphate forms compete with native nucleotides
• Incorporation leads to premature DNA chain termination
• Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase enzyme.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetic and safety profiles of Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with Tenofovir alafenamide (TAF).
back:
• TDF: High plasma levels; associated with proximal renal tubulopathy and bone mineral density loss.
• TAF: Lower plasma levels; higher intracellular loading in lymphoid cells; improved renal and bone safety profile.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain the pharmacokinetic rationale behind using low-dose Ritonavir in combination with other Protease Inhibitors (PIs).
back:
• Potent inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism
• Acts as a "booster" to increase drug exposure (AUC)
• Allows for lower doses or reduced frequency
• Enhances the genetic barrier to resistance.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The anti-influenza agent that acts by competitively and reversibly inhibiting the viral enzyme [___], leading to the clumping of newly released virions, is oseltamivir.
back:
• Neuraminidase
• Effective against both Influenza A and B
• Prevents virion release from infected cells
• Must be initiated within 48 hours of onset.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A patient with HIV is scheduled to begin a regimen containing Abacavir. Which genetic screen must be performed to prevent a potentially fatal multi-organ hypersensitivity reaction?
back:
• HLA-B*5701 allele screening
• Negative test approaches 100% predictive value
• Positive status makes abacavir strictly contraindicated
• Prevents fever, rash, and respiratory failure syndrome.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Describe the molecular difference between Nucleoside and Non-Nucleoside NS5B Polymerase Inhibitors used in Hepatitis C (HCV) therapy.
back:
• Nucleoside (Sofosbuvir): Targets catalytic site; activated by phosphorylation; pan-genotypic activity.
• Non-Nucleoside (Dasabuvir): Allosteric inhibitor; binds outside the active site; typically restricted to Genotype 1.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the requirement for viral enzymes in the mechanisms of action for Ganciclovir versus Foscarnet.
back:
• Ganciclovir: Requires UL97 kinase for initial phosphorylation; ineffective if UL97 is mutated.
• Foscarnet: Pyrophosphate analog; directly inhibits DNA polymerase without phosphorylation; active against kinase-deficient strains.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Identify the mandatory pre-treatment laboratory requirement before initiating Maraviroc therapy in HIV-1 infected patients.
back:
• Co-receptor tropism assay
• Determines if virus uses CCR5, CXCR4, or both
• Maraviroc is only effective against CCR5-tropic strains
• Ineffective against dual or mixed tropic viruses.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: The antiretroviral drug Maraviroc inhibits the viral attachment step by selectively binding to the [___] co-receptor on the host cell surface.
back:
• CCR5 receptor
• Prevents conformational changes in gp120 required for viral entry
• Only effective against CCR5-tropic strains.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 70-year-old patient with a history of Parkinson's disease is treated for Influenza A. The prescribed agent historically used for this condition acts by blocking the [___] step of viral replication.
back:
• Uncoating
• Drug: Amantadine or Rimantadine
• Mechanism: Blocks the M2 proton ion channel to prevent viral RNA release.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Selective Inhibition of Viral DNA Polymerase
front: Explain the role of viral thymidine kinase in the selectivity of Acyclovir during nucleic acid synthesis inhibition.
back:
• Acts as the initial catalyst for mono-phosphorylation
• Ensures Acyclovir is only activated within virus-infected cells
• Triphosphate form then competitively inhibits DNA polymerase.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the specific replication steps targeted by Raltegravir versus Enfuvirtide in the HIV life cycle.
back:
• Raltegravir: Inhibits Integration (strand transfer into host DNA)
• Enfuvirtide: Inhibits Fusion (gp41-mediated entry into host cell).

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the viral enzyme targeted by Oseltamivir to prevent the dissemination of infection within the respiratory tract.
back:
• Neuraminidase
• Action: Cleaves sialic acid receptors to allow release of progeny virions
• Result: Virions remain clumped to the host cell membrane.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: The nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) Zidovudine (AZT) functions by causing premature [___] during the reverse transcription phase.
back:
• Chain termination
• Competes with natural nucleotides for incorporation into the viral DNA provirus
• Lacks a 3'-hydroxyl group required for further elongation.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: An HIV patient develops painful subcutaneous nodules at injection sites. Identify the viral replication step targeted by the drug most likely causing this reaction.
back:
• Fusion/Entry
• Drug: Enfuvirtide
• Mechanism: Binds gp41 to prevent conformational changes needed for membrane fusion.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe how HIV Protease Inhibitors (PIs) interfere with the production of infectious viral particles.
back:
• Inhibit post-translational cleavage of Gag-Pol polyproteins
• Prevents processing of viral proteins into functional conformations
• Result: Production of immature, noninfectious virions.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the targets of Sofosbuvir and Daclatasvir in the management of Chronic Hepatitis C (HCV).
back:
• Sofosbuvir: NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (chain termination)
• Daclatasvir: NS5A protein (viral replication and assembly complex).

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Which step of the viral life cycle is specifically inhibited by non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) like Efavirenz?
back:
• Reverse transcription (RNA to DNA)
• Mechanism: Allosteric (non-competitive) inhibition of DNA polymerase activity
• Does not require intracellular phosphorylation.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Integrase as a Target for Viral Integration
front: The HIV enzyme responsible for the provirus formation step by inserting viral DNA into the host genome, targeted by drugs like Raltegravir, is [___].
back:
• Integrase
• Facilitates the integration step of the viral life cycle
• Prevents the final step of provirus formation
• Inhibited by Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs)

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 28-year-old male with HIV is started on Maraviroc. Identify the specific host cell surface protein this agent binds to in order to prevent viral entry.
back:
• CCR5 co-receptor
• Blocks the binding step of viral attachment
• Only effective against CCR5-tropic HIV strains
• Prevents conformational changes in gp120/gp41

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of Neuraminidase upon the maturation of progeny Influenza A virions.
back:
• Facilitates viral release from infected cells
• Cleaves sialic acid receptors to prevent clumping
• Inhibited by Oseltamivir and Zanamivir
• Limits the spread of infection to new respiratory cells

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Fusion Inhibition vs Membrane Fusion Blockade
front: Contrast the inhibitory mechanisms of Enfuvirtide and Docosanol in preventing viral infection.
back:
• Enfuvirtide: Binds gp41 to block HIV-1 fusion with host membranes
• Docosanol: Inhibits fusion between host plasma membrane and HSV envelope
• Both prevent the entry step but target different viral glycoproteins

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the early replication step blocked by Amantadine during the Influenza A life cycle.
back:
• Viral Uncoating
• Blocks the M2 proton ion channel
• Prevents acid-mediated release of viral RNA into the host cytoplasm
• High levels of resistance have rendered it mostly obsolete

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Reverse Transcriptase as a Replication Target
front: In the HIV replication cycle, NRTIs and NNRTIs both competitively or allosterically target the specific step of [___].
back:
• Reverse Transcription
• Converts single-stranded RNA into double-stranded DNA
• NRTIs cause chain termination
• NNRTIs cause non-competitive allosteric inhibition

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient on a HAART regimen develops lipodystrophy and hyperglycemia. Identify the specific replication step targeted by the drug class causing these effects.
back:
• Viral Maturation (Protein Processing)
• Targeted by Protease Inhibitors (PIs)
• Prevents cleavage of Gag-Pol polyproteins into functional structural proteins
• Results in production of non-infectious, immature virions

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe the biochemical process that occurs in the absence of Protease Inhibitors to enable viral infectivity.
back:
• Post-translational cleavage of precursor polyproteins
• Protease enzyme cuts long Gag-Pol chains into active subunits
• Essential for core structure formation
• Maturation occurs during or after budding from the host cell

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the target sites of Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) versus Non-nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs).
back:
• NRTIs: Target the active catalytic site of Reverse Transcriptase
• NNRTIs: Target a distinct allosteric hydrophobic pocket
• NRTIs require intracellular phosphorylation; NNRTIs do not

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Monoclonal Antibody Blockade of RSV Entry
front: Identify the replication target of Palivizumab used for Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) prophylaxis in infants.
back:
• Viral Entry (Fusion protein block)
• Monoclonal antibody against the A-antigen site on the F-protein
• Prevents the virus from merging with host cell membranes
• Used primarily for prophylaxis in high-risk premature infants

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Inhibition of Viral Release via Neuraminidase
front: The step in the influenza virus life cycle where progeny virions are released from the host cell is specifically inhibited by the class of drugs known as [___].
back:
* **Neuraminidase Inhibitors** (e.g., Oseltamivir, Zanamivir).
* Mechanism: They prevent the cleavage of sialic acid, causing virions to clump to the cell membrane.
* Clinical Effect: Halts the spread of infection within the respiratory tract.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient with Influenza A is treated with a drug that prevents the acidification of the endosome, thereby blocking viral uncoating. This mechanism is characteristic of [___].
back:
* **Adamantanes** (Amantadine and Rimantadine).
* Target: They block the M2 proton ion channel of the virus particle.
* Spectrum: Only active against Influenza A, though resistance is now nearly universal.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of HIV integrase and how Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) block the viral replication cycle.
back:
* **HIV Integrase**: Mediates the insertion of reverse-transcribed viral DNA into host chromosomes.
* **INSTI Action**: Agents like Raltegravir bind the enzyme-DNA complex.
* **Outcome**: Inhibits 'strand transfer,' preventing provirus integration into host DNA.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the mechanism of action of Nucleoside NS5B inhibitors (e.g., Sofosbuvir) with Non-nucleoside NS5B inhibitors (e.g., Dasabuvir) in Hepatitis C replication.
back:
* **Nucleoside (Sofosbuvir)**: Acts as a chain terminator by competing with natural nucleotides for the catalytic site.
* **Non-nucleoside (Dasabuvir)**: Acts as an allosteric inhibitor, binding to non-catalytic sites to cause inhibitory conformational changes.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the viral replication step targeted by Maraviroc and the specific host cell requirement for its efficacy.
back:
* **Step**: Viral attachment and entry.
* **Target**: Host CCR5 co-receptor.
* **Requirement**: Only effective against 'R5-tropic' HIV strains; ineffective against CXCR4 or mixed-tropic viruses.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Protease inhibitors like Atazanavir and Darunavir prevent the maturation of HIV by blocking the cleavage of the [___] polyprotein.
back:
* **Gag-Pol polyprotein**.
* Action: Prevents processing of viral proteins into functional conformations.
* Result: Production of immature, noninfectious viral particles that cannot infect new cells.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: An HIV-infected patient fails initial therapy and is started on a subcutaneous agent that binds the gp41 subunit of the viral envelope. Name the drug and the replication step inhibited.
back:
* **Drug**: Enfuvirtide.
* **Step**: Viral fusion and entry.
* **Mechanism**: Binds gp41 to prevent the conformational changes required for fusion between viral and host cell membranes.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe the selective activation mechanism of Acyclovir that targets viral DNA synthesis in HSV-infected cells.
back:
* **Viral Activation**: First phosphorylation is catalyzed by virus-specified **thymidine kinase**.
* **Host Activation**: Host kinases complete conversion to triphosphate.
* **Mechanism**: Triphosphate competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase and causes chain termination.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) and Non-nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs) regarding their binding and activation requirements.
back:
* **NRTIs**: Pro-drugs requiring intracellular phosphorylation; bind to the enzyme's active site.
* **NNRTIs**: Not pro-drugs; bind allosterically to a distinct hydrophobic pocket, inducing a conformational change in the enzyme.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Name the over-the-counter topical agent that inhibits HSV replication by preventing fusion between the host cell plasma membrane and the viral envelope.
back:
* **Docosanol** (Abreva).
* Mechanism: Blocks fusion between the host cell and the HSV envelope.
* Clinical: Shortens healing time in orolabial herpes if applied during the prodromal phase.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The class of antiretroviral drugs requiring three intracellular phosphorylation steps to competitively inhibit HIV reverse transcriptase and cause premature DNA chain termination is [___].
back: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs). Examples include Abacavir, Emtricitabine, and Tenofovir.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A 68-year-old patient presents with sudden onset high fever, myalgia, and dry cough during an influenza outbreak. To effectively halt the spread of the infection by preventing the release of progeny virions, the clinician should prescribe [___].
back: Neuraminidase inhibitors (e.g., Oseltamivir, Zanamivir). These agents cause clumping of newly released influenza A and B virions to the host cell membrane.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of the viral protein kinase phosphotransferase UL97 in the activation of Ganciclovir for CMV treatment.
back: UL97 catalyzes the initial phosphorylation of Ganciclovir into its monophosphate form. Host cell kinases then complete the conversion to the active triphosphate metabolite, which inhibits viral DNA polymerase.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
coreConcept: HCV Protease Inhibitors and Resistance Testing
front: A patient with chronic Hepatitis C, genotype 1a, undergoes screening for the Q80K polymorphism before initiating a regimen containing [___].
back: Simeprevir. This NS3/4A protease inhibitor shows significantly reduced efficacy (SVR rates) in genotype 1a patients harboring the baseline Q80K mutation.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Identify the specific viral enzyme targeted by Raltegravir and Dolutegravir to prevent the insertion of reverse-transcribed HIV DNA into host chromosomes.
back: Integrase. These drugs are classified as Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs).

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: In the management of HIV, the drug [___] requires pre-treatment screening for the HLA-B*5701 allele to mitigate the risk of a potentially fatal systemic hypersensitivity reaction.
back: Abacavir. Patients testing positive for this allele are at significantly higher risk for multi-organ hypersensitivity symptoms (fever, rash, GI distress).

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: A pregnant woman with chronic HBV infection is initiated on therapy in her last month of gestation to reduce vertical transmission. The nucleoside analog favored for its clinical efficacy and documented ability to prevent fetal infection is [___].
back: Lamivudine. It inhibits HBV DNA polymerase and has been used effectively in late pregnancy to lower the viral load before delivery.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the genetic barrier to resistance between first-generation NNRTIs (e.g., Nevirapine) and second-generation agents (e.g., Etravirine).
back: First-generation NNRTIs have a low genetic barrier; a single mutation (K103N) often causes high-level resistance. Etravirine is a diarylpyrimidine with a higher barrier, effective against many first-generation resistant strains.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the pharmacological roles of Ritonavir and Cobicistat in combination antiretroviral therapy.
back: Both act as 'boosters' by inhibiting CYP3A4 to increase levels of primary drugs. Ritonavir is a Protease Inhibitor with independent antiviral activity; Cobicistat is a pharmacokinetic enhancer with no antiviral activity.

category: Classify antiviral drugs
front: The anti-influenza agent that inhibits viral uncoating by blocking the M2 proton ion channel of the virus particle is [___].
back: Amantadine (or Rimantadine). These adamantanes are only active against Influenza A, though high-level resistance currently limits their clinical utility.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: The topical antiviral agent [___] inhibits viral replication by blocking the fusion between the host cell plasma membrane and the HSV envelope, preventing viral entry.
back:
• Docosanol (10% cream)
• Prevents viral penetration into the host cell
• Shortens healing time in recurrent orolabial herpes

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient with influenza A is treated with Amantadine. This drug interferes with viral replication primarily by targeting which specific stage of the life cycle?
back:
• Viral Uncoating
• Mechanism: Blocks the M2 proton ion channel
• Prevents the release of viral RNA into the host cell cytoplasm

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain how Neuraminidase inhibitors (e.g., Oseltamivir) interfere with the spread of the influenza virus within the respiratory tract.
back:
• Inhibits viral neuraminidase enzyme
• Blocks the release of progeny virions from infected cells
• Causes newly released viruses to clump to the host membrane

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the replication cycle targets of Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) with those of Protease Inhibitors (PIs) in HIV management.
back:
• INSTIs: Block integration of proviral DNA into host chromosomes
• PIs: Inhibit proteolytic cleavage of Gag-Pol polyproteins
• Prevents maturation of immature budding particles into infectious virions

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the primary mechanism by which Enfuvirtide prevents HIV from infecting host CD4+ cells.
back:
• Fusion Inhibition
• Binds to the gp41 subunit of the viral envelope glycoprotein
• Blocks the conformational changes required for membrane fusion

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: In the treatment of chronic Hepatitis B, nucleoside analogs like Entecavir primarily target the [___] stage of the viral replication cycle.
back:
• Nucleic acid synthesis (DNA Polymerase)
• Competitively inhibits base priming and reverse transcription
• Causes chain termination of the viral DNA strand

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 32-year-old HIV-positive patient is prescribed Maraviroc. This medication prevents viral replication by targeting which specific host cell structure?
back:
• CCR5 Co-receptor
• Blocks the binding of viral gp120 to the host chemokine receptor
• Prevents viral attachment and entry into the cell

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe the multiple sites of action of Interferon-alfa in treating chronic viral hepatitis infections.
back:
• Inhibits viral penetration, transcription, and translation
• Blocks protein processing and viral release
• Augments host MHC expression and T-cell survival

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the binding interactions of NRTIs versus NNRTIs with the HIV reverse transcriptase enzyme.
back:
• NRTIs: Competitively inhibit the active site; cause chain termination
• NNRTIs: Bind allosterically to cause non-competitive inhibition
• NRTIs require intracellular phosphorylation; NNRTIs do not

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the stage of the viral life cycle targeted by Acyclovir and its prodrug Valacyclovir.
back:
• Nucleic acid synthesis (DNA Polymerase)
• Requires viral thymidine kinase for initial phosphorylation
• Competes with dGTP to cause DNA chain termination

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: In the management of HIV-1 infection, the chemokine receptor [___] is the specific host protein targeted by Maraviroc to block viral entry.
back:
• CCR5 receptor
• Maraviroc blocks the interaction between the viral gp120 and host CCR5
• It is ineffective against CXCR4-tropic strains

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 68-year-old female presents with acute onset of fever, myalgia, and dry cough during an influenza A outbreak. She is prescribed Oseltamivir. Identify the specific viral step inhibited by this drug.
back:
• Viral release from host cells
• Inhibits viral neuraminidase
• Prevents the clumping and spread of progeny virions

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the biochemical requirement for Acyclovir's selective toxicity against Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) in infected cells.
back:
• Requires initial phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase
• Host kinases then form the active triphosphate
• Selectively accumulates only in virus-infected cells

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the binding mechanisms of Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) versus Non-Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs) during HIV replication.
back:
• NRTIs: Compete for the catalytic site and cause DNA chain termination
• NNRTIs: Bind to an allosteric site to cause non-competitive inhibition
• NRTIs require intracellular phosphorylation; NNRTIs do not

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the specific viral enzyme targeted by Raltegravir to prevent the insertion of the HIV provirus into the host chromosome.
back:
• HIV Integrase
• Specifically inhibits the strand transfer step
• Prevents formation of a stable provirus within host DNA

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: The fusion inhibitor [___] acts by binding to the gp41 subunit of the HIV viral envelope glycoprotein, preventing conformational changes necessary for cell entry.
back:
• Enfuvirtide
• Administered subcutaneously
• Blocks the fusion of viral and host cell membranes

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient with influenza A is treated with Amantadine. This agent prevents viral replication by targeting the [___] proton ion channel.
back:
• M2 proton channel
• Inhibits the uncoating of the viral RNA
• Only active against Influenza A, not Influenza B

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe how HIV Protease Inhibitors (e.g., Atazanavir) result in the production of noninfectious viral particles.
back:
• Prevent cleavage of the Gag-Pol polyprotein
• Blocks maturation of viral proteins into functional conformations
• Progeny virions remain immature and unable to infect new cells

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the molecular targets of Sofosbuvir and Simeprevir in the treatment of Chronic Hepatitis C (HCV).
back:
• Sofosbuvir: NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase inhibitor
• Simeprevir: NS3/4A serine protease inhibitor
• Both are direct-acting antivirals (DAAs)

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: What is the primary mechanism by which topical Docosanol interferes with the Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) life cycle?
back:
• Inhibits fusion between the host cell plasma membrane and the HSV envelope
• Prevents viral entry into the host cell
• Must be applied during the prodromal phase for efficacy

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Antiviral agents like enfuvirtide and maraviroc act specifically at the viral replication step of [___].
back:
• Viral attachment and entry
• Enfuvirtide blocks gp41-mediated fusion
• Maraviroc is a CCR5 co-receptor antagonist

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient with HIV starts a regimen including Raltegravir. This drug prevents the insertion of reverse-transcribed viral DNA into the host genome by targeting the step of [___].
back:
• Integration
• It inhibits the viral enzyme integrase
• Prevents formation of the provirus within the host nucleus

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the role of Non-nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs) in arresting viral nucleic acid synthesis.
back:
• Bind to a specific allosteric site on reverse transcriptase
• Induce conformational changes that inhibit enzyme activity
• Unlike NRTIs, they do not require intracellular phosphorylation

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the metabolic activation requirements of Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) versus Non-nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs).
back:
• NRTIs: Require three intracellular phosphorylations to the active triphosphate form
• NNRTIs: Direct inhibitors; require no intracellular activation or phosphorylation

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the replication stage disrupted by HIV protease inhibitors and the resulting effect on progeny virions.
back:
• Stage: Maturation (Post-translational cleavage)
• Effect: Prevents cleavage of Gag-Pol polyproteins
• Result: Production of immature, non-infectious viral particles

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Amantadine and rimantadine interfere with the [___] stage of the Influenza A virus life cycle by blocking the M2 proton channel.
back:
• Uncoating
• Blockade prevents the acidification needed to release viral RNA into the host cytoplasm

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient presenting with acute influenza is prescribed Oseltamivir. Describe the specific viral replication step inhibited by this drug to limit the spread of infection.
back:
• Viral release (Budding)
• Competitively inhibits neuraminidase
• Prevents the cleavage of sialic acid, causing newly formed virions to clump to the cell membrane

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe the mechanism by which Ledipasvir disrupts the Hepatitis C virus (HCV) replication cycle.
back:
• Inhibits the NS5A protein
• Disrupts both viral RNA replication and the assembly/packaging of new HCV virions

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the primary enzymatic targets of Sofosbuvir and Simeprevir in the treatment of Hepatitis C.
back:
• Sofosbuvir: NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (inhibits nucleic acid synthesis)
• Simeprevir: NS3/4A serine protease (inhibits polyprotein processing/maturation)

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: State the primary replication steps inhibited by Interferon-alfa during the treatment of Chronic Hepatitis B.
back:
• Translation and protein synthesis
• Also affects viral penetration, transcription, and release
• Acts via induction of host cell ribonuclease that degrades viral mRNA

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: The antiviral agent [___] prevents herpes simplex virus (HSV) entry into host cells by inhibiting the fusion between the host cell plasma membrane and the HSV envelope.
back:
• Docosanol
• Topical 10% cream used for orolabial herpes
• Inhibits fusion to prevent viral entry and subsequent replication
• Must be applied during prodromal phase for maximum efficacy

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 28-year-old HIV-positive patient is started on a regimen including Raltegravir. This medication specifically targets which step of the HIV replication cycle?
back:
• Integration
• It is an Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitor (INSTI)
• Blocks the viral enzyme integrase from inserting reverse-transcribed HIV DNA into the host cell chromosome

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the mechanism by which Neuraminidase Inhibitors like Oseltamivir disrupt the influenza virus life cycle.
back:
• They competitively inhibit viral neuraminidase
• This prevents the cleavage of sialic acid residues
• Results in progeny virions clumping to the host cell membrane and each other
• Halts the spread of infection within the respiratory tract

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the molecular targets of Enfuvirtide and Maraviroc in the prevention of HIV cell entry.
back:
• Enfuvirtide: Binds to the gp41 subunit of the viral envelope to block membrane fusion
• Maraviroc: Binds to the host CCR5 co-receptor to block viral attachment (gp120 binding)

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the specific viral process inhibited by Protease Inhibitors (PIs) such as Atazanavir or Darunavir.
back:
• Post-translational processing (Maturation)
• Prevents HIV protease from cleaving the Gag-Pol polyprotein
• Results in the production of immature, noninfectious viral particles

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: The adamantanes (Amantadine and Rimantadine) block the influenza virus [___] step by interfering with the M2 proton ion channel.
back:
• Uncoating
• Specifically inhibits the uncoating of viral RNA within infected host cells
• Only active against Influenza A; now rarely used due to high resistance

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient with chronic Hepatitis B is treated with Entecavir. Describe the specific replication steps targeted by this agent.
back:
• Nucleic acid synthesis (DNA Polymerase inhibition)
• Inhibits three functions: Base priming, reverse transcription of the negative strand, and synthesis of the positive HBV DNA strand

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe the intracellular activation requirement of Acyclovir that accounts for its selective toxicity against HSV-infected cells.
back:
• Requires initial phosphorylation by virus-specified thymidine kinase
• Host cell enzymes perform subsequent phosphorylations to the active triphosphate form
• Triphosphate competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase and causes chain termination

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the binding sites of Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) versus Non-nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs).
back:
• NRTIs: Bind at the active catalytic site (compete with natural nucleotides)
• NNRTIs: Bind at a distinct allosteric site near the active site, inducing a conformational change

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the target protein and virus associated with the monoclonal antibody Palivizumab.
back:
• Target: Fusion (F) surface protein
• Virus: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)
• Prevents viral attachment and entry; used for prophylaxis in high-risk infants

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: In the replication cycle of the influenza virus, the step of viral release from the host cell is specifically inhibited by [___] inhibitors.
back:
• Neuraminidase inhibitors
• Prevents clumping of progeny virions
• Examples: Oseltamivir, Zanamivir

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 32-year-old HIV-positive patient is started on a regimen including Raltegravir. This drug class exerts its antiviral effect by preventing the [___] of reverse-transcribed viral DNA into the host cell genome.
back:
• Integration
• Inhibits the viral enzyme integrase
• Essential for the formation of a provirus

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the biological stage of viral replication inhibited by HIV Protease Inhibitors (PIs) such as Atazanavir or Darunavir.
back:
• Packaging and Assembly (Maturation)
• Prevents proteolytic cleavage of polyproteins
• Results in immature, noninfectious virions

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the specific host or viral structures targeted by the entry inhibitors Maraviroc and Enfuvirtide in HIV management.
back:
• Maraviroc: Binds host CCR5 co-receptors (Attachment).
• Enfuvirtide: Binds viral gp41 subunit (Fusion).
• Both block entry into the host cytoplasm.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: M2 Channel Blockade and Viral Uncoating
front: Identify the specific early step in the viral life cycle targeted by the adamantane class of anti-influenza agents (Amantadine and Rimantadine).
back:
• Viral Uncoating
• Blocks the M2 proton ion channel
• Prevents release of viral RNA into the cytoplasm

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) act by competitive inhibition of reverse transcriptase, which directly leads to premature [___] of the viral DNA chain.
back:
• Chain termination
• Incorporation of an analog instead of a nucleotide
• Example: Zidovudine, Tenofovir

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
coreConcept: Selective Phosphorylation in Viral DNA Synthesis
front: A patient with herpes encephalitis is treated with IV Acyclovir. This drug requires initial phosphorylation by a virus-specified [___] before it can target the nucleic acid synthesis stage.
back:
• Thymidine kinase
• Ensures selective activation only in infected cells
• Inhibits viral DNA polymerase

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Describe the multiple steps of the viral life cycle modulated by Interferon-alfa in the treatment of chronic Hepatitis B or C.
back:
• Inhibits viral penetration, translation, and transcription
• Blocks protein processing and viral release
• Enhances host expression of MHC antigens

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the binding interactions of NRTIs versus NNRTIs on the HIV-1 reverse transcriptase enzyme.
back:
• NRTIs: Competitive inhibition at the catalytic site.
• NNRTIs: Allosteric (non-competitive) inhibition at a distinct site.
• Both target nucleic acid synthesis.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the specific stage of the herpes simplex virus (HSV) life cycle inhibited by the topical agent Docosanol.
back:
• Viral entry (Fusion)
• Inhibits fusion between host cell and HSV envelope
• Blocks penetration into the target cell

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: In the influenza replication cycle, the specific step involving the release of mature progeny virions from the host cell membrane is targeted by the drug class known as [___].
back:
Neuraminidase Inhibitors (e.g., Oseltamivir, Zanamivir).
• Block viral neuraminidase enzyme.
• Prevent cleavage of sialic acid residues.
• Induce clumping of virions at the host cell surface.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A patient is prescribed Amantadine to treat Influenza A. This agent acts early in the viral life cycle by blocking the M2 proton ion channel, which primarily prevents the process of [___].
back:
Viral Uncoating.
• Prevents acidification of the virus interior.
• Blocks release of the viral RNP (ribonucleoprotein) into the host cytoplasm.
• Only effective against Influenza A strains.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs), such as Raltegravir, disrupt the HIV replication cycle.
back:
Inhibition of Genomic Integration.
• Binds to the viral integrase enzyme.
• Prevents insertion of reverse-transcribed viral DNA into host chromosomes.
• Blocks the formation of a permanent genetic reservoir.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the molecular mechanisms of the entry inhibitors Enfuvirtide and Maraviroc in the prevention of HIV infection of CD4+ T-cells.
back:
Fusion vs. Co-receptor Blockade.
• Enfuvirtide: Binds gp41 to prevent viral-host membrane fusion.
• Maraviroc: Binds host CCR5 receptor to prevent gp120 attachment.
• Target: Enfuvirtide (Viral), Maraviroc (Host).

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Identify the late-stage maturation process in the HIV life cycle that is inhibited by the administration of Atazanavir or Darunavir.
back:
Post-translational Proteolytic Cleavage.
• Inhibits HIV aspartyl protease.
• Prevents cleavage of Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors.
• Results in immature, non-infectious virion production.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Antiviral agents categorized as NRTIs (e.g., Zidovudine) and NNRTIs (e.g., Efavirenz) both target the replication stage known as [___].
back:
Reverse Transcription.
• NRTIs: Competitively inhibit RT and cause DNA chain termination.
• NNRTIs: Allosterically inhibit the RT enzyme.
• Converts viral RNA into double-stranded DNA.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: A 22-year-old female with genital herpes is treated with Acyclovir. This drug requires initial activation by viral thymidine kinase to eventually inhibit the viral enzyme [___].
back:
DNA Polymerase.
• Acts as a competitive substrate for dGTP.
• Incorporation leads to irreversible DNA chain termination.
• Selective toxicity: Requires viral-specific kinase for activation.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Discuss how NS5A inhibitors, such as Ledipasvir, provide clinical benefit in the management of Chronic Hepatitis C (HCV).
back:
Viral Replication and Assembly.
• Targets the NS5A non-structural protein.
• Disrupts the HCV replication complex and virion assembly.
• Essential component of curative interferon-free regimens.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: Contrast the specific sites of action for the Hepatitis C (HCV) drugs Sofosbuvir and Dasabuvir within the NS5B polymerase complex.
back:
Catalytic vs. Allosteric Inhibition.
• Sofosbuvir: Nucleotide analog targeting the catalytic active site.
• Dasabuvir: Non-nucleoside inhibitor targeting allosteric palm sites.
• Both result in premature RNA chain termination.

category: Discuss the main steps of viral replication that are targets for antiviral drugs
front: State the broad-spectrum targets of Interferon-alfa that contribute to its efficacy against HBV and HCV.
back:
Transcription, Translation, and Release.
• Induces 2',5'-oligoadenylate synthetase (degrades viral mRNA).
• Activates protein kinase R (inhibits translation initiation).
• Increases host MHC expression for immune detection.

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The initial phosphorylation of acyclovir to its monophosphate form is selectively catalyzed by the virus-specified enzyme [___].
back:
• Viral thymidine kinase
• This ensures the drug is only activated in infected cells
• Host cell enzymes complete the conversion to the active triphosphate form

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 35-year-old HIV patient being treated for CMV retinitis presents with a significantly decreased absolute neutrophil count. Identify the most likely drug responsible and its primary toxicity.
back:
• Ganciclovir (or Valganciclovir)
• Myelosuppression (Neutropenia and Thrombocytopenia)
• Toxicity is usually reversible upon drug discontinuation

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the role of Foscarnet in inhibiting viral DNA polymerase in terms of its requirement for intracellular activation.
back:
• Acts directly without requiring phosphorylation
• Blocks the pyrophosphate binding site of DNA polymerase
• Inhibits cleavage of pyrophosphate from deoxynucleotide triphosphates

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast Ganciclovir and Cidofovir regarding their efficacy against thymidine kinase-deficient herpesvirus strains.
back:
• Ganciclovir: Ineffective; requires viral kinase (UL97/Thymidine kinase) for activation
• Cidofovir: Effective; phosphorylation is independent of viral enzymes (uses host kinases)

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Identify the systemic agents used as the treatment of choice for acyclovir-resistant HSV or VZV infections.
back:
• Foscarnet
• Cidofovir
• These do not rely on viral thymidine kinase for activation

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: [___] is the L-valyl ester prodrug of acyclovir that provides three to five times higher oral bioavailability than the parent compound.
back:
• Valacyclovir
• Undergoes rapid first-pass enzymatic hydrolysis in the liver and intestine
• Achieves serum levels approximating intravenous acyclovir

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A neonate receiving high-dose intravenous acyclovir for encephalitis develops acute renal failure. This is most likely caused by [___].
back:
• Crystalline nephropathy (Obstructive nephropathy)
• Caused by drug precipitation in renal tubules
• Prevented by adequate hydration and slow infusion rates

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the difference in resistance patterns between CMV mutations in the UL97 gene versus the UL54 gene.
back:
• UL97 mutation: Affects ganciclovir activation; foscarnet and cidofovir remain active
• UL54 mutation: Affects DNA polymerase; confers broad resistance to ganciclovir, cidofovir, and occasionally foscarnet

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast Acyclovir and Trifluridine regarding their mechanism of toxicity and suitability for systemic use.
back:
• Acyclovir: Selective for viral kinase; safe systemically
• Trifluridine: Phosphorylated by host enzymes; incorporates into host DNA; restricted to topical use (herpes keratitis)

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Which over-the-counter topical agent inhibits the fusion between the host cell plasma membrane and the HSV envelope?
back:
• Docosanol (10% cream)
• Prevents viral entry into cells
• Used for recurrent orolabial herpes labialis

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Acyclovir must be selectively activated via initial monophosphorylation by the virus-encoded enzyme [___] to exert its effect.
back:
• Viral thymidine kinase (TK)
• Selectivity ensures accumulation only in infected cells
• Host kinases complete the di- and tri-phosphorylation steps

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: A 32-year-old with shingles is prescribed an L-valyl ester of acyclovir to improve oral bioavailability and allow less frequent dosing. This drug is [___].
back:
• Valacyclovir
• Prodrug rapidly converted to acyclovir by first-pass metabolism
• Achieves 3–5 times higher serum levels than oral acyclovir

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Explain the biochemical advantage of utilizing Foscarnet in the management of acyclovir-resistant Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV).
back:
• It is a pyrophosphate analog
• Directly inhibits viral DNA polymerase
• Does not require activation by viral thymidine kinase (TK)

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast Ganciclovir and Acyclovir regarding the specific viral enzymes required for their initial intracellular phosphorylation.
back:
• Acyclovir: Thymidine kinase (HSV/VZV)
• Ganciclovir: UL97 phosphotransferase (CMV)
• Both drugs competitively inhibit viral DNA polymerase

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: What is the most frequent molecular basis for clinical resistance to Acyclovir in HSV isolates?
back:
• Deficiency or mutation in viral thymidine kinase (TK)
• Less commonly due to mutations in DNA polymerase
• Confers cross-resistance to Valacyclovir and Famciclovir

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The primary dose-limiting toxicity associated with the systemic administration of the anti-CMV drug Ganciclovir is [___].
back:
• Myelosuppression (Leukopenia and Thrombocytopenia)
• Usually reversible upon discontinuation
• Risk is additive with other myelosuppressive drugs like Zidovudine

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: An AIDS patient treated for CMV retinitis develops symptomatic hypocalcemia and tremors. Which anti-CMV agent is most likely responsible?
back:
• Foscarnet
• Mechanism: Chelation of divalent cations
• Also causes nephrotoxicity and magnesium/potassium wasting

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Describe the mechanism by which Cidofovir maintains activity against thymidine kinase-deficient strains of CMV.
back:
• It is a nucleotide (phosphonate) analog
• Phosphorylation is independent of viral enzymes
• Utilizes host cell kinases to achieve its active form

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Contrast Acyclovir and Valganciclovir regarding their primary clinical utility in Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections.
back:
• Acyclovir: Weak activity; not used for CMV end-organ disease
• Valganciclovir: High oral bioavailability; drug of choice for CMV retinitis and prophylaxis

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: Which over-the-counter topical agent inhibits HSV by blocking viral entry into the host cell via membrane fusion inhibition?
back:
• Docosanol
• 22-carbon aliphatic alcohol
• Prevents viral attachment and subsequent replication

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
front: The selective activation of [___] requires a virus-specified thymidine kinase to catalyze its initial phosphorylation into a monophosphate derivative.
back:
• Acyclovir
• Guanosine analog active against HSV and VZV
• Selectively accumulates only in infected cells
• Further di- and triphosphorylation is completed by host cell enzymes

category: Describe drugs used in treatment of herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and cytomegalovirus virus infection with their pharmacological properties, mechanism of action and adverse effects
