• Sulfonamides: Compete with PABA to inhibit dihydropteroate synthase.
• Trimethoprim: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Result: Sequential blockade of tetrahydrofolate synthesis.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Name the two specific organ systems most commonly affected by the cumulative toxicity of gentamicin.
back:
• Kidney (Nephrotoxicity: renal tubular injury).
• Inner Ear (Ototoxicity: vestibular and auditory damage).
• Risk increases with loop diuretics.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Unlike beta-lactams that bind to transpeptidase enzymes, the glycopeptide Vancomycin inhibits cell wall synthesis by binding directly to the [___] terminus of nascent peptidoglycan.
back:
• D-alanyl-D-alanine (D-Ala-D-Ala).
• This action sterically blocks both transglycosylase (elongation) and transpeptidase (cross-linking) reactions.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A patient being treated with Daptomycin for MRSA bacteremia requires weekly monitoring of [___] levels because the drug's primary dose-related toxicity involves skeletal muscle damage.
back:
• Creatine phosphokinase (CPK).
• Daptomycin can cause myopathy and, in rare cases, rhabdomyolysis.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Explain the role of the transmembrane electrochemical gradient in the entry of Aminoglycosides into the bacterial cytoplasm.
back:
• It provides energy for the active transport of the drug across the inner membrane.
• This is an oxygen-dependent process, explaining why aminoglycosides lack activity against anaerobic bacteria.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Contrast the 'ribosomal protection' mechanisms that confer resistance to Tetracyclines versus Macrolides.
back:
• Tetracyclines: Production of Tet(M) proteins that physically displace the drug from the 30S subunit.
• Macrolides: Methylation of the 23S rRNA binding site on the 50S subunit by methylase enzymes (MLS-B resistance).

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Why must the dosage of Chloramphenicol be strictly limited in neonates to avoid circulatory collapse?
back:
• Newborns lack adequate glucuronic acid conjugation enzymes in the liver.
• Inability to detoxify the drug leads to 'Gray Baby Syndrome' (hypothermia, flaccid paralysis, and shock).

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: The macrolide Erythromycin acts as a 'motilin agonist' in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to the common adverse effect of [___].
back:
• Increased GI motility (diarrhea and abdominal cramping).
• This effect is sometimes used therapeutically to treat gastroparesis.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A patient treated for a pelvic infection with Cefotetan consumes alcohol and develops severe flushing, tachycardia, and nausea. This is caused by the presence of a [___] in the drug's structure.
back:
• Methylthiotetrazole (MTT) side chain.
• This chemical group inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, causing a disulfiram-like reaction.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Explain why Daptomycin is clinically ineffective in treating pneumonia despite having potent in vitro activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae.
back:
• The drug is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant.
• Surfactant binds to the daptomycin molecules, preventing them from inserting into the bacterial cell membrane.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Contrast the inhibitory targets of Linezolid versus Aminoglycosides within the ribosomal initiation process.
back:
• Linezolid: Binds to 23S RNA of the 50S subunit to prevent formation of the 70S initiation complex.
• Aminoglycosides: Bind 30S subunit to block the 30S initiation complex and induce mRNA misreading.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Identify the primary mechanism of action of the Nitroimidazole drug Metronidazole against anaerobic bacteria.
back:
• Intracellular reduction by ferredoxin creates reactive oxygen species and toxic metabolites.
• These metabolites cause DNA strand breakage and loss of helical structure.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Benzimidazoles like albendazole and mebendazole exert their broad-spectrum antihelminthic activity by inhibiting [___] synthesis in parasites.
back:
• Microtubule synthesis.
• Leads to impaired glucose uptake and depletion of glycogen stores.
• Results in parasite immobilization and death.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A newborn infant treated for a suspected infection develops vomiting, flaccidity, hypothermia, and a cyanotic "ash-gray" skin color. Identify the antibiotic and the biochemical reason for this toxicity.
back:
• Drug: Chloramphenicol.
• Reaction: Gray baby syndrome.
• Mechanism: Accumulation due to immature hepatic glucuronyl transferase and poor renal excretion in neonates.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Explain the mechanism of action of daptomycin against Gram-positive bacteria.
back:
• Binds to the cell membrane via calcium-dependent insertion of its lipid tail.
• Causes rapid membrane depolarization and potassium efflux.
• Results in arrest of DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis leading to death.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A transplant recipient with CMV retinitis fails ganciclovir therapy due to a viral UL97 kinase mutation. Contrast why foscarnet remains effective in this patient whereas valganciclovir does not.
back:
• Valganciclovir: Prodrug of ganciclovir; requires viral UL97 kinase for initial activation (phosphorylation).
• Foscarnet: Inhibits viral DNA polymerase directly; does not require activation by viral or host kinases.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Identify the screening test required before initiating primaquine for the radical cure of P. vivax and the rationale for this precaution.
back:
• Test: G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) level.
• Rationale: Primaquine causes oxidative stress; G6PD-deficient patients cannot protect RBCs, leading to acute hemolytic anemia.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: The urinary antiseptic [___] is bactericidal in the bladder because its reactive intermediates, formed by bacterial reductases, non-specifically damage bacterial proteins and DNA.
back:
• Nitrofurantoin.
• Useful for uncomplicated cystitis due to E. coli.
• Note: Ineffective in renal failure (poor concentration).

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A patient receiving a rapid intravenous infusion of vancomycin for MRSA develops intense erythematous flushing and pruritus of the face and neck. Identify the mechanism of this reaction.
back:
• "Red man" syndrome.
• Direct, non-immunologic release of histamine from mast cells.
• Prevented by slowing infusion rate (to 1–2 hours) or antihistamine pretreatment.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Explain the mechanism by which artemisinin derivatives (e.g., artesunate) exert rapid cidal activity and why they are specifically indicated for severe malaria.
back:
• Mechanism: Iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge produces toxic free radicals that damage parasite proteins.
• Utility: Most rapid-acting blood schizonticides; significantly reduce mortality in severe P. falciparum disease.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Contrast the specific enzymes inhibited by sulfonamides versus trimethoprim in the bacterial folate synthesis pathway.
back:
• Sulfonamides: Inhibit dihydropteroate synthase (PABA analog).
• Trimethoprim: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
• Result: Sequential blockade of tetrahydrofolate synthesis.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Identify the pharmacological interaction that necessitates instructing patients to avoid alcohol while taking metronidazole.
back:
• Disulfiram-like effect.
• Metronidazole inhibits acetaldehyde dehydrogenase.
• Accumulation of acetaldehyde causes nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and flushing.

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: The primary mechanism of action for benzimidazole antihelminthics, such as Albendazole and Mebendazole, involves the inhibition of [___] in susceptible nematodes.
back:
* Inhibition of microtubule synthesis by binding to β-tubulin
* Leads to impaired glucose uptake and depletion of glycogen stores
* Results in parasite death

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A patient treated for Onchocerciasis with Ivermectin develops fever, pruritus, and lymphadenitis 24 hours after the first dose. This systemic response is triggered by [___].
back:
* Host inflammatory response to antigens/proteins from dying microfilariae
* Known as a Mazzotti-like reaction
* Managed with corticosteroids if severe

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Explain the role of calcium ions in the mechanism of action of Praziquantel against Schistosomes.
back:
* Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium
* Induces massive contraction and spastic paralysis of the worm
* Causes tegumental damage, allowing host immune cells to destroy the parasite

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetic effect of concomitant corticosteroid (e.g., dexamethasone) administration on the serum levels of Albendazole versus Praziquantel.
back:
* Albendazole: Serum levels increase (improves efficacy in neurocysticercosis)
* Praziquantel: Serum levels decrease by up to 50%
* Clinical significance: Albendazole is often preferred in brain cyst treatment

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Identify the mechanism by which Pyrantel pamoate induces the expulsion of Ascaris lumbricoides from the host intestinal tract.
back:
* Acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent
* Causes release of acetylcholine and inhibition of cholinesterase
* Results in spastic paralysis; worms are expelled by normal peristalsis

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: The anti-filarial drug Diethylcarbamazine citrate (DEC) is considered the drug of choice for [___] and tropical eosinophilia.
back:
* Loa loa (Loiasis)
* Wuchereria bancrofti
* Brugia malayi

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: A 26-year-old female in her first trimester of pregnancy is diagnosed with hookworm. Benzimidazoles are avoided in this case primarily because they are [___].
back:
* Teratogenic (based on animal studies)
* Embryotoxic
* Generally contraindicated in pregnancy and children < 2 years

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Describe the unique indirect mechanism by which Doxycycline acts as a macrofilaricide in lymphatic filariasis.
back:
* Targets and kills Wolbachia (intracellular bacterial symbionts)
* Wolbachia are essential for filarial fertility and survival
* Results in sterility and death of adult worms

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Contrast the site of action for Niclosamide with that of Ivermectin.
back:
* Niclosamide: Inhibits mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATPase
* Ivermectin: Intensifies GABA-mediated transmission in peripheral nerves

category: Describe their mechanism of action and their adverse effects
front: Identify the toxic metabolite produced by Metrifonate that is responsible for its anti-schistosomal activity.
back:
* Dichlorvos
* Acts as an organophosphate cholinesterase inhibitor
* Paralyzes Schistosoma haematobium adult worms

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: Within the Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor (NRTI) class, Lamivudine and Emtricitabine are specifically classified as [___] analogs.
back:
• Cytidine analogs
• Both select for the M184V/I resistance mutation
• Possess clinical activity against Hepatitis B virus (HBV)

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: A treatment-experienced patient with multi-drug resistant HIV is started on Tipranavir. This agent is unique in its class as it is the only Protease Inhibitor (PI) classified as a [___].
back:
• Non-peptidomimetic Protease Inhibitor
• Retains efficacy against strains resistant to older peptidomimetic PIs
• Requires pharmacokinetic boosting with Ritonavir

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: Explain the classification of Tenofovir Alafenamide (TAF) relative to Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate (TDF) in terms of systemic exposure and toxicity.
back:
• TAF: Phosphonoamidate prodrug; achieves high intracellular active levels with 90% lower plasma exposure
• TDF: Disoproxil prodrug; results in higher systemic plasma levels
• TAF has superior renal and bone safety profiles

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: Contrast the generation classification and genetic barrier to resistance between Nevirapine and Etravirine.
back:
• Nevirapine: First-generation NNRTI; low genetic barrier (single mutation like K103N causes failure)
• Etravirine: Second-generation NNRTI (diarylpyrimidine); high genetic barrier; flexible binding pocket retains efficacy against many first-generation resistant strains

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: Classify the antiretroviral agent Maraviroc according to its host-cell target and the diagnostic test required before initiation.
back:
• Target: Host-cell CCR5 chemokine co-receptor (Entry Inhibitor)
• Required Test: Coreceptor Tropism Assay (e.g., Trofile)
• Note: Not active against CXCR4 or mixed-tropic viruses

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: The antiretroviral agent [___] is currently the only member of the Fusion Inhibitor class and is uniquely administered via subcutaneous injection.
back:
• Enfuvirtide (T-20)
• Binds to the gp41 subunit of the viral envelope
• Blocks the conformational change required for membrane fusion

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: A patient is prescribed the Stribild single-tablet regimen containing Elvitegravir. This drug requires co-formulation with [___], classified as a pharmacokinetic enhancer with no independent antiviral activity.
back:
• Cobicistat
• Potent inhibitor of CYP3A4 to increase Elvitegravir levels
• Inhibits renal tubular secretion of creatinine (causing benign serum creatinine elevation)

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
coreConcept: INSTI Mechanism and Life Cycle Target
front: Explain how the Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitor (INSTI) class carries out its biological function in the HIV life cycle.
back:
• Binds to the viral integrase catalytic site
• Blocks the "strand transfer" step (insertion of viral DNA into host chromosomes)
• Prevents the formation of the HIV provirus

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: Contrast the primary metabolic clearance pathways of Raltegravir with those of most Protease Inhibitors (PIs).
back:
• Raltegravir: Glucuronidation via UGT1A1 (low potential for CYP-mediated drug interactions)
• Protease Inhibitors: Extensive oxidative metabolism via the Cytochrome P450 (CYP3A4) system
• PIs frequently require dosage adjustments for co-administered drugs

category: Classify antiretroviral agents
front: Among the NRTI class, classify Didanosine (ddI) and Abacavir according to the specific nucleoside base they analogize.
back:
• Didanosine (ddI): Adenosine analog
• Abacavir: Guanosine analog
• Both competitively inhibit reverse transcriptase and cause chain termination

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: The intravenous prodrug [___] acts as a nucleotide analog that competes with adenosine triphosphate for incorporation into the viral RNA chain, resulting in delayed chain termination.
back:
• Remdesivir
• Target: RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp)
• Clinical Use: Hospitalized patients with COVID-19 requiring supplemental oxygen
• Efficacy: Shortens time to clinical recovery.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: A 65-year-old obese female with hypertension presents with 2 days of mild cough and a positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR. To prevent progression to severe disease, the most appropriate oral combination therapy is [___].
back:
• Paxlovid (Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir)
• Nirmatrelvir: Inhibits Mpro (3CL protease)
• Ritonavir: Inhibits CYP3A4 to boost nirmatrelvir levels
• Clinical Use: Non-hospitalized, high-risk patients within 5 days of symptom onset.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Explain the mechanism of 'lethal mutagenesis' or 'error catastrophe' induced by Molnupiravir during SARS-CoV-2 replication.
back:
• It is a ribonucleoside analog
• Incorporated into viral RNA by RdRp
• Causes transition mutations (G-to-A or C-to-U)
• Result: Accumulation of deleterious mutations leading to viral extinction.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Contrast the molecular targets and administration routes of Remdesivir and Paxlovid.
back:
• Remdesivir: Inhibits RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp); administered intravenously
• Paxlovid: Inhibits the Main Protease (Mpro/3CLpro); administered orally
• Remdesivir is a nucleotide analog; Nirmatrelvir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Identify the pharmacological rationale for including Ritonavir in the Paxlovid co-formulation despite it lacking intrinsic activity against SARS-CoV-2.
back:
• Pharmacokinetic boosting
• Ritonavir is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor
• Prevents rapid hepatic metabolism of Nirmatrelvir
• Maintains therapeutic concentrations of the active protease inhibitor.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: In the management of severe COVID-19 pneumonia, the systemic corticosteroid [___] is the standard of care to reduce mortality in patients requiring mechanical ventilation or oxygen therapy.
back:
• Dexamethasone
• Mechanism: Suppresses host hyper-inflammatory response (Cytokine Storm)
• Caution: Contraindicated in mild cases not requiring oxygen (may increase viral replication).

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: A hospitalized patient with worsening respiratory failure shows markedly elevated C-reactive protein and Interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels. The adjunctive monoclonal antibody indicated here is [___].
back:
• Tocilizumab
• Target: IL-6 receptor antagonist
• Application: Used in combination with Dexamethasone for severe disease
• Goal: Mitigation of the systemic inflammatory response syndrome.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Describe the intracellular signaling pathway inhibited by Baricitinib in the treatment of hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
back:
• Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitor
• Blocks the JAK-STAT signaling pathway
• Inhibits cytokine-mediated inflammation (e.g., IL-2, IL-6, IFN-gamma)
• Provides anti-inflammatory effects in severe COVID-19 disease.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Contrast the clinical timing and physiological goals of Antiviral therapy versus Immunomodulatory therapy in COVID-19 management.
back:
• Antivirals (Remdesivir/Paxlovid): Used early to stop viral replication
• Immunomodulators (Steroids/Tocilizumab): Used later to stop the hyper-inflammatory phase
• Antivirals target the virus; Immunomodulators target the host immune system.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Identify the specific viral structural component targeted by neutralizing monoclonal antibodies like Sotrovimab to prevent host cell entry.
back:
• Spike (S) Glycoprotein
• Mechanism: Binds to the receptor-binding domain (RBD)
• Effect: Blocks interaction with host ACE2 receptors
• Limitation: Efficacy varies significantly across different viral variants (e.g., Omicron).

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: Beta-lactam antibiotics are structural analogs of the natural [___] substrate, allowing them to covalently bind to the active site of penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs).
back:
• D-alanyl-D-alanine (D-Ala-D-Ala)
• Binding inhibits the transpeptidation reaction.
• Halts peptidoglycan synthesis, resulting in bacterial cell lysis and death.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: A 45-year-old patient with bacterial meningitis is treated with a third-generation cephalosporin. Despite having severe renal failure, which drug in this class requires no dose adjustment?
back:
• Ceftriaxone
• Eliminated primarily via the biliary tract rather than the kidneys.
• Long half-life (8 hours) allows once-daily dosing.
• Achieves therapeutic CNS concentrations in inflamed meninges.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: Explain the primary mechanism by which Gram-negative bacteria develop clinical resistance against the bactericidal activity of Aminoglycosides (e.g., Gentamicin).
back:
• Production of plasmid-mediated transferase enzymes.
• These enzymes inactivate the drug via adenylylation, acetylation, or phosphorylation.
• Prevents the aminoglycoside from binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: Contrast the effect of concomitant corticosteroid administration on the plasma levels of Praziquantel versus Albendazole during therapy for neurocysticercosis.
back:
• Praziquantel: Bioavailability is significantly reduced (up to 50%) by corticosteroids.
• Albendazole: Plasma concentration of its active metabolite is increased by corticosteroids.
• Albendazole is generally preferred for neurocysticercosis due to better subarachnoid penetration.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: Describe the biochemical activation required for Metronidazole to inhibit DNA synthesis in anaerobic pathogens.
back:
• Nonenzymatic reduction of its nitro group by reduced ferredoxin.
• Occurs only in anaerobic organisms or environments.
• Reduced metabolites disrupt bacterial DNA, causing strand breakage and cell death.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: In patients with a G6PD deficiency, the use of Sulfonamides (e.g., Sulfamethoxazole) is likely to trigger a [___] reaction due to oxidative stress on erythrocytes.
back:
• Hemolytic anemia
• Sulfonamides act as oxidizing agents.
• Without G6PD, RBCs cannot maintain reduced glutathione to protect against oxidative damage.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: A patient on long-term Nitrofurantoin for recurrent UTIs presents with dyspnea, non-productive cough, and pulmonary fibrosis on imaging. What is the most likely cause?
back:
• Nitrofurantoin-induced pulmonary toxicity.
• Can manifest as acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis or chronic interstitial fibrosis.
• Requires immediate discontinuation; more common in elderly or renally impaired patients.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: How does Mupirocin selectively inhibit the growth of Staphylococcus aureus without affecting human protein synthesis?
back:
• Inhibits bacterial isoleucyl tRNA synthetase.
• Prevents the incorporation of isoleucine into growing polypeptide chains.
• High selectivity because it does not bind to the mammalian version of the enzyme.

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: Contrast the primary clinical indications for using Mebendazole versus Ivermectin.
back:
• Mebendazole: Drug of choice for intestinal nematodes (Ascaris, hookworm, pinworm).
• Ivermectin: Drug of choice for Strongyloides stercoralis (threadworm) and Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness).

category: Discuss their mechanism of action, resistance, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, and adverse effects
front: Which urinary antiseptic provides bactericidal activity only when the urine pH is maintained below 5.5?
back:
• Methenamine (Mandelate or Hippurate)
• At acidic pH, it releases formaldehyde.
• Formaldehyde is the active antibacterial agent.
• Requires acidic environment to be effective.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: In the pharmacological management of COVID-19, the nucleotide analog that acts as a prodrug to inhibit the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is [___].
back: • Remdesivir. • Inhibits viral replication through premature RNA chain termination. • Primarily administered intravenously for hospitalized patients requiring oxygen.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: A 65-year-old male with COVID-19 develops respiratory distress and requires mechanical ventilation. The corticosteroid indicated to reduce mortality by dampening the hyper-inflammatory response is [___].
back: • Dexamethasone. • Reduces 28-day mortality in patients requiring oxygen or ventilation. • Acts by suppressing the 'cytokine storm' associated with severe disease.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which Nirmatrelvir (a component of Paxlovid) halts the maturation and replication of the coronavirus.
back: • Inhibits the Main Protease (Mpro or 3CLpro). • Prevents cleavage of viral polyproteins into functional units. • Blocks the assembly of new infectious virions.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Contrast the pharmacological mechanisms of Remdesivir and Molnupiravir regarding their effect on viral RNA synthesis.
back: • Remdesivir: Causes premature termination of the viral RNA chain. • Molnupiravir: Induces 'lethal mutagenesis' by creating error-prone nucleoside copies. • Both direct-acting antivirals target replication.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Explain the primary pharmacological purpose of including Ritonavir in the Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir (Paxlovid) drug combination.
back: • Acts as a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor. • 'Boosts' Nirmatrelvir plasma levels by slowing its hepatic metabolism. • Ensures sustained therapeutic concentrations throughout the dosing interval.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Tocilizumab is a monoclonal antibody used in severe COVID-19 cases to specifically antagonize the [___] receptor to prevent tissue damage.
back: • Interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor. • Dampens the systemic inflammatory cascade (cytokine storm). • Indicated for hospitalized patients with rapid respiratory decline.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: A high-risk 55-year-old diabetic patient presents with 3 days of mild COVID-19 symptoms. To be effective, the nirmatrelvir/ritonavir regimen must be initiated within [___] days of symptom onset.
back: • Five (5) days. • Early initiation is critical to block the initial viral replication phase. • Reduces risk of hospitalization by approximately 88%.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: How does Baricitinib provide therapeutic benefit in hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring high-flow oxygen?
back: • Inhibits Janus Kinases (JAK 1 and JAK 2). • Blocks intracellular signaling of pro-inflammatory cytokines. • Reduces mortality and shortens time to recovery.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Contrast the therapeutic target of Monoclonal Antibodies (e.g., Sotrovimab) with that of Direct-Acting Antivirals (e.g., Remdesivir).
back: • Monoclonal Antibodies: Bind to the viral Spike protein to block cell attachment. • Antivirals: Target intracellular replication enzymes like protease or RdRp. • Antibodies prevent entry; antivirals stop production.

category: Enumerate the drugs used to treat coronavirus
front: Identify the broad-spectrum antiviral agent, also used for Hepatitis C, that acts by inhibiting RNA capping and viral polymerase in many RNA viruses including coronaviruses: [___].
back: • Ribavirin. • Inhibits RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and viral mRNA capping. • Explored early in the pandemic but limited by clinical efficacy and anemia.
